title: Update: SA Butlers Academy
oneLiner: We revisit our story of a former student taking a self-proclaimed world class butlers academy to court over allegations of misrepresentation.
summary:
Lin Yang took the South African Butlers Academy to court in August 2020, claiming that SABA was guilty of misrepresentation and demanding a refund of her fees. In August this year, Yang reached a settlement with SABA in the Western Cape High Court. SABA agreed to refund her fees with interest, and has been ordered to pay her legal costs. In return, Yang has withdrawn her case with the NCC and Information Regulator. Both parties have to issue a statement in which SABA admits that it made "not entirely correct" claims on its website and agrees to remove such material from all its platforms. However, Yang says she has had to battle SABA to remove such content, and to pay her legal costs. Meanwhile, a complaint laid with the National Consumer Commission in September 2020 by a handful of students gained traction following our CB story. There are now over 20 students claiming their fees back from SABA under the Consumer Protection Act. However, for more than three years the NCC has failed to act on their complaints.

The South African Butlers Academy claimed to be world class...but dozens of students say differently. We revisit our story to hear the resolution of one student's case against the academy, and ask why the National Consumer Commission doesn't seem to following up on complaints.
caseStudies: Yang Lin Joachim Prinsloo

title: Mia Botha
oneLiner: Three children are murdered every day in South Africa. Many of these cases go unsolved. Communities across the country are being failed by an inept police service and a shortage of detectives.
summary:
Four year old Mia Botha went missing on Sunday, 25 September, last year. She was playing outside in the late afternoon as she often did. The community of Klein Nederberg in Paarl East watches out for all the children in the area. But on that day, nobody was witness to her abduction. Despite an extensive search, the little girl's body was found the following day on the field of a school close to her home. Plastic had been shoved into her mouth and her body had been placed in a bag. Soon after the horrific discovery, two suspects were arrested and appeared in court. But, they were released, as the investigation docket was empty, and court prosecutors had no evidence against them to proceed with the case. In a recent development, police visited the family last week to inform them that semen was found on the child's underwear. This was the first time they had heard of this. In an email response to Carte Blanche, police said DNA samples were "being processed". But, would not give any further information.

A four year old girl, Mia Botha, went missing in September last year. Her body was found the following day. She had been suffocated, wrapped in plastic and dumped on a school field near her home. It's been almost a year since then, and the investigation into her murder has seemingly stalled.
caseStudies: Udene Botha

title: CHURCH ABUSE
oneLiner: The church is meant to be a place of refuge and salvation. But for the people in this story, it's been a symbol of their torment and trauma.
summary:
A broader investigation into instances of abuse - including spiritual abuse - at churches. I’d particularly like to approach this as an undercover investigation, attempting to capture first-hand accounts of the alleged abuse. I also have victims and doctors who will speak to me for this story.

It’s a megachurch with branches around South Africa, with a particularly large following in Du Noon. Each week, thousands of worshippers flock to its doors, seeking prayer, guidance, and salvation. But for some congregants, the St John’s Apostolic faith Mission Church is also a place of torment. It’s here where some teenagers and young adults who have displayed signs of mental illness are brought to by their concerned family - for ‘spiritual cleansing’ and healing. The method of ‘redemption’: physical beatings and other forms of abuse - whilst their hands or feet are chained! The church leaders believe that mental illness is a form of demonic possession, and that anyone displaying signs of such or psychosis, must be ‘treated’ accordingly. Some former congregants who have come forward claim they were beaten with a sjambok whilst chained up, and even burnt with battery acid! Similar accounts have been heard by worshippers at the church’s Delft branch. Most of the cases have been reported to the Cape Mental Health Board by doctors working at mental health facilities (Lentegeur, Karl Bremer and Eerste River Hospitals, in particular), who have treated these patients post their church encounters. The scope of these complaints has now warranted an investigation by the Cape Mental Health Board, into instances of abuse at these churches.

title: The Skaftin & The Cat
oneLiner: Murder most foul using poison
summary:
"Within the infant rind of this small flower, poison hath residence and medicine power." Poison is older than Shakespeare. It was discovered by ancient civilizations and was used as a hunting tool to expedite the death of prey or enemies. Humanity may have "progressed" in our development of weaponry to rid ourselves of our enemies but the use of poison has not ceased. In fact, perhaps this is the power of poison in a technological age - why use poison when you can simply use a gun? It makes sense when your enemy holds many secrets which are traceable to you and therefore, a "quiet" inexplicable death which mirrors some unknown illness is more palatable. Carte Blanche delves into the murky world of political poisonings through the stories of those who claim they were victims of the invisible sword.

- The mysteriousness of poison - Murder by poison - Plots to kill whistleblowers - An unintentionally murdered cat - Conspiracy theories - is it fact or fiction?

title: Art of the Con
oneLiner: When con artist Art Viljoen was caught with his pants down, he fled the country. His thieving ways revealed much more. An investigation that lead us to unexpected PPE misconduct.
summary:
Then the big sell - Art has designed rendering software that Architects use worldwide to render their complex drawings. Because architects may have too many clients and don't have enough server space, they rent server and rendering capacity from Art. He is so over capacitated by clients that he needs to get more computers so that he can service them. He shows Mr Mazibuko his bank account sporting a 'mere' R6 million rand. Mr Mazibuko asks why don't you buy more computers if you have that kind of money? Why do you want to share your profits? Art says he's trying to secure a property in the Cape so he'd rather bring investors on board. All Mr Mazibuko has to do is for every computer he invests in for R100 000 per computer, he will get at least a 10 to 20 percent return monthly. Mr Mazibuko is hooked - He immediately finds R500 000, to invest in 5 computers. And in the first two months sees substantial returns, as is the case in every good Ponzi, Mr Mazibuko is so excited that he voluntarily dips into his access bond for another R1 million this time. True to his word and the "Evergreen" contracts that were signed between them, the next two months Mr Mazibuko saw a R200 000 return on his investment, he was so impressed, he knew he could see that his rockstar life-style would soon be a reality. So what does he do? He hocks his R 800 000 car, for another R500 000 investment into RolfArt! So now he's R2M down the hole and waiting for his next payout, but he gets a frantic call from Art to say the account has been frozen by SARS and he needs R1M to get out of this situation. Mr Mazibuko wants to oblige, but he has no money left and he's desperate for his returns, so he goes in search for someone to bail Art out for R1M, after all this guy is living the dream and he's successful. But no-one wants to help Mr Mazibuko out. Then Art calls him to say it's okay, all he needs is R250K to pay the SARS person off to make it all go away. But Mr Mazibuko is out of contacts, so in theory the money stays frozen. But then he gets a call from Keagan, the side kick to say listen all is not good, you need to come and see Art. When he arrives at the mansion Art is beaten up black and blue.. the concerned Mr Mazibuko wants to help, but Art says there's no point, he owes a lot of people money and he can't pay it back. Mr Mazibuko doesn't want to believe what he is hearing, so he still thinks he can salvage the situation and get his R2 M back, but here Art confesses that there is no money, and it was all a con and that some really bad people are after him. Dejected Mr Mazibuko leaves, but he wasn't going to take things lying down, the next day he goes to Art's father's house but they tell him to go away. He goes back to the mansion, but Art is gone. When he speaks to the people in the other houses, they tell him Art was renting the properties and he owed them a lot of money. He gets the contact to call the Israelis who were the one's that supposedly beat Art up for owing them money, but they tell Mr Mazibuko to butt out of their business. And the supercars are gone. He was hoping to attach one, so that he could at least get something back from his investment.

Meet Art Viljoen (ex NBA Basketball player) or don't! Who is Art Viljoen and what did he do? Art lived the dream lifestyle - With prime property in Sandhurst - a mansion or two - expensive watches, and supercars gallore! Maclarens, Lambos, Porches and Ferarris strewn in his driveways with personalised number plates, parked for everyone to see. On return from America Art settled back in SA creating a reputation as an internet nerd who'd made it big. He was introduced to a number of high rollers through a "Supercar club." Meet "Mr Mazibuko", who wants to keep his identity hidden. A dentist with modest earnings. He was introduced to Art at the Supercar club and was told that Art had a special investment opportunity for a few "special"people. At first Mr Mazibuko wasn't that interested, but a few weeks later he was told the opportunity was still open. So he agreed to meet Art at his mansion in Sandhurst. On arrival he is dazzled by the supercars in the driveway, then led into the mansion where he is taken into a tightly secured computer server room together with Keagan, Art's sidekick. To gain entrance Art has to do full retina and fingerprint ID and then the doors open! The ice cold room is lit up with computers and lights flashing in vivid colours. Here is where the business is done Art tells him. He shows Mr Mazibuko a portfolio of his clients from Macdonalds to BMW on his RolfArt website.

summary:
It’s been another year of devastation on the job market, food prices rocketing and a growing number of South Africans on SASSA grants. The EFF said: Where there is vacant land, we will take it. Meanwhile Minister of Labour said that the ANC wants to create 2 million jobs in the next year. But what he might really be saying is that this will be temporary, taxpayer funded jobs. South African labour minister Thulas Nxesi wants to add as many as 2 million new jobs before the next elections as the nation grapples with one of the highest unemployment rates in the world. Economist Dawie Roodt says its all rubbish. It’s also two years away from the next national election.

Apart from food prices which has been covered, we are all seeing an increase in beggars at robots, we all seem to know someone who lost their jobs, and there seems to be no job creation at all beyond temporary state contracts. Are we losing the economic battle?

title: Coral Reefs Are Dying
oneLiner: there are few coral reefs in the world, and they are dying due to climate change. Along with it, billions in tourism and important ingredients in pharmaceiticals
summary:
If you have ever been scuba diving or snorkeling in the tropics or even just enjoyed a nature documentary on marine life, Coral reefs are the go-to place in the oceans where almost 25% of all marine life exists. And this is fascinating, considering that reefs cover less than 0.2% of the sea floor. They are essential to the livelihoods of thousands of species, including millions of Homo Sapiens, who are dependent on the reefs for food and economic security. Tourism plays a huge role in this. Then there are the pharmaceutical benefits of coral reefs. The antiretroviral ZAT is made from a sponge that grows in the Caribbean reefs, for example. There are anti cancer agents and host of other medications being researched, sourced from coral. In total the monetized value of global reefs exceed USD 4 trillion last year. And then there’s the protection that reefs afford shorelines, typically in areas that are vulnerable to hurricanes and typhoons, coral reefs break the power of large waves and protects shorelines from erosion, for example. In turn this creates perfect breeding grounds for other shore to sea marine life like turtles. And the reefs are disappearing, Nature has already sent her warning signs.

Apatr from snorkelling nobody really understands reefs, what they are and the benefits it holds for humanity. And they are dying at a rapid rate. We have unique access to a successful coral farming project in Seychelles to illustrate how the world can save reefs, and save billions in tourism spend and many lives as critical cancer and HIV antiretovirals are made from coral spunge. It's all about halting climate change and rising temperatures, and saving our environment.
caseStudies: Flavien Joubert Minister of Environment Seychelles
experts: Dr. Camilla Floros

title: Child abuse early warning system breakdown
oneLiner: Has the state's early warning system broken down?
summary:
The story will interrogate the failure of Western Cape Department of Social Development social workers to detect and intervene in a child abuse case which turned fatal. Baby CJ Frans was allegedly murdered by his caregiver in Vrygrond near Cape Town in December 2021, reportedly after many months of physical abuse. The Frans family have been on a mission for answers and justice, because they say they had reported the abuse many times in the months before CJ's murder. Their complaints were scorned and belittled by the assigned social worker, they say. The issue is systemic, and is rooted in social workers' routine reluctance to follow protocols when confronted with reports of child abuse. The attached document discusses our research into this. The target of this investigation is the social worker assigned to Baby CJ's case, Western Cape leadership of Department Social Development and the National Minister, to answer to the department's failure to maintain a child protection register and to enforce proper "safety assessments" of potentially at-risk children. Attached also are photos of baby CJ with his mom taken before he moved in with his caregiver (when she could no longer care for him due to addiction). Also, a photo of police removing CJ's body from where it was buried in a shallow grave in December 2021.

In-depth investigation showing, through a case study, that social workers fail to detect and intervene to remove children from abusive situations, sometimes resulting in the children's deaths/

title: The story of Gibson Ndzimande
oneLiner: His is a story of resilience and determination : How did this once homeless waste picker fulfill his dream of obtaining a masters degree.
summary: Gibson Nzimande was well on his way to success when tragedy struck. After graduating from the University of Johannesburg and enrolling for his master’s, his plans were put on hold after his mom passed away and a family feud over her house and belongings saw him lose everything leaving him homeless. He was then forced to drop out of school and take to the streets of Sandton where he started recycling bottles and cans to get by. Despite having a BA in Humanities and a BA honours in Gender Studies, he started living in the streets while trying to make a living through recycling and scrap collecting. Unable to go back to school he continued to visit libraries to study literature.Nzimande never gave up on his dreams of becoming a lecturer and is adamant that one day he’ll be exactly where he wants to be. Finally -with the help of a stranger come friend - Sonia Datyi and support from his former lecturer Bret Bennett...Gibson is finally realising his dream and completing his master's at the University of Johannesburg.His is a story of strength and resilience despite insurmountable odds against him.

title: Only Fans
oneLiner: we look at how young South African women are coining it online.
summary:
Some call it a new way to access salacious content online, others say that pay for play social media platform Only Fans empowers the women that take all or most of it off for cash on the platform. Only Fans is a social media platform, similar to Facebook or Instagram, where users are able to scroll through profiles in much the same way as on facebook and Instagram. Difference is that users pay for the content of profile holders who are either masked or unmasked (their families may not know they are doing this) and content ranges from naughty and nice through to explicit. Users subscribe, have the opportunity to tip content providers and also request paid for, personalised content. We meet Centurion-based Only Fans entrepreneur Kyla van Schalkwyk (22) who believes that Only Fans empowers her to determine her own future, and she plans to grow her already impressive USD income to eventually fund her ideals of becoming a property tycoon. She doesn’t fully strip down, but makes a significant amount of cash from her endeavour. We meet her during a photoshoot while designing content for her profile. We also speak to a Cape Town based Only Fans content creator who has made a small fortune from her profile.

- Nobody to my knowledge has ever, in SA, interviewed an Only Fans profile holder on camera. We will be talking to 3. One newbie, a musician whose day job is Only Fans and a sex coach, who experienced the darker side of Only Fans. - It is a way in which young women, particularly millennials, are enriching themselves, quickly. - It is vastly different from other adult industries.

title: Burnt Lions
oneLiner: Free State veld fires in July 2021 reveals the horrific neglect of captive bred lions on a farm near Brandford
summary:
The recent incident of Lion abuse and neglect has shocked the Bloemfontein SPCA to the bone. Charl Terblanche is a hunter. His farm Olivia Lodge is a game farm with lodging where people can go stay overnight and hunt game like impala, wildebeest and zebra. No mention is made on his website about Lions or Lion breeding. However, not only did he have about 50 lions, also 3 white tigers that he allegedly bred with. But, whether it was the recent news that Canned Lion Hunting would stop or the impact of Covid, Terblanche lost interest in his lions and refused to spend any more money on their care. The lions deteriorated. When the veld fires swept through his farm on 13 July, the lions were trapped. Besides the fact that many were already to weak to run away, they had nowhere to go and they suffered sever burns. 30 were euthanised by the SPCA, some had died during the fire... Currently there are 17 lions and 3 tigers that are being cared for by the SPCA. They are making the trip to Brandford twice a week to check on the beasts and feed them.

The Bloem SPCA stumbled upon a captive Lion breeding facility whilst tending to wildlife in need after the devastating veld fires of July 2021. The lions were severely burnt - 30 had to be euthanised. Cell phone videos show the lions, limping, collapsing from severe injuries and smoke inhalation... But that was just the beginning. it was clear that the lions had been grossly neglected, even before the fires broke out. The lions were emaciated, in bad condition and the enclosures were clearly not maintained. Farm workers say the farmer, Charl Terblanche stopped feeding and caring for them some time ago. They (the farm workers) did their best to feed the lions some of the livestock that died on the farm, or the odd chicken. The Bloem SPCA has made several cases against Mr Terblanche and the case in ongoing.
experts: Ms. Reinet Meyer Bloemfontein SPCA

title: Emigrating with pets
oneLiner: Are you leaving South Africa and taking your pets with you? We share the story of three families who did just that and what it took to get their fury friends safe and sound on the other side.
summary:
In 2020, roughly 915 million people left South Africa to settle in a different part of the world. The majority settled in the United Kingdom, followed by Australia. Portugal was also on the list of popular migration choices for many due to the relatively inexpensive way of living. Inspired by Clovid-19, recent riots and crime people are seeking safer options to start a new life. From young families to middle age and retired people, greener pastures are calling them to make that big break and emigrate. The choice is hard when leaving family and friends behind, a big house and relatively inexpensive way of living. But the one thing many South Africans will tell you is that their pets are going with! No matter what it takes and at what cost. We spend a few days with three families from Cape Town, each with their own story to tell: what motivated them to leave the country, why they are taking their pets along, and the emotional roller coaster journey they went through to leave the comfort of their home, their loved ones and face an uncertain but new future.

During Covid-19 many South Africans have acquired a pet as a company. But then there are those families who have always had a very close bond with their furry friends and regard their pets as ‘their children’ who they will never part with. The story takes us through the processes involved to emigrate with pets and the many cogs in the wheel that have to fall in place. The traumatic experience of leaving family and friends and selling your house and the anxiousness pet owners experience when separated from their animals who fly out without the comfort of their owners in a closed cargo section for many hours caged in and not knowing what is going on. Then there are the quarantine sections where some countries require and the ‘pet hotel’ nights where pets are kept until their paperwork has been checked and they are good to be released. Then there are the vet checks and medical certificates, the chips to identify the pets, the size and quality of the crates, the food which needs to go with and the fact that the animals are not allowed to be given a tranquilizer to calm them when they are in a strange environment and no-one to comfort them. There are a million and one elements involved which most of our viewers are unaware of which we will cover in the story.
caseStudies: Lynn Edmeston Jones Pet owner Kim Hosking Pet owner Jade Potgieter Pet owner Riekie Fourie Owner: Pet Travel Agency
experts: Dr. Gary Buhrman Chief State Veterinarian

title: Zama v. Cradle Gold Mine
oneLiner: The cradle of humankind is a UNESCO world heritage site, so is its Goldmine, however, Zama Zama's are picking our heritage apart - we go with the police to see situation evolve first hand.
summary:
I have spoken to Brig. Naidoo and he said that we can set up a big police operation and go in and take them out and arrest them. When I spoke to the DMR they said that they cannot assist with illegal miners, who are also not south african. They can only assist with an already running gold mine that has a license. After a conversation with Anna-maria, I called back, and the DMR national said that this mine would never be granted a license to operate, and this is nothing they can assist us with. I have contacted Mogale city and am awaiting a response.

ZAMA ZAMAS AT OLD KROMDRAAI GOLDMINE AND IBIS RIDGE FARM. In 1992 Gavin Whatley and his wife returned from the UK and set about converting buildings on the family farm for Tourism, ie Art Gallery and Tea Garden. They had heard there was an old mine on the property. In 1993 Gavin met a Mine Engineer from the CSIR and asked him to research the history of the Mine. A week laterGavin was advised that The Kromdraai Goldmine was the first discovery of Gold in the Witwatersrand and suggested that gavin open it to the public. With his technical advice and assistance, Gavin had the mine made safe with 6 tons of timber and a team from Randfontein Estates Gold mine and did the necessary applications with the Mineral Rights owners and the Department of Mineral Energy. The then mineral rights owners stipulated that no actual mining would be allowed to take place, but Gavin would allowed to take visitors in as a Museum experience. A rock engineer assisted with educating Gavin on how to check the mine regularly, and advised to keep an inspection book, which he did for all these years. Outbuildings were converted to a museum and over the years they have collected a substantial amount of maps, documents and artefacts related to the mine. Since opening in 1993 they've had visitors from 136 countries and had a very good response from visitors. The original farm Kromdraai was 4000 hectares. After years of subdivisions, the largest part of the underground mine fell under Portion 26, a farm which was acquired around 2010 by Mogale City Council. It has since developed into an informal settlement. In July 2017, during a routine inspection, Gavin found a hammer and chisel in the mine tunnels. 1st September 2021 That was the first indication that illegal miners were working in the mine. The numbers of miners has increased steadily since that time. Gavin assumed and was informed that the mine closed in 1914 as its gold had been exhausted. The miners were initially removing the pillars of the gold bearing quartz that had been left for support. They then seemed to have found a continuation of the quartz vein. During their couple of years of working the mine, they removed the props (supporting timber we had installed) and damaged the mine to the extent that it has become very dangerous for anyone to enter. Police have failed to remove the miners and so the historical Kromdraai Mine has had to close. It is heartbreaking to see such an important part of South Africa’s goldmining history destroyed. The miners then began excavating the outcrop on the koppie behind Portion 26 and our farm Portion 43. Gavin noted that they were moving down the hill and were soon excavating on his southern boundary. Recently they have cut the fence and are now excavating within metres of their back door. He's talked to them but obviously without result. He'd avoided making them angry or any confrontation with the miners who are about 20-30.

title: The murder of Anni Dewani ten years on

summary:
It is one of South Africa’s strangest cases. It seemed to have been a slam dunk for the prosecution because all those involved in the death of Annie Dewani pointed their fingers at Shrien as the mastermind to kill his wife on their honeymoon. So convinced was the sate that they spend 10’s of millions of Rands to get Dewani extradited to South Africa. But the case was surprisingly dismissed after the State presented its case. title: US Elections
oneLiner: .......we take a look at the US elections taking place on Tuesday 3 November
summary:
The US elections take place on the 3rd of November and we should take note of it – because it is an incredible spectacle and because it affects us directly. One can look at it on the 1st of November, before the election and explain how American elections work, because they are so different. The electoral college system got Trump elected in 2016, although he got less actual votes than Hillary. And what is the issue with mail-in votes. One can also take a brief look at the polarizing left-right conflict and how what is taking place in the US is, is affecting us, and Africa. The US has an enormous cultural and ideological influence on South Africa, such a the BLM movement, etc. Or one can wait a week or so until the election is over and see what is going on – there will be claims of a stolen election and missive civil unrest as the US descend into madness.

title: Munsamy's Millions
oneLiner: An investigation into a millionaire fuel trader reveals fraud totalling hundreds of millions, and allegations of corruption in the highest echelons of the National Prosecuting Authority
summary:
NB NB NB NB NB - WE HAVE DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BACK UP ALL OF THE FOLLOWING CLAIMS The story starts between Jan and Jun 2011 - when Munsamy managed to defraud FNB bank of R310 million, by getting a bank manager Preggy Reddy to issue fraudulent guarantees that Munsamy used to purchase fuel from SASOL through his company Lavela. Munsamy bought Lavela in early 2011 for his wife Leegale Adonis. Using the guarantees, Munsamy was able to move about R300 million worth of fuel out of SA, in two separate deals. He never paid Sasol, and instead Lavela was liquidated shortly after. After the theft, Munsamy and Leegale went on a spending spree, purchasing the $4 million properties in Mauritius and R65 milllion in properties in SA. They also used the money to fund an extremely lavish lifestyle. Since then, Munsamy has also taken lots of local fuel traders for millions. The scam is simple - he promises them that he can buy fuel at a great price from a legitimate fuel company Al-SAA, which will be imported into South Africa and distributed via Munsamy's distribution network run through his company Gas2Liquids. To sweeten the deal, he doesn't ask his victims to pay him directly, but only pay Al-SAA directly through the invoices they send. But in reality the invoices from Al-SAA are fake, and sent by Munsamy to the victims, with a bank account owned by Munsamy. Two of our case studies have laid criminal charges in this regard, in what seems to be very open and shut cases of fraud. But they say Munsamy is not being arrested because he has very strong connections in the NPA and SAPS.

Dr Mahendran Munsamy, a medical doctor who claims to be a hugely successful petroleum trader, likes to live the high life. Together with his wife Prof Leegale Adonis, the couple own properties in Mauritius bought for $4 million (US DOLLARS), a R50 million rand home in Hydepark, easily spend R2 million on a 40th birthday party for Leegale and spend a lot of time travelling to the world's most luxurious and exotic destinations. But beneath the veneer of respectability, Munsamy has a long list of criminal charges against him, has been found guilty of bribing SARS Customs and Excise officials to evade taxes for cross border fuel transports, is a co-accused of the notorious crime boss Radovan Krejcir in a case of defrauding the Bank of Swaziland and is accused of scamming members of the public out of millions in elaborate fuel investment schemes. Our case studies fear their cases will never go to court, as Munsamy seems to have powerful friends in the NPA.
caseStudies: Ravesh Moodley Investor Gerrit Booysen Investor X HIDDEN ID

title: RSA Search
oneLiner: Another one bites the dust
summary:
His modus operandi - a huge ad spend on Kyknet, and radio stations. Utterly convincing and charming. But his desperation for money is evidenced by the fact that he actually accompanied older ladies to the bank to supervise them transferring their funds into his RSA account. And yes, investors did get high returns. Inevitably it all collapsed. Here is the gall of the man: he would approach investors who now have just lost their investments and ask them them for more money for another scheme. He has a history as well - over a decade ago he sold and issued share certificates but did not list them. many people lost millions.

A Potchestroom businessman Ben Otto ran an online directory called RSA Search - an advertising booking platform for accommodation businesses in South Africa. He invited investors to invest into profit sharing of his company. He employed about 15 people. He took in over 40 million rand over the last three years and he paid high dividends . 3 per cent a month, and that is huge. The contract allowed for investors to withdraw their investments after 2 years. But, what he did was use new investments to pay these dividends and when people started to want their money back, he went into voluntarily liquidation during lock down - blaming covid 19. But here is the rub - his little business with so many employees was only taking in about R75 000 a month. Everybody has lost their investments, over 100charges have been laid against him, and following a report on this man I sent to the FSCA, they issued a public warning in the media against Otto and RSA Search.
caseStudies: Kallie Fourie
experts: Dr. Larissa Painera Peter Mr. FSCA Mr. attorney/forensic auditor Mr. Danie Jordan Mr. Hester Ms. Sharleen Williams Mr. Ria Hanekom

title: Kitty Killers
summary:
Many cat owners believe their well-fed feline babies don’t kill and just lie around in the sun, but at night they go hunting, and GPS trackers show they can range as far as 3km from their homes. Those living on the edge of the Table Mountain National Park are killing off an astounding number of creatures, just one cat can kill up to 90,000 animals a year. They mostly kill reptiles and amphibians like the endangered Leopard Toad, but also birds and mice. They kill the reptiles, sometimes eating them, but cats like to play with their prey and so they will bring back an injured bird or mouse to play with at home. Most studies to date have been done by surveys and it turns out that most owners are blissfully unaware of what their cats are up to at night. The UCT and SANBI study, which was conducted over the last 10 years, attached “Kittycams” to cats and monitored what they kill and how far they ranged. They discovered that 80% of the prey is never brought home.

Those sweet kitties who are social media darlings and have more YouTube and Instagram followers than most politicians are killing 30 million wild creatures a year on their midnight prowls. A recent paper released by SA National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI) and UCT has revealed that it’s not just happening on the urban edge of Table Mountain National Park, but right across Cape Town - 200,000 cats. Could well be far higher cause the kittycam batteries die after 2.30 and the cats hunt easily till 6.30am. Cat are a major contributor to the extinction of 26% of the worlds reptiles, mammals and birds and a threat to a further 25%
caseStudies: Teressa Thompson Charl and Melany Brenda Kett
experts: Prof. Rob Simmons Dr. Koebraa Peters Ms. Frances Morling

title: Thuma Mina
summary: Thuma Mina is a call from the people of South Africa to the people of South Africa to show up for each other and carry each other. Hugh Masekela’s Thuma Mina was the message President Cyril Ramaphosa brought to his 2018 state of the nation address to South Africa’s Parliament. He was not only honouring the musician, who had passed away but using the song ‘Send Me’ to highlight – implore - South African citizens to stand up and take individual responsibility for the state of our nation. Now, in the middle of the worst pandemic the world has seen in a century, Bra Hugh’s fellow musicians and artists have come together for a collaborative remix and remake of his haunting call. Why? Well in the words of Zolani Mahola (ex-lead singer of Freshly Ground), who has taken part in this re make, this is an amazing sentiment and call to action for South Africans at this time. She speaks about the spirit of the message, a need to inspire and uplift. We all have a role to play in this country, however small.

title: Child Medi
oneLiner: Making money off sick children
summary:
A private investigator says that he is investigating 30 - 40 cases of fraud against her. Husigenoot wrote several affirming articles on med- help but more recently wrote a scathing article on Amore. Some other case studies - we have Carina Putter - proof that money was paid to Medihelp for her son's operation - R2500. Amor denies this. We have the donor's name as well. case opened. Then there is Christel Le Grange - whose child was born with a cleft palate. Haylee'operation would cost R85 000 Child Medi announced that R83 000 had beeb raised for the operations. She was about to take take the child for an operation but the hospital told her that the it had not received the funds from Child Medi. She was devastated as was her donor San-Mari who was so touched by Christel's story that she alone raised over R23 000 for the operation. Then there is Salena, grand mother of Nathan who too had a cleft palate. One Pretoria donor raised R200 000 but only R100 000 was paid out by Amor - more operations were needed but now Amore is apparently dead and uncontactable! ` Then there is a lady Takkie Nortjie who in 2017 smelt a rat and began depositing money into Child Medi's account to see if she could trick Amore. Sure enough Amore said that no money had been raised. A question that must be asked: How did Amore make money? Surely she would have to be upfront to say that she would take a percentage of what came in? Who works for her? is the operation still running? Where is she?

It's been around for years - a web page - Child Medi that assists parents who need urgent medical help for their children - often these parents do not have medical aid. And by many accounts many children were helped. The face of this organisation - Amor Schoeman - and then it was announced on facebook that she had died. Parents who were helped or parents about to be assisted were devastated. At the same time Narisha Czovek has an interesting story. Child Medi raided R500 000 for her child's operation - the first of many - and the hospital wanted to refund her R130 000 after his first major operation. She said that the hospital must pay it back to Child Medi and she would draw on it when further operations were called for. When she tired to contact Amor, a Linda rang her to tell her that Amor was dead, but she recognised the voice as belonging to Amore and Linda admitted that she was in fact Amor - she was not dead - she took the money for an operation she herself needed. I Have her apologies on whats app, and voice recordings of her negotiating with Narisha on how to refund her R130 000.
caseStudies: Narisha Carina Christel San- Marie Grandmother Selona Takkie Nortjie
experts: Mr. Bryan Bailey Mr. HUISGENOOT

title: Animal caregivers – not all heroes wear capes
oneLiner: Choosing to be locked down at work, sacrificing time away from their families for weeks on end – we put the spotlight on animal caregivers, the unsung heroes of the lockdown.
summary:
We tell stories of amazing individuals who refuse to let animals in their care suffer during the ongoing lockdown, highlighting personal sacrifices in the line of duty. The insert does cover challenges but the takeaways here are the solutions, the “whatever-it-takes” attitude of animal welfare staff and how the public has kept the animal welfare sector afloat. We show how these workers have themselves been getting by while at the centre – preparation of meals, sleeping arrangements, social distancing protocols.

The highlight of the insert is definitely the South African Lipizzaners – a unique breed of white stallions featured in dressage exhibitions. For their upkeep and wellbeing, the animals rely on income from the public paying to see their performances but with the lockdown in effect, there have been no shows so their caregivers rely on donations to care for the horses. At the Lipizzaners base in Midrand, some staff at the facility chose to be in lockdown at the stables where they can continue to care for the horses and come up with ways to raise funds for food and other supplies, not only for the horses but for themselves too.
caseStudies: Adriaan South African Lipizzaners Vivienne Saints Animal Charity Cora Community-Led Animal Welfare (CLAW) Case study who surrendered a pet

title: CRIME CRASHING
oneLiner: COVID-19 impacts all sectors… even Crime. There’s been a dramatic drop in crime in South Africa, but there are new crime trends rearing its ugly head every day as we move further into LockDown.
summary:
With restricted movement, more people home and more cops on the streets criminals are finding it tough to go about business as usual. Last week the Police Minister Bheki Cele reported a dramatic drop in crime since the lockdown. While the figures are somewhat of a silverlining to the chaos of COVID-19 – there are new crime trends surfacing. We look at these trends and unpack the current situation with the help of criminologists.

* IT's A COVID RELEVANT STORY WITH SLIGHTLY DIFFERENT ANGLE * SHIFTING FOCUS - LESS ABOUT INFECTION, VIRUS SPREAD & PPE - MORE CRIME & CORRUPTION - THE CB STAPLE * FOOTAGE OF ROBBERIES

title: INSIDE ST AUGUSTINE's HOSPITAL - EXCLUSIVE
oneLiner: The first private hospital to be closed down amid a COVID-19 outbreak in SA, takes Carte Blanche inside the hospital to explore the tragedy, the threats and the future of the fight against this virus.
summary:
CARTE BLANCHE EXCLUSIVE! We go inside St Augustine – no other media has been in, we go inside the COVID ward, inside ICU and see what has been done. This has been approved by Netcare. We hear first hand from the medical professionals – who speak openly about the shortcomings, the tragedy and imminent threats. These doctors want to warn the medical professionals – they want don’t want the loss of life and trauma they’ve experienced to be in vain.

* EXCLUSIVE ACCESS TO NETCARE HOSPITAL * WE HEAR FROM THE HEALTHWORKERS ON THE FRONTLINE * WE GIVE CONTEXT TO A NEWS STORY THAT's BEEN EVERYWHERE - BUT LARGELY ONE SIDED.

title: BOOZE BAN
oneLiner: LockDown restrictions for South African have a whole other level to it – a flat out ban on booze – we ask what are the driving forces and the impacts of this unprecedented ban.
summary:
The lockdown has been one of the more draconian in the world. Besides a ban on exercising outdoors, buying cooked food and cigarettes, one of the most unpopular regulations has been a ban on alcohol sales. We look at government's reasoning, the impact on the economy and opportunists driving the black market.

* TOPICAL * OPPORTUNITY TO CREATE PUBLIC AWARENESS AROUND THE REASONING BEHIND THE BAN * BOOTLEGGER SEXY ELEMENT * IMPACT ON ECONOMY & EMERGENCY ROOMS

title: Helium 2%
summary: Around 2 billion years ago South Africa was struck by a very large meteor resulting in a huge crater, the Vredefort Dome ..the world’s largest known crater on earth. Fast forward a billion or so years, an IT man Nick Mitchell and banker Stefani Marani - who know nothing about minerals or gases - buy a piece of land 187 hectares in an area around Welkom, Virginia and Theunissen in the Free State, that has gas exploration rights. They buy it for US$1.00. Backed by investment from friends and family, the pair took the project on with the intention of generating a small amount of power to Sibanye and Harmony with the existing wells. A side line industry. They discover from a gas sample that contains 2 % Helium. They know nothing about Helium, it’s what you fill party balloons with! But they do some research and discover it’s critical not only in the making of MRI and CATSCAN machines but also for manufacturing other life saving equipment.

title: Meerkat Investigation
oneLiner: How easy is it to get your hands on a meerkat for a pet? And would you really want one?
summary: There are many people in South Africa illegally breeding and selling meerkats for the pet market. Films like The Lion King and others have romanticised meerkats and more and more people want them as pets, not knowing what they are in for. The truth is meerkats are sociable mongooses. They bond fiercely with their families and if you keep one in your home, you automatically become one of the tribe. The meerkat will bond with you, protect you and viscously attack anyone who comes near you - because that's what meerkats do. It will need to be with you 24/7, urinate on you to claim you as part of his/her tribe, and also urinate on everything in your house as being part of his territory. Alpha females will not tolerate anyone else in the family getting pregnant, and they will not tolerate anyone else mating/bonding with you.

title: Medical Robots
oneLiner: Would you like to have a robot cut into your bones or perform heart surgery, it's not just science fiction, medical robots are making waves right here in South African operating theatres.
summary:
Robotic surgery first became popular in the 1980s. The first surgery was performed in 1985 when a robot was used to improve precision in neurosurgical biopsies and the da Vinci system was used for prostate surgery. Surgery is the most commonly used robotic application in healthcare. Sadly South Africa has been lagging behind, that is until recently. In December last year Dr Faizel Lorgat at the Christiaan Barnard Memorial hospital in Cape Town, an interventional cardiologist succesfully completed the firsts robotic coronary angioplasties in Africa. In Johannesburg, Dr Chris McCready, performed the first state-of-the-art robotic knee replacement operation. This technology could signal a new era in personalised joint replacement.

Soon autonomous robots could be a regular member of any hospital's medical staff, performing duties from taking a patient's pulse and scanning vital signs, to reading case notes and even performing surgery. Some might say thats just science fiction but doctor controlled-robots already have a massive presence in the medical field, and demand for the less invasive, more patient tailored, doctor controlled procedures are growing. Now, in a first in Africa , two South African doctors are performing robotic-assisted total knee replacements and robotic coronary angioplaties.

experts: Dr. Chris McCready Dr. Faizel Lorgat Mr. Neil Kirby

title: Philasande's New Heart
oneLiner: ... in a first for the continent... the boy with a mechanical heart finally gets a new heart...
summary:
In a first on the African continent, a surgical team from Netcare's Milpark Hospital performed the delicate 8 hour surgery which included removing the mechanical heart device, then removing his own organ before transplanting the donor heart. The operation was successful and Philasande is removing in hospital. This operation has never been attempted before and Philasande will be thw first child to ever receive a heart donor after living with a mechanical heart.

In 2016 Philasande Dladla's family received the devastating new that the ten-year-old boy was suffering from heart failure and desperately needed a new heart. But he was too young and too small and there were no viable heart donors available for him. So his doctors hatched a plan... to give him a mechanical heart as a bridge to transplantation - buying him just five years to grow and be big enough to receive a heart transplant. Now after living with his mechanical heart for three years, Philasande's got a new heart.
caseStudies: Sindi Dladla Mother Phumlani Dladla Father
experts: Dr. Graham Cassels Surgeon Dr. Willie Koen Cardiologist

title: Project Flamingo - Spreading feathers of hope.
oneLiner: Women trying to cope with breast cancer diagnoses often face agonising long waiting times for surgery , but a group of surgeons decided that something had to be done giving timely surgery.
summary:
Timely surgery for newly diagnosed beast cancer patients= currently achieved by funded catch-up surgery lits, performed at Groote Schuur and Tygerberg hospital (paying for theatre time and nursing staff) The project started with surgeons doing the surgery pro-bono and initially funding it from their own pockets. This was to compensate for the tremendous strain on theatre and staff resources that have led t a waiting time up to 12 weeks for surgery. The Project Flamingo was initiated when the Amabele Belles Dragonboat Racing team pledged the first donation. It was Kismet. Project Flamingo has subsequently changed hundreds of lives. The project has been expanded to to patients urgently requiring surgery at GSH for colorectal as well.

When faced with the heartbreaking, stretched out and often chaotic journey of a breast cancer patient in the public sector many women find it daunting and feel isolated in their struggle with the diagnoses. Dr Liana Roodt, surgeon at the Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town decided that something needed to be done. Many of these women were subjected to agonizingly long waiting times for surgery. The simple yet profoundle effective idea of "Catch up Surgeries" and "Pamper packs" was born.
caseStudies: Current Patient
experts: Ms. Michelle Rennie

title: End of an era for SA oldest rugby stadium
summary:
It’s been on the cards since 2012 but remains an emotional issue for many old timers. ”Save Newlands Stadium” a group of diehards are desperately fighting back trying to save the oldest rugby stadium in South Africa and the fourth-oldest rugby stadium in the world. The first-ever Springbok Test series against a touring British team was played in 1891. Newlands used to be regarded as one of the best rugby grounds in the world, combining intimate seating, a beautiful view of Table Mountain, and a great atmosphere. But it’s history is not entirely rosy. During Apartheid the Coloured fans were squashed into what used to be known as the Malay stands, later the South stand, squashed behind the goal posts. SACOS boycotted Newlands stadium for many years only returning after 1994. Newlands stadium doesn’t meet the fire and safety standards of modern stadiums, the stands, field and scoreboard all need upgrading and to the WPRU just does not have the finances to upgrade the grand old lady. The WPRU has been in dire financial straits for many years now- current debt could be as high R53-million after interest payments were not settled with Remgro.

It’s the end of an era for Western Province Rugby fans and players alike- the grand old lady will be retired- after three years of negotiations Western Province Rugby Union has finally announced they are moving to Cape Town Stadium as the anchor tenant with 99 year lease. The first Super Rugby series to be played there in 2021. 2020 will be DHL Stormers last year at Newlands Stadium. That’s the end of a 128 years of fine rugby. The City of Cape Town will retain responsibility for repairs and maintenance and the operational costs of Cape Town Stadium. It will remain a multipurpose entity, with Western Province Rugby leasing the Cape Town Stadium for matches

experts: Mr. Paul Zacks Mr. Rob Houwing

title: The ultimate conman
oneLiner: Promises miracle cures through his sauna ozone tent
summary:
Already there is controversy surrounding ozone medical treatment - its still frowned upon by FDA. Now we have wonder cures promised by Ozone Sauna treatment - it can cure AIDS, more than likely kill the cancer you have, or alleviate suffering or help you into remission....take away your diabetes, cure your auto immune illnesses etc. Just buy one of Pieterse's tent systems - R15 000. He supplies a tent, a steamer and a cheap home ozone water purifier. On TakeALot the steamer and tent go for R3950. The ozone purifier goes for 30 dollars on overseas sites. Dr Weir, an oxygen hyperbaric specialist and who treats people in specialist oxygen chambers refutes all of the claims by this man - ozone cannot pass through the skin.......and Dr Harris Steinman, who has a website CamCheck agrees. His modus operandi is to get himself onto local radio stations to peddle his "cure" and then clients call him. Unhappy clients - Indian lady buys tent for for diabetic mother. Tent malfunctions, mother almost faints. Diabetes is not cured. They want their money back. he refuses. Another man buys tent for his brother who has thyroid cancer. he follows the protocol. Dies. Brother wants money back....sensational whats app recording of Pieterse swearing at brother - calling him a fucking idiot. Port Elizabeth lady spends R100 000 on a chamber - he does not deliver. Cancels order.Pieterse says he will pay her back but with 40% cancellation feee. She refuses. Same with a cape town lady who spent R30 000 on two tents but nothing delivered. She refuses. As with a man from PE. Handed over R15 000. Got nothing. A lady in cape town gets machine but it malfunctions and the tent leaks. Then there are two ex reps who say that they did not get any commission. And so the list goes on.

Andries Zagries Pieterse is an alleged conman who promotes wonder cures for all ailments - through his wonder miracle ozone sauna tent - he takes money and seldom delivers. he has been arrested before for non delivery. Operates from Cape Town - great video of his promises.....and we have plenty of fed up case studies whom he owes money to, and experts to refute his claims. The ozone association of SA refutes his claims.
caseStudies: Prakash
experts: Dr. Gregory Weir

title: Forgotten heroes
oneLiner: We hear the stories of four anti-apartheid activists killed in Athlone during the late Eighties. Thirty years later and families still seeking for the truth and hope the NPA will revise their cases.
summary:
The Eighties was a time of turmoil when many young people from the Cape Flats became part of The Armed Strugggle against the apartheid regime. They joined uMkhonto weSizwe (MK), the armed wing of the African National Congress, to overthrow the aparthed state and achieve democracy and freedom. MK leaders became the target of the apartheid security police and some paid the ultimate price. Between 1987 and 1989, four of the leaders lost their lives in Athlone: Ashley Kriel was shot and killed on July 9, 1987 after police tracked him down to a house in Hazendal, Athlone. During the Truth and Reconciliation amnesty hearing, security police officer Jeffrey Benzien admitted shooting Kriel in the back while he was handcuffed, but Benzien was granted amnesty in 1999. Anton Fransch’s last stand was one of the most heroic moments in the struggle against apartheid. On 17 November 1989, he kept the security forces that had besieged his home at bay for seven hours before being blown up. A witness next door watched a hand grenade being thrown onto the roof contradicting the official story: that he had blown himself up. Coline Williams and Robbie Waterwitch were killed while on a mission to bomb the Athlone Magistrate's Court in an anti-election campaign. According to the apartheid authorities, the two blew themselves up when the device detonated prematurely. Their loved ones, however, believe they were the victims of a security force assassination. Their stories were heard by the TRC but, to the family’s disappointment, no one was prosecuted for their deaths. They felt justice was not served. To keep their memory alive, members of the family, comrades and friends, formed a group called CARA - an acronym for Coline, Ashley, Robbie and Anton - and each year, a commemoration is held in their honour. This year, new NPA head Shamila Batohi has promised to reopen some of the 300 cases requiring further investigation, bringing hope to families like those of CARA.

The Truth and Reconcilliation amnesty hearings offered the world a snapshot of apartheid atrocities, but little is known of the impact on family and friends of the victims and whether real reconcilliation ever took place at a personal level.

title: Octopus fishing suspended
oneLiner: In June two whales died in False Bay entangled in octopus fishing gear causing a public outcry and pressure on the minister to suspend all octopus fishing. Carte Blanche investigates.
summary:
Octopus fishing started at the end of 2003 when the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestries - now the Department of Environment Fisheries and Forestries - granted exploration permits for eight coastal regions in the Cape. The idea was to establish a new line of fishing that would be sustainable and relieve the pressure off the West Coast Rock Lobster, a marine resource which continued to decline since 1996 due to illegal harvesting. In Australia octopus fishing was created when their own crayfish industry was facing a collapse due to dwindling stock. South Africa was heading the same way.

There is a misconception that octopus fishing gear is solely responsible for all whale entanglement in False Bay. However scientific research has shown that static fishing gear - especially the type used in West Coast Rock lobster fishing, and gillnets used to reduce shark attacks - have been the cause of most whale entanglement incidents. Secondly, an increase in the whale population the last five years have added to the number of deaths. Since 2014 there have been 5 whale deaths as a result of octopus rope entanglement. Compared to 300 000 whale entanglements worldwide this is a small number. Unfortunately June saw two whale deaths in one month which caused a public outcry and pressure on Barbara Creecy, minister of Environment Forestry and Fisheries (DEFF), to ban octopus fishing; a decision she made on 28 June. In her words: “We will suspend all octopus fishing until scientists can investigate the matter further and explore possible mitigation measures to reduce entanglements,” she said.

title: Painted Fish
oneLiner: Some tropical fish enthusiasts are going to great lengths to make their collection extra colourful and unique... but at what cost?
summary:
The idea of putting together an aquarium of colourful tropical fish appeals to many. And there are a variety of quirky, bright and colourful fish available to give the enthusiasts hours of pleasure. But for some reason, many people are not satisfied with the vibrant variety that mother nature supplied us with. And so a range of ways have been developed to enhance tropical fish... Painted fish are ornamental aquarium fish which have been artificially coloured to appeal to consumers. This artificial colouring, also known as juicing, is achieved by a number of methods, such as injecting the fish with a hypodermic syringe containing bright fluorescent colour dye, dipping the fish into a dye solution, or feeding the fish dyed food. This controversial process is usually done to make the fish a brighter colour and more attractive to consumers. The colouring of the fish is not permanent, and usually fades away in six to nine months.

A couple of weeks ago a Pet Shop in Durban was in the news for selling a tattooed cichlid, or parrot fish. Someone took a picture of the fish and it ended up in a social media storm with animal rightists staging a protests outside the pet shop. The practice is considered cruel and inhumane to the fish. But this is not an isolated incident. Many online aquarium fish shops advertise tattooed fish, and other colour modified variants for sale. It seems to be a thriving industry. The fish are tattooed or injected with ink in the far east and then exported across the world. They are readily imported into South Africa and there is no legislation prohibiting this practice or the selling of these fish. However, some pet shops and aquarium enthusiasts are refusing to take part in this trade as they believe it to be unethical.

title: A step closer to an HIV cure
oneLiner: Two patients have recently been reported cured of HIV - but is a cure really the best way to tackle this decades long global pandemic?
summary:
In 2008, HIV positive leukaemia patient Timothy Ray Brown received donor stem cells with a genetic mutation called CCR5delta32. Brown also received aggressive chemotherapy and radiation therapy; he also relapsed and received a second transplant. After treatment, he stopped ARVs and has since tested negative for HIV. Although researchers believed the CCR5 cells were the key to his cure, it was unknown what role the extreme treatment played until now. This year, two more patients have been reported cured of HIV by stem cell transplant: the London Patient and the Dusseldorf Patient. This proves a cure is possible with a single transplant, low-level chemotherapy and no radiation. But stem cell therapy is expensive and very risky, while treatment and prevention are now extremely effective. By taking a single tablet daily, an HIV+ patient often has a life expectancy higher than average. ARVs reduce your viral load to undetectable, meaning you cannot infect another person. What's more, those at risk of exposure can take PrEP, which removes the risk of infection almost completely. The side effects of ARVs are now almost non-existent, and the drug is cheaply and widely available. South African scientists are also researching the reservoirs in which HIV lurks in the body. At Klerksdorp Hospital, needle biopsies of deceased HIV positive patients determine whether the virus sits in the brain, the back of the eyeball, the liver, the heart....areas difficult to access in a living patient. This research will help to develop drugs that penetrate these areas. Why then, the emphasis on a cure? Patients demand a cure - treatment may be cheaper and more practical. This has been described as an arms race between cure and treatment.

For more than a decade, the so-called 'Berlin Patient' American Timothy Ray Brown has held the distinction of being the only person in the world to be cured of HIV. He was cleared after undergoing intensive rounds of chemotherapy, radiation and crucially, stem cell transplant to treat his aggressive leukaemia. Now Brown has been joined by two more patients - the London Patient and the Dusseldorf Patient - who also received stem cell transplant for blood diseases. The announcement brings excitement that we may be a step closer to curing HIV - but with treatment and prevention now so effective and non-toxic, is an expensive high-tech cure really the way forward?

title: Sleep - The New Wonder Drug
summary: Scientists have discovered a revolutionary new treatment that makes you live longer. It enhances your memory, makes you more attractive. It keeps you slim and lowers food cravings. It protects you from cancer and dementia. It wards off colds and flu. It lowers your risk of heart attacks and stroke, not to mention diabetes. You’ll even feel happier, less depressed, and less anxious. Its called sleep, what we don’t have enough of, Chronic sleep deprivation has been called ‘the disease of our time’. A century ago, people slept for an average of nine hours a night, today it is closer to seven hours. Strict schedules of full work or school days, early mornings for exercise, late nights for television or emails all disrupt our circadian rhythms. Sleep is the thing we regularly sacrifice for ‘more important’ activities. The effects of insufficient sleep are horrifying: poor memory, weight gain, low mood, higher anxiety, lower libido, shorter life expectancy. It makes you more likely to get cancer, dementia, Alzheimer’s, diabetes, flu or a cold. You’re more likely to suffer a heart attack or stroke and more likely to die in a car crash. Regularly getting less than seven hours a night is as harmful as smoking or drinking to excess. There is serious evidence that lack of sleep is a factor in the onset of depression and schizophrenia, and is even associated with the symptoms of ADHD.

title: Death Matters
oneLiner: Space for traditional burials is fast running out, but besides cremation, what are the alternatives?
summary:
In South Africa, a new trend of eco burials is emerging. This means that the body is not embalmed, often wrapped in cloth and buried in a wicker or paper mache coffin. This makes the actual burial a lot more environmental friendly, but it does not solve the space problem. Cremation solves the space problem, but it has a huge environmental footprint. It takes about 15KWH of electricity to cremate one body. Besides the smoke pumped into the atmosphere, greenhouse gases are also released, not to mention toxic formaldehyde from the embalming process and other chemicals used in the making and varnishing of the coffin. Every body is cremated in a wood coffin, once again using a great deal of wood. Internationally there are some alternatives emerging...

It is estimated that there are about 25,000 burials in Johannesburg per annum, and space is fast running out. Not only do burials take up space, but cemeteries are often dead space and costly to maintain. On top of that is the environmental footprint of a traditional burial. Bodies are embalmed with formaldehyde and coffins are made of wood (a precious resource) and often lacquered and glued that end up leaching into the soil. Coffins are also very often lined with plastic which slows down the decomposition of the body. But what are the alternatives and are they viable options for the future?

title: The house that hemp built
oneLiner: Tonight on Carte Blanche: We look at the revival of hemp and why marijuana’s cousin could soon be big business.
summary:
Not to be confused with marijuana or dagga, hemp is a non-psychoactive related crop which has many uses - fabric, oil, cosmetic, and building materials - all extremely eco-friendly. Tony Budden, Co-founder of Hemporium explains: “The industrial varieties of cannabis, referred to as hemp, are low in tetrahydrocannabinol or THC, the psychoactive compound found in recreational and medicinal cannabis that makes you high. Hemp is prized for its long stalk with few branches and strong fibre, while marijuana or dagga is prized for its flowers and bushy shape. Industrial cannabis is planted around 200 plants per square metre while the smokeable varieties are around 1 plant per square metre. Hemp is an agriculture while marijuana is generally horticulture,” he says. Budden is a Cape Town based hemp producer from Noordhoek, recognised globally for his research and expertise in the manufacturing, packaging and selling of hemp products.

Hemp is more than a plant, more than a food, more than a material. Sometimes a hot button topic; impressions of hemp can range from misconceptions about its relation to drugs to the rough, all-natural craft items sold on the streets of Cape Town. Hemp is grown legally in over 40 countries worldwide: South Africa is not one them. The reason? For the last 20 years government has been dragging its heels in the issuing of commercial licenses to grow hemp locally. With a renewed interest in the commercial value of the plant globally, the South African government is now putting together an intergovernmental team to provide a legal framework for the hemp industry which could change the landscape forever.

title: Leslee Udwin
oneLiner: Can you teach empathy? internationally acclaimed film director and producer, Leslee Udwin is bringing her revolutionary educational program to South Africa
summary:
Leslee was voted by the NY Times the No 2 Most Impactful Woman of 2015 (second to Hillary Clinton), and has been awarded the prestigious Swedish Anna Lindh Human Rights Prize (previously won by Madeleine Albright). She has also been named Safe’s Global Hero of 2015, Global Thinker by Foreign Policy. A BAFTA and multi-award winning filmmaker and Human Rights Campaigner, Leslee’s documentary “India’s Daughter”, has been critically acclaimed around the globe, won 32 awards (including the Peabody Award and the Amnesty International Media Award for Best Documentary 2016) and sparked a global movement to end violence against women and girls. The searing insights yielded by the 2½ journey making “India’s Daughter”, led Leslee to found UK-and-US-based Not for Profit global education initiative “Think Equal”.In consultation with some of the world's best educators and creative thinkers, including Sir Ken Robinson, she came up with a programme called Think Equal. This course is designed for 3, 4, 5 and 6 year-olds (being the age children are forming their values and personalities) to teach empathy, non-racialism, equality and non-violence. It is being taught in 8 countries around the world , including India, Sri Lanka, Canada, Kenya, Mexico, Argentina and in January the pilot project will be rolled out in dozens of pre-schools in South Africa.

South African educated Leslee Udwin has won several awards for her hit film East is East. But it is the Peabody Award she won for the documentary India's Daughter that has helped to define her new interest. Detailing the rape and murder of young medical student on a bus, this was the crime that galvanised Indians to protest against the treatment of women and girls in their country. Leslee was so shocked by the prevailing attitude of men, including educated men towards the rights of women, that she decided to try and change the way society treats its girls and each other.

title: Fourth Power
oneLiner: More than 12 000 people have been cheated out of their hard earned cash when they invested in a company called Fourth Power Investments. We track down the fraudster behind the scheme and put him on th
summary: In 2016 a Pastor by the name of David Cupido from Touws River in the Western Cape started spreading the word about an investment option that will earn the local folk thousands of rands without lifting a finger. He lured them in by promising unusual high returns of 117% per month which will effectively more than double their money each month. (For example if they invested R1000 this month then they will have R2 340 the next month). It was easy to convince them from the pulpit where Cupido cut out a trusted figure. From a handful of churchgoers to a few hundred investors Cupido’s scheme became the talk about town and so the money rolled in for the pastor. The pastor realised the power of ‘four’ and so he called upon friends to become his ‘agents’ to triple the mission of gaining investors. It was not hard to convince the agents as they were promised a percentage every month as long as they bring in the investors. The scheme was easy to explain and no training needed for the agents: You give us your cash and we pay it into the bank account of Cupido or his company, Fourth Power. We give you a receipt as proof and ‘Bob's your uncle.’ The word spread like wildfire and in no time Cupido had agents in the neighbouring towns and investors streamed in from De Doorns, Worcester, Paarl, Cape Town and even as far as Port Elizabeth in the Eastern Cape. in the first month, some investors received high returns as promised by Cupido. This was a perfect marketing tool as it attracted more investors.

title: The Vilakasi TV Scandal
oneLiner: We ask if start up TV channel Vilakasi TV is bonafide or a bogus job scam
summary:
When Multichoice announced in February that it would not be renewing ANN7's contract with DSTV and that it would replace it with a black-owned 24 hour news channel, it set off a frenzy with over 60 companies launching bids to claim the coveted slot. One of those companies is Vila Kasi Holdings led by Channon Merricks. Allegedly claiming that he had won the bid (even though the winning company will only be announced on 20 August), he contracted around 95 television professionals to work for his budding station (some recruited from the soon to be defunct ANN7). Most began work on the 1 June at Vilakasi TV's offices in Braamfontein. However when it came time to pay salaries at the end of the month, no payment was forthcoming. To date, no salaries have yet been paid. Tonight on Carte Blanche we investigate what's going on. How is Merricks funding his operation? How is he planning to pay the salaries of his staff? Is Vilakasi TV a genuine contender to win the Multichoice Bid? And how has his actions affected the lives of people who claim they've been duped into working for a bogus tv channel?

We ask Vilakasi TV MD Channon Merricks why the 95 people he's employed at his budding television channel have not yet been paid their salaries. How is he funding an operation that seems to be collapsing before it even starts?

title: Ingonyama Trust
summary:
Since the ANC's announcement of their intention to expropriate land without compensation, emotions have run high and confusion reigned amongst most South Africans. None more angry than the King of the Zulu Kingdom following a recommendation by a high level panel report to either disband the Ingonyama Trust and return the land to the people, or to amend the Ingonyama Trust Act. King Goodwill Zwelithini and some Makhosis (Chiefs) in the rural KZN, say this is intended to take power away from traditional leaders and it’s certainly a provocation of war. As a result King Goodwill Zwelithini called an Imbizo with his Zulu nation and although it is an annual event to celebrate the burning of king....’s palace, it was the perfect platform for him to vent his anger. The King threatened the state with war if the ITB land is to be touched and urged his serpents not vote for political parties that don’t care about them. This prompted president Cyril Ramaphosa to pay the King a visit to reassure him that his land will not be touched through land expropriation without compensation. However, although all is well and true for the King, this still leaves some members of his nation living on his ITB land in a place of uncertainty and dissatisfaction. Their legitimate cries will have to continue for now. The Ingonyama Trust was established in 1994, (4 days before the 1994 elections) by the KwaZulu Government in terms of the KwaZulu Ingonyama Trust Act, (Act No 3KZ of 1994) to hold all the land that was owned or belonged to the KwaZulu Government. The mandate of the Trust is to hold land for “the benefit, material welfare and social well-being of the members of the tribes and communities” living on the land. The Trust is a corporate body established in law and is the registered owner of various pieces of land in KwaZulu – Natal that have always historically been part of the Zulu Kingdom dating back to various Zulu kings. His Majesty the King is the sole Trustee of the land.

Tempers are flaring in Zululand as the Zulu king and his Amakhosi reject government’s recommendation to possibly terminate the Ingonyama Trust which gives the King control of over some 2.8 million hectares of land in the KZN province.
