title: 3 Major breakthroughs in the Fight against TB
oneLiner: TB is the biggest killer in South Africa attacking both rich and poor alike now 3 major medical break through ate giving hope
summary:
First there was Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi’s announcement in June that Bedaquiline, the preferred treatment for extreme MDR TB, would be readily available - now TB patients have a third choice, not just deaf or dead. The second breakthrough is UCT has developed a two hour test for both TB Meningitis, which is ground-breaking: rapid diagnosis saves lives and keeps infection levels down. And the 3rd breakthrough is that major funding has been allocated to developing a vaccine against TB, bringing hope to especially healthcare workers who are at more than twofold higher risk of contracting TB than the general population. All three of these landmarks in fighting the scourge of TB have been developed in Cape Town

It’s been a momentous few weeks for the health profession - three major breakthroughs in treating one of the oldest and most deadly diseases in the world, tuberculosis. More people contract and die from TB in South Africa than any other illness.
caseStudies: Dr Muki Shey Professor Keertan Dheda

title: PHARMAGEDDON
oneLiner: Students turn to prescription medication as study aids – just how healthy is this new trend? Could this be the start of a pharmageddon - an age fueled by an unhealthy reliance on “legal” drugs?
summary:
In a hypercompetitive world, drugs like Concerta, Ritalin and Adderall offer students, athletes, young professionals a way to do more -- faster and better. But at what cost? Presecription medication is fast becoming the preferred high. Students are turning to prescription stimulants to help them focus. Popping pills designed for ADHD sufferers they zone into a super alert and tapping into super level of concentration. They study without sleeping and push through exams. Are we entering an age of Pharmageddon fueled by the illegal trade in scheduled pharmaceutical drugs from seeming legitimate pharmacies. We expose pharmacies breaking the law by selling scheduled meds over the counter without scripts and shed light on a frightening new global trend of drug dependence.

This story appeals to both a younger millennial audience as well as our older audience who are parents to teens and millennials. A feature type story with the sexy element of undercover footage and bust. THE FOCUS OF THIS STORY SHOULD SPECIFICALLY BE SMART DRUGS WITHOUT SCRIPTS – we’ve done cough mixtures, fake viagra and sleeping pills before – but this angle will draw that young audience and the older parent groups.

title: Gaming Addiction
summary:
The World Health Organization has included “gaming disorder” in its 11th International Classification of Diseases (IDC). The document describes it as a pattern of persistence and reoccurring gaming behavior so severe that it takes precedence over other life interests. Some of its symptoms include impaired control over gaming, increased priority given to gaming and continuation or escalation of gaming despite negative consequences. Over the past few years, an increased number of documented cases have emerged prompting the WHO to take digital addiction as a whole seriously. Dr Hein Hofmyer, a clinical psychologist at Akeso believes some of the games are designed to tab into the addictive psyche of the player. The use of winning a cash price or having to wait a certain period of time to regain a ‘life” are some of the aspects that create and enhance the addictive behavior. Dr Hofmyer mentions a 19-year-old patient he treated some time back who had lost all sense of reality and was living the virtual life of an Avatar he was playing as in the game. He believes the addiction to gaming and technology is getting wider and wider. Although it’s still in the age groups of teen to mid thirties largely at the moment, it might get even wider as time goes.

When does gaming become harmless fun? Gaming addiction is becoming more and more rife across the world so much so that it has now been classified as a disease.
caseStudies: James Kukoch Nick Watson Mykayla Banger
experts: Ms. Jacqui Russon Mr. Travis Bulford Ms. Adrienne Kirsten

title: Soccer grannies
oneLiner: Limpopo's soccer show us that there is life after 70
summary:
Rebecca Ntsanwisi aka "Mama Beka" started the soccer grannies after she was diagnosed with colon cancer. She wanted to find a way to take the elderly people from her village and get their mind off their problems. So she started a soccer team. And when the game starts all their problems are left behind. Most of these woman are still taking care of grandchildren and suffer from extreme poverty, but soccer gives them an out. It keeps them healthy and makes them laugh. They are a team now on and off the field All old people and children with older parents will be able to relate to this story, if we tell it right Since they started there are now 40 other teams across SA, sorry I think I said 52. I have a call with Mama Beki tonight and will update this with two of the woman with the strongest backstories

This could be a sad story about poverty, abuse and neglect, but when you meet these grannies you realise it is so so much more than just that. It is a story about the joy of life and how no matter how harsh the situation you can always find the light. It is about the fact that life doesn't end because you are over 70, your best years may still be ahead of you. When these grannies starting playing soccer together in 2003 they never thought they would start a movement of veteran soccer in SA or travel overseas to play soccer. And look at them now
caseStudies: Rebecca Ntsanwisi

title: PIC
oneLiner: Over 2 trillion in assets, the Public Investment Corporation, is the largest asset manager on the African Continent. Irregular behaviour by it's CEO and Board Members could destabilize the SA economy.
summary:
The Public Investment Corporation is a public investment entity and the largest asset management company on the African continent. it holds large stakes in several South African companies, and is one of the entities through which the government implements its policy of Broad- based Black Economic Empowerment. The PIC is estimated at 2 trillion in assets and their biggest client is the Government Employee Pension Fund. Over the past few months since October 2017 allegations of corruption and misdealing have surfaced against the state entity, particularly against its CEO Dr Dan Matjila. On the 5th of September 2017 the PIC board received an email containing various allegations against the PIC CEO Dr Dan Matjila. The email contained allegations that the PIC CEO had funded an alleged girlfriend to the value of R21 Million using pensioner’s monies. Other details mentioned in email were that funds meant for the PIC corporate social investment (CSI) were used to finance fully fledged profit making initiatives of MST, and that PIC policy was not followed in extending this facility. It was further alleged that the PIC CEO instructed a PIC investee company to settle the debt of the alleged girlfriend’s company, which was facing financial issues. Following an Internal Audit within the PIC, the CEO Dr Dan Matjila was cleared of all these allegations by the PIC board but Carte Blanche investigations prove that cover ups, corruption and irregular conduct were undertaken by the CEO of the PIC and the Board. Our source says that corruption is systematic within the organization that manages 3 trillion of government employee pension funds.

Over the past few months since October 2017 allegations of corruption and misdealings have surfaced against the state entity, particularly against its CEO Dr Dan Matjila. This stemmed from an anonymous email from 'James Nogu" titled "PIC CEO funds Girlfriend" that was sent to the PIC board and subsequently to the whole company. We have evidence on how the witch-hunt for the sender ensued, and how Dr Dan Matjila ordered an internal audit against the allegations which had specified exclusions, namely his relationship with said girlfriend Ms Pretty Louw. A whistle blower has come to Carte Blanche, who was tasked in finding the sender and who in turn became a victim in the fallout of the investigation.

title: Letters from Mandela
summary: On July 18th, Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela would have turned 100 years. This 20 minute piece, on the centenary of his birth, to celebrate and reveal new information about South Africa’s greatest icon. For the best part of 10 years the Nelson Mandela Foundation and South African National Archives have been collecting and assembling letters written by Nelson Mandela during his 27 years incarceration. Poignant, impassioned, gripping and always inspirational the letters – many of them never seen before by the public - provide new insight into how Mandela maintained his inner spirits while living in almost complete isolation and how he engaged with the outside world that became increasingly outraged by his plight as his imprisonment dragged into its fourth decade. A landmark book, *“The Prison Letters of Nelson Mandela” - the first and only authorised and authenticated collection of correspondence spanning the 27 years Mandela was held as a political prisoner - will be released a week before Mandela’s Birthday. In perfect synchronicity our documentary Mandela 100 will reveal some of the most poignant, the most witty, the most dramatic of his letters.

title: The Lawyer who Lied
oneLiner: What would be the gain to pretend to be an attorney, pretend to practice as one and in the process create so much legal havoc for the victims who trusted you? Lies, betrayal and conning exposed.
summary:
It goes without saying that acting as an attorney would require of one to have a valid legal degree, right? Correct! It just so happens that Shawn Boshoff does not have a legal degree -- as several of his online profiles showed, he has indicated to so many people for so many years that in deed he is an attorney, acted as one for the church in every capacity - on business side and in ecclesiastical manners. Unisa is confirming that Shawn Boshoff never completed his LLB degree. Astonishingly, his 2016 online profiles indicated that he did not only have an LLB, but also an LLM! The Law Society of Northern Provinces is confirming that Boshoff has never been registered as a practicing or non-practicing attorney and that none of his "legal practices" were in fact legal practices, but only privately registered businesses. One of his online profiles which previously indicated that he has an LLB and LLM, has been changed and now reads that he is in fact a "legal consultant" -- still, to be a "legal" consultant consulting on any "legal matters" one would still have to be a practicing or non-practicing attorney with at least a legal degree, right?

What would be the gain to pretend to be an attorney, pretend to practice as one, pretend to have a legal practice and in the process -- in betraying the good faith of your fellow church congregation -- create so much legal havoc for the victims who trusted you? Lies, betrayal and conning exposed. Thirthy-eight year old Shawn Boshoff fits this description perfectly. A highly regarded member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latterday Saints, he was trusted by his church and his congregation. Known as the go-to attorney of the church, Boshoff derived 99% of work for his business, Africa Law Online, from the church as their legal counselor, traveling to Africa constantly to act on behalf of the church in legal matters pertaining to the buying and set-up of business structure and even representing the church as legal counsel in litigation in Zimbabwe, a matter that was settled out of court. On the ecclesiastical side, churchgoers trusted him as a person, their "state president" and attorney. He pretended to have been able to do anything a registered attorney would be able to do -- drawing up anti-nuptial agreements, handling divorces and acting as marriage officer.

title: From Rags to Riesling
oneLiner: We meet two Zimbabweans from very different backgrounds but similar destinies: becoming respected wine-makers in their adoptive South Africa.
summary:
This is the story of Tariro Masayiti and Joseph Dhafana. The former is a bio-chemistry graduate from Zim who grew up next to one of that country's few wine farms. During his studies, he would volunteer on the farm and, over time, developed a fascination for wine and the alchemy of its production. He now works at one of the Cape's most prestigious farms, Nederburg, as one of only two senior winemakers. Two of his selection were chosen by Fifa as the official wines of the 2010 World Cup. His passion, though, is the fragility and complexity of the white varietals. Dhafana came to South Africa in more traumatic circumstances: he and his wife fled Zim in 2009 and arrived in the country illegally. He sought asylum, and once settled began work as a waiter at a restaurant in the hamlet of Riebeek Kasteel. From there he progressed to more sophisticated establishments such as the world-renowned La Colombe,in Constantia, where he would become a sommelier. But, not satisfied with merely serving wine, he too set out to understand the chemistry of wine-making and now makes and markets his very own. Called Mosi wines, he focuses on the red varietals like Shiraz. He is also one of only eight certified sommeliers in the country. Both men, against great odds, have made an extraordinary impact in a competitive and notoriously fickle industry.

The wine industry is in many ways the preserve of the elite: grand homesteads surrounded by hectares of ripening vines in often the most spectacular of settings. Who would have thought it possible for two young Zimbabwean immigrants, one a former refugee, to force their way into this world through sheer force of will and endeavor? Not only that, but to develop reputations as among the finest of their generation. We meet both.

title: Joburg Billing 2018
oneLiner: Despite promises from the Joburg Mayor himself, the city's billing systems remain in a mess...
summary:
The so-called Billing Crisis in the City of Johannesburg has been dragging on for almost 15 years. Initially the blame was laid on the ANC government but in August 2016 the DA took over governance of the city and yet the problems persist. A quick search on social media and in local newspapers reveals that many citizens are still frustrated with billing issues, incorrect readings and unhelpful call centre staff. In short. The billing process in Johannesburg is still a nightmare. Lawyers dealing with the COJ on a daily basis say that the problems are not going away and puts the blame on a faulty billing system, one that simply bumps a query off the system after 30 days - whether it has been resolved or not. At the same time there seems to be a lack of control from the top. Mayor Herman Mashaba is adamant the problem is being sorted, but the range of issues that remain a problem speaks to the fact that there is little or no control over the city's various departments that are in charge of running the billing system. There are issues with meter readings, inconsistent readings & and numbers captured to the system incorrectly. Smart meters are not necessarily solving the matters as the supposed reading they send to the billing department are sometimes altered (not sure whether this is intentional or a system error). The COJ Query System is another point of contention. Call centre operators are untrained and unskilled and can really do very little to assist the customer. Essentially when you log a query it gets placed on a big pile and if it get sorted it is a miracle. The City's contractors are clearly flouting the City's own rules. By law your water cannot be cut, and electricity cannot be cut if your account is being disputed, but there are hundreds of cases of people being disconnected from services.

We have Mayor Herman Mashaba on camera promising to resolve the so-called Billing Crisis. Former MMC for Finance Dr Rabelani Dagada also promised on two occasions that he would personally solve the city's billing woes. Yet here we are one year later and judging by the amount of complaints and newspaper articles, and social media posts, the City's problems are far from over.

title: Hate Crime and Hate Speech Bill
oneLiner: The bill to criminalise hate crimes and hate speech has been approved by cabinet, with a prison sentence of up to three years or more. Some Legal experts argue that morality cannot be legislated.
summary:
Over the last couple of years South Africans have seen an escalation to the intolerance of hate speech and hate crimes. From Racial slurs posted on social media and seemingly harmless throw away comments that have not let the perpetrators off the hook. Helen Ziller had to apologise for saying “colonialism's Legacy was not all negative” Followed by Penny Sparrow, the racist estate agent who also had to make a public apology after “tweeting that black people are like monkeys. But recently crazed estate agent Vicky Momberg wasn't so lucky, she received a 3 year prison sentence after shouting the “K” word 43 times to a police officer, when he was trying to help her after her after a smash and grab incident. She was convicted for “crimen injuria” in a landmark case against racist and hate speech. Mark Lamberti CEO of Imperial resigned after referring to one of his employees Adila Chowan, as ”an employment equity employee” Could the new Hate Crime and Hate Speech Bill open the floodgates to a litigation frenzy, and cross the boundaries of what is really an impairment to one's dignity? How will this affect the way we communicate in anger or in jest? When is the comment so serious that it gets to court, and why do we need a new bill when there are already measures in our law and constitution that cover these types of crimes? Carte Blanche explores the consequences of such a bill, and talks to some people who have had incidents of race and gender bashing etc and who wish that if the bill had existed in the past, they may have done something about the way they had been treated.

Can the next insult you make land you in prison? With the New Hate Crime and Speech Bill you will have to mind your p's and q's or else...

title: Qooh me
oneLiner: An app called Qooh me is giving teenagers the perfect porthole to bully each other anonymously
summary: Qooh is an app that allows the user to ask questions and anyone can answer them anonymously. Its main users are between the age of 10-16. Over the years it has had a bad reputation for creating a safe space for bullies and sexual predators to verbally assault young people. In an era where a child's self-esteem is now almost entirely build from their online presence, this app is dangerous and parents need to be warned. You can’t keep your kids off social media, but you can be informed and protect them. Adriennes daughter's Carmen tried to take her own life last year after being bullied on Qooh me. At the time Adrienne didn't even know that Carmen was on Qooh me, she was informed by the school principle after one of the other students brought in frame grabs from Carmens Qooh me show how badly she was being bullied. Adrienne has these frame grabs still. Carmen has been moved to another school and has been in therapy since she tried to take her own life. She is willing to tell us her story. Carmen's friend Bianca was also bullied to the point where she didn't want to leave the house anymore. She stopped eating, because people on Qooh me where telling her she was fat. Both girls have now left Qooh me, but everyday more young people are joining this app. Within the first 6 months of launching, in 2011, the app had 170 000 registered users Many teenagers link the app to their Instagram, so they will share a photo and ask “do I look good in this?” or “what do you think of my hair?”. They are actively seeking affirmation from strangers online. When asked why they keep going onto the app if people are so cruel one teen responded by saying that “the positive things that are said are worth trying to ignore the mean stuff” Qooh me was created by a 23 year old South Africa lawyer. The IP is now based n Vegas though. Its revenue is largely generated by google adverts. Advertisers like Damlin and Moyo are regulars on the app. I know you are not mad on using Emma again, but she is so clued up on this and is representing 5 bullying cases from the app. We can interview her partner instead of her if you would prefer? Then I am currently looking for a strong black child psychologist to explain these tweens psyche with regards to being online and why they would even entertain such a toxic app.

title: A Hike of Hope
summary:
The horror of being burnt and the painful months of reconstructive surgery are only the start of a life adapting to living on the edges of society. This is the journey William Baartman, it began at the age of three when he survived 75% of his body burnt in a fire that killed his sister. This April, William embarks on another journey - climbing from Kathmandu to Base camp with 15 others from around the world who are highlighting the plight of burn survivors. They aim to raise R2 million to refurbish the Kimberley Burn Unit and establish the work of the Avela Foundation. William dropped out of school at 12 because he couldn’t handle the teasing and bullying anymore. Today, William heads up the Volunteer group at the Burns Unit at Red Cross Children’s hospital and is working with survivors’ families thanks to an incredible encounter with El Salvadorian volunteer, Cami Paloma. Cami Paloma came to South Africa to work as a volunteer - as a retired successful businesswoman and recently divorced, she was looking for a new challenge in her life. Cami volunteered in the Burn Unit at Red Cross for three years, co-ordinating the work of volunteers. Because of her work with the Burns Unit, she met William through a mutual friend. William was unemployed and together they decided to do the Lifeline training course. William had never received any psychological help and had spent his life feeling useless and isolated. When the course was over, he felt a void in his life and Cami invited him to join her as a volunteer at the hospital. Working with children and their families at the Burns Unit has changed his life. He now heads up the programme and Cami spends her life fund-raising for the Avela Foundation. Avela has teamed up with the Smile Foundation and together they donated a laser machine to the Red Cross Children’s Hospital. Laser treatment softens keloid scarring and helps to heal disfigurement.

This story is about hope and new beginnings. A story that could be very bleak is instead one of inspiration and hope. Fifteen people are walking from Kathmandu to Everest Base camp to raise funds and awareness for burn survivors and their families, and in their party is William Baartman, a 42-year-old survivor. William, who has been unemployed all his life, has recently found his purpose, campaigning for the cause of burn survivors and helping them and society live with their scars.

title: Footsteps to Inspire
summary: Footsteps to Inspire 2017 will go down as the year that saw the silence around sexual harassment and abuse vocalized. In fact TIME magazine named their person of the year “The Silence Breakers” – the people who came forward and broke the silence and shared their stories…. A movement which saw powerful men and prominent men being forced to step down from their prominent positions. Claire McFarlane is a South African, her story of survival and strength reads very much like Alisons. In 1999 she was brutally raped and left for dead on the streets of Paris, France. After her ordeal she buried what had happened never speaking about it, trying not to think about her brutal assailant. Ten years later her rapist was identified after another rape and his DNA matched, Claire returned to Paris to identify him. What followed was long struggle to find justice and it only came to a close on 1 October 2015. The ordeal lasted 16 years, during which she relived her trauma but she believes through sharing her own story of survival, she has become become an advocate for survivors of rape.
caseStudies: Claire Mcfarlane

title: Land Expropriation Without Compensation
summary:
“The time for reconciliation is over. Now is the time for justice”, these are the words by EEF CIC Julius Malema as he raised a motion in parliament for Land Expropriation without compensation in South Africa. All under a banner of social justice and economic equality for all who are South African, but in particular black South Africans. The debate on land is however not new as for years it has been believed that the restoration of black dignity and economic justice for the majority of South Africa lies in the said over 80% of the country’s land that is the hand of the white minority. However the numbers are never the same as political parties and organization always churn out numbers that suit their side of the race or interest. According to AgriSA Black ownership of fertile Land has increased significantly since 1994. It found previously disadvantaged individuals currently owned 26.7% of farming land, up from 14.9% in 1994, and almost half of “land potential” – which AgriSA defined as land having potential fertility, the share is 46.5%. But for years political parties have been fueling the notion that over 80% of the land is in “white” hands. The information is always blurred across racial lines, so who is in fact is fooling whom?

24 years after democracy, black disenfranchised South Africans only own 4% of rural land and 30% of urban land while the white minority own 72% and 49% of rural and urban land respectively, according to the land audit report. Following a motion in parliament to review the constitution on Land expropriation without compensation, is government finally correcting the injustices of the 1913 land act or are the fears of economic instability justifiable?
experts: Mr. Tembeka Ngcukaitobi Mr. Julius Malema Prof. Ruth Hall Mr. Enoch Gondogwana

title: Tower of Terror
oneLiner: Shocking conditions at Tower hospital in the Eastern Cape revealed...
summary:
According to Sukeri the number of deaths at Tower is far greater than the official figures supplied by the Department of Health. According to the Department 25 patients died between 2012 and 2017. However, Sukeri claims that the original register was replaced with a new one, which was backdated. He has copies of the original register which shows that 90 patients have died since 2010 – 4 in January 2018. Sukeri also claims that only two of the four patients that passed away in January were officially signed off by a doctor. Other complaints include; the state of the clothes of the patients, which are threadbare despite a sizeable amount budgeted for, food is of a poor quality and very little, and there is no doctor on duty over the weekends. According to reports there is only 1 psychiatrist at the Tower Hospital. The rest of the care is managed by sisters an nursing staff. Patients who become rowdy are moved to solitary confinement, but at Tower Hospital they choose to ignore guidelines, often leaving patients in solitary confinement for long periods, in a room with only a bucket and no toilet facilities.

In the wake of the Esidimeni scandal in Gauteng, psychiatrist Dt Kiran Sukeri has exposed the dire conditions at the Tower Psychiatric Hospital in the Eastern Cape. As far back as 2010 the Democratic Nursing Association of South Africa raised concerns about the hospital, claiming that there was a desperate need for more doctors. Nurses were expected to perform duties outside their area of expertise and the organisation complained about the working conditions and long hours expected from the nursing staff. Now, eight years later Dr Kiran Sukeri is speaking out about the hospital. It seems that conditions deteriorated, despite the Eastern Cape Department of Health claiming that their services has improved over the years.
caseStudies: Kiran Sukeri Khaya Sodidi DENOSA Eastern Cape
experts: Mr. Anusha Lachman Dr. Pumza P Dyantyi MEC for Eastern Cape Health

title: The Land Reform Lie
oneLiner: Expropriation of land without compensation is on the cards. The question is , why has the government embarked on this radical approach to land reform?
summary:
Currently the Constitution does not make provision for expropriation without compensation. Amending a fundamental right in the Constitutions is a drastic measure. Agri SA is in agreement with the High Level Motlanthe Commission on Key Legislation , that section 25 and the requirement of compensation upon expropriation are not impediments to land reform, but rather a lack of political will, wholly insufficient budget, poor implementation and corruption. South Africa's Land Act of 1913 prohibited inter-racial transfers of land both inside and outside what later were designated as the "homelands". It was repealed in 1991, as was the 1936 act. Since repeal, millions of hectares of farm land have been transferred from white to black via the restitution and redistribution processes. An unknown but possibly very large quantity of agricultural land has also changed hands as blacks have simply bought it on the market. If this were to be taken into account, the government's objective that 30% of white agricultural land should be transferred to blacks might already have been met. A recent Agri SA land audit shows much of South Africa’s high-potential land is in the governments hands. According to the AGR SA report, the share of farmland owned by the government and PDIs has risen from 14,9% to 26.7%. In two provinces PDIs and government own more than 50% in tow others more than 40%. Gauteng has gone up from zero to 39%. If the value of the land is taken into account instead of just quantity, the government/PDI share goes up from 26.7% to 29.1% and if potential is considered then it goes up to 46.5% The increased government PDI share is based on deeds office transactions other than transfers. In other words money has changed hands. Potential is based on carrying capacity for livestock and land fertility.

Land ownership and land reform is a highly emotional and contentious topic. Last week Parliament accepted a motion that paves the way for the possible amendment of the property clause in the Constitution to allow expropriation without compensation. The question being asked is why is does government suddenly have this radical approach to land reform? Government currently owns thousands of buildings and has purchased over 2,2 million hectares of land since 1994. What government isn’t telling is why this land has not been handed over to emerging farmers, why is 1,8 million hectares lying bare and why is government holding onto title deeds?

title: The not so dream team
oneLiner: On monday President Cyril Ramaphosa announced his new cabinet: who's in, who's out and what does it mean for you and me?
summary:
By far the most significant announcement is that of David "DD" Mabuza as Deputy President. Mabuza is a man with a somewhat notorious reputation, having been accused of several crimes over the past few years. His rise to power has been impressive, playing kingmaker in the elective conference last December and said by some to have "sold out" the Dlamini Zuma camp. South Africans will take some reassurance from the fact that state capture implicated Lynne Brown, Mosebenzi Zwane, Faith Muthambi and Des van Rooyen have all been given the boot, along with people like Bongani Bongo and David Mahlobo. Significantly Pravin Gordhan now heads public enterprises and Nhlanhla Nene is back as finance minister. The return of Blade Nzimande might be an attempt to heal the wounds between the ANC and SACP, and Nkosazana DLamini-Zuma is minister in the Presidency in charge of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation. This might be because the president expects troubled times ahead for ANC Secretary General Ace Magashule. But strong criticism can be expected by the retaining of Bathabile Dlamini, who has been moved to Women in the presidency (She is the president of the ANC Women's league...) Malusi Gigaba also stays but has been moved back to Home Affairs, despite allegations that he aided the Guptas in expediting citizenship during his previous tenure there. Bheke Celehas not exactly covered himself in glory during his time in SAPS but is now the minister of police. And then a very interesting move is Gwede Mantashe to mineral resources - a move one analyst described as either pure genius or epic failure in the making because of Mantashe's past in with labour union's and his abrasive nature.

On monday night just after 10 pm president Cyril Ramaphosa announced his new cabinet, making significant changes to the executive. And while some appointments will be met with both relief and support, others are sure to receive a fair amount of blow back. Is this the dream team South Africa has been waiting for or a clever compromise by the president in an attempt to unify a still deeply divided ANC?

title: Teachers trading results for sex
oneLiner: How can the people we trust to look after our children during their school hours be the ones abusing them
summary: At a high school in Flagstaff 6 teachers have been accused of only passing pupils if they agreed to have sex with them. Pupils that refused were failed. So far two girls have come forward to say that they actually had sexual intercourse with a teacher to ensure they passed. One of the girls is now pregnant The investigation began when some of the students discovered a bunch of discarded exam papers that showed that many pupils who had failed the previous year had in fact passed During a teacher parent conference that followed many girls came forward to say that this practice is common knowledge. They all knew what these teachers were doing, but they were too scared to come forward The school has been closed until the states investigations have been concluded, which means these kids are having to find alternative schooling in far away villages. The MEC for education in the Eastern Cape says they will disclose what they have found during their investigations on the 22nd of Feb. But no date has been set for the school to re-open. This statement really gave me chills. Grade 9 pupil: “At times, I just wish I was a boy because they are not really affected by this thing. What is happening is unfair and evil. They are ruining our future. How can a teacher whom you see as a father figure say he will only give you marks provided you sleep with him? This is one of the reasons I want to study social work to help young girls who have been abused,” she said. I am in contact with local representative in Flagstaff whom we worked with on Lionmamma. So far we are working on: Parents of the girl that is pregnant A girl who said no and failed MEC for education

title: CHEFS CHOPPED
oneLiner: Who is standing in the way of true transformation in the South African chefs fraternity? Are the old boys club willing to relinquish the reins?
summary:
WHO IS CHEF SHAUN? Shaun Smith is a celebrity chef, cooking school principal, restaurateur, food scientist, and molecular gastronomist. Chef Shaun is the appointed South African National Expert for World Skills - Cooking. Shaun is currently developing the new QCTO (Quality Council for Trades and Occupations) Chef Qualification for South Africa, and is also the DHET (Dept of Higher Education and Training) appointed representative to NAMB (National Artisan Moderation Body). He is co-principal of The Fusion Cooking School and co-patron chef of Fusion World Food Café in Durban, South Africa.

Conflict brewing in the SA Chefs Association (SACA) is threatening to boil over with an affidavit of corruption charges being drawn up by Durban-based Chef Shaun Smith, until June, SACA board member (new board elected 2015), and head of training as well as Designated Head Chef for SACA. Smith is drawing up this affidavit as part of his High Court bid to have his dismissal from SA Chefs reviewed. Smith greatly values his 12-year membership of SA Chefs and was excited to be appointed by government's qualifications authority as trainer and developer of a new curriculum that would for the first time provide a meaningful career trajectory for people who enter the hospitality kitchens through the back doors. Smith has found that despite a vast number of black staff manning kitchens, he's found black chefs running kitchens for 25, and 30 years, but without the paperwork and skills qualifications that would give them the proper salaries and job mobility. He's also found that despite SA Chefs APPEARING on paper to have 70% black membership, it's largely sleight of hand -- large corporate memberships from Tsogo Sun and Sun International make it LOOK like many black chefs have membership of the association, but it's not active, paid-up membership that renewed annually and that brings the chefs into committees and opportunities. When Smith became a director and head of training of SA Chefs he saw a real opportunity to change that. But in the last year two things happened -- the president of SA Chefs Stephen Billingham who runs the fast growing "HTA School of Culinary Art" slated a young black chef on Facebook for questioning the association's role in transformation and Smith uncovered what looks like an attempt by Billingham to siphon association money for certain contracts into his own HTA. According to Smith's affidavit, it was about a year ago, when he was providing training at the SACA Centre for Cullinary Excellence, a kitchen based at the SACA Head Office at the University of Johannesburg, that he was privy to documents that suggested that there were deals in which SACA president Stephen Billingham and his company "HTA School of Culinary Art" unduly benefitted. Shaun saw sample contracts with Lucky Star and the Red Meat Industry Association, where HTA would get 50% of training contracts that had come into the SACA head office -- the contracts had never been submitted to the SACA board or been opened for all the chefs of SACA to tender. One of SACA's founding principles is that all chefs should be able to tender freely for work coming into the association, which is set up to promote and build the industry and develop skills. Smith's claims have not been tested in court or subjected to a forensic analysis...but from the papers there certainly seems to be a case one can put to Stephen Billingham. These papers will be made public when Smith lodged his review application in the Durban High Court in coming days. Almost concurrent with Smith's discovery, as he was still trying to make sense of the information and he was asking questions in SACA meetings, there was an incident where CHEF ELIAS SAMBOKO was slated on Smith's facebook for asking questions about what he perceived as lack of transformation in SACA -- and that the conditions of black chefs had not fundamentally transformed in this country. Smith was about to answer in his diplomatic and conciliatory way, when Billingham launched a rude assault on the young man which left Smith, and members of SA Chefs in turmoil over the poor leadership shown by Billingham and inferences of racism that might be drawn f the government-endorsed SA Chefs Association. Allegations of lack of transformation in leadership of SACA emerged in a flurry of emails between members after the whole Facebook incident in March last year, in which Billingham apologised to his directors after some of the senior chefs and Shaun took him on for his poor, rude, inaccessible, borderline racist response...but the incident exposed fault-lines in the Association where some feel Billingham is trying to hold onto the Presidency unduly (been in the set for 8 years). All Smith's questions about the SACA funds and money to HTA, and his criticism of Billingham, led to his unceremonious axing at the end of June. Colleagues and his fellow KZN chefs (I have emails) expressed outrage at the unprocedural, unsubstantiated and unconstitutional in terms of SACA rules that say he deserves to have charges put to him and a chance to defend himself. Meanwhile the Association's annual general meeting was meant to be held in October, where Billingham would have stepped off -- but this has been postponed indefinitely and there have been attempts by the President and Vice-President (Billingham and a back chef who works for him) have been trying to push through changes to the Association bylaws to make it ever more difficult for young black chefs to get involved -- Smith's efforts to nominate two black chefs to the Gauteng structures last year have amounted to nothing.

title: Ans Botha
oneLiner: The coach that put South African athletics on the map
summary:
In 2013, van Niekerk started focusing on 400m at Ans’ advice to improve his endurance and aid recovery for persistent hamstring injuries. They have been planning to win a medal for three years. In that time, van Niekerk has managed to knock four seconds off his 400m time, allowing him to smash a 17-year-old world record during the 2016 Rio Olympics. Ans observes other athletes and tries to implement techniques in her own coaching that she thinks will work on her athletes. She believes it is important for them to enjoy training. She tries to prevent injuries by listening to the athlete’s body: “if the body says stop, we stop, or go a little softer”. Ans is a former athlete who used to compete in sprinting and long jump. She began coaching her son in the 1960s before other rising stars in the area began to seek her advice. She is currently head coach at the University of Free State where van Niekerk studied marketing.

"Tannie" Ans Botha came into the spotlight during the 2016 Olympics when she was revealed as World Champion, Wayde van Niekerk's coach. Anna Sofia Botha is 75 years old and she has been working with Wayde since 2012. We visit Ans in Bloemfontein where she is training athletes for the current season. Last November she received the IAAF's Coaching Achievement Award in Monaco.

title: East-London zoo
summary: The NSPCA opened a case of animal cruelty against the East-London in May 2017 after they found a baboon, Willian, with paralysis in its back legs and severally infected wounds on its behind being neglected in its cage. The baboon has not been given medical attention and the cage floor was smeared with blood and skin from his wound. The zoo was told to give him medical attention, but after they failed to do so it was recommended that the baboon be put down. A small Gibbon called peanut was also found dead in his cage after contracting TB that went untreated. The NSPCA suspects the TB was from the fact that the condition of the Gibbons cage allowed human to access the animal. The case has been withdrawn awaiting further evidence. The SAPS have not managed to obtain vet reports from the Zoo. And while nothing is being done Carte Blanche has received numerous reports on the terrible conditions of the zoo. There are various people accountable for the state of the zoo. One being the East-London Municipality, who have a budget to take care of the Zoo. Municipality spokesman Samkelo Ngwenya, called the NSPCA's charges “dramatic” and “a publicity stunt". The zoo curator Alison Roux and then the National conservation department who are responsible for issuing permits to the zoo's to house these wild animals The NSPCA had someone at the zoo today and will be able to give us a report on their findings tomorrow. I have someone going to films all the cages tomorrow morning. The questions we are asking are around the case, but also around the animals that are currently been held there. Also why are so many of the cages empty and the grounds neglected. Looking for a Wildlife NGO that could actually help rehabilitate the animals that are left at the zoo, to show that there is an alternative plan

title: "Music Men"
oneLiner: In 2014, Vincent Bones won SA Idols. Vincent was a street child until he was taken into Boys Town. Judge Unathi was deeply moved by his exceptional musical talent and his story of sheer determination.
summary:
This is the story of 'Street Child to Idol' - a story of how Music offers hope and release to replace hopelessness and anger - Music creates a refuge emotionally, physically and psychologically. This insert will clearly demonstrate that children's natural interest in music results in positive emotional therapy, healing and self confidence. With Vincent Bones, winner of SA Idols 2014 leading the way, we will examine the power of musical healing for damaged young souls. We will witness the children's original performances of song, lead by their much loved teacher Kerry Neuwoud. Kerry's appeals for donated instruments for the Boys has had an unprecedented response. We will film the boy's reactions to the introduction of these new internments. Vincent has offered to donate an instrument as well. We are hoping for confirmation to interview 2 boys that show great talent and enthusiasm in their musical skills and an interview with a parent that could not take care of her son - her desperation turned to relief as Boys Town came to her rescue.

Music Men - Boys Town was home to SA Idols winner, Vincent Bones, from age 11, where from an orphaned street child, he was given a home at the NGO. Here Vincent found solace in music and his amazing journey from the Streets to the National Stage began. Mentor - Vincent is keen to spend the day with boys in music classes at Boys Town, Tongaat KZN. Vincent will mentor the students by sharing his commitment to his musical dreams against all odds and his special story of Hopeless to Success. Vincent 'gets them' as he too stood in their place as a young man. Music is a powerful therapeutic tool that can be used to soothe a wide variety of painful human conditions from depression to extreme anxiety. Developmentally, almost all children respond to music as a medium to vent sadness, express anger and facilitate the development of prosocial skills, trust and feelings of positive attachment. According to Music teacher, Kerry Nieuwoud - her students at Boys Town, many who have been robbed of their youth, have shown remarkable progress musically and developed a camaraderie and trust in their group. Most of the students in her class come from Abusive backgrounds, often abandoned by their parents and caretakers. 2 boys will tell us about their road to Boys Town and how music is a way to express their pain and bring them creative release. Programme will be emotive, positive and demonstrate the healing power of music.

title: "Say my Name"
oneLiner: Advocates for the decriminalisation of Sex Work in South Africa, welcomed the ANC announcement at the final media briefing, December 2017, that a resolution had been taken to decriminalise Sex Work.
summary:
The far reaching implications of decriminalisation of all sex work will be examined. We will hear strong opinions both for and against the legal changes. According to Gender Rights activists the removal of criminal laws, will not only make sex work and sex workers safer, but will also reduce the high levels of Gender Based Violence and the high incidences of HIV and STIs in the country. Historically, sex workers have been among South Africa’s most marginalised populations. The current climate of criminalisation means that prostituted persons are abused financially, sexually and physically by gangsters, clients, brothel owners and pimps, often with impunity. Research shows that irrespective of the legal option followed, women and girls in prostitution have a mortality rate 40 times higher than the national average. Sally Shackleton, Director of Sex Workers Education and Advocacy Taskforce (SWEAT) says "Current Criminal legislation has been shown to increase sex workers’ vulnerability to violence and illness and reduces the likelihood abuse will be reported. Shackleton says this new announcement to decriminalise Sex Work is welcomed with cautious optimism. On the other hand, "Embrace Dignity", is a group that maintains sex work prostitutes dignity and freedom and believes that offering a way out for sex workers to find legal employment is what should be lobbied for. Ex sex workers who have, been rescued from violence and human trafficking, will share their stories. The programme will present arguments for and against the full decriminalisation of Sex Work, offering viewers the opportunity to come to their own conclusions.

68% of South Africans within the sex industry have reported being threatened within a weapon, 66% reported being assaulted, and 56% reported being raped. Of the 56% who reported being raped, 58% reported being raped more than 5 times. ANC’S decision to decriminalise Sex Work, recently announced at the final Nasrec media briefing, December 2017, comes as a long awaited, welcome change for Gender Rights advocates. Human settlement portfolio committee chair, Nocawe Mafu, confirmed the ANC decision to legalise all sex work. Once this major shift in the legal frame work is implemented - South Africa will become the first African Country to decriminalise all aspects of sex work.

title: Public Prosecutions
oneLiner: With the capture of the National Prosecuting Authority by the Zuma clique, institutions with financial muscle are pursuing private prosecutions on behalf of individuals who have had cases declined, or
summary:
Private prosecutions are rare, but under our Criminal Procedure Act, ‘any aggrieved private person may launch a prosecution’ if the NPA has declined to prosecute (nolle prosequi). In 2017 AfriForum started the first dedicated private prosecutions unit, headed by former state advocate, Gerrie Nel. Once accused of protecting only white Afrikaner interests, AfriForum is taking on any cases where an individual has ‘suffered personal injury or prejudice’ and for which the NPA has issued a nolle prosequi certificate. Private prosecution is expensive: AfriForum will have to pay a deposit to cover the costs of the prosecution, but if convicted, either the accused, or the NPA can be ordered by the court to reimburse the private prosecutor. Cases have to begin within 3 months of the issuing of a nolle prosequi certificate.

We will examine 3 cases for which the NPA has been given a deadline to prosecute, or has issued a nolle prosequi certificate.

title: Operation Phakisa theft of our Oceans
summary:
Jacob Zuma has sold off our Economic Exclusion Zone- our marine environment in a project known as Operation Phakisa- meaning hurry up. It an ambitious project launched in 2013 after Zuma visited Malaysia which is meant to fast track economic exploitation of marine area for mineral, gas and oil extraction. Phakisa is nominally run by the Environmental Department but the mineral resources department and PetroSA are heavily involved. They grant licences for mining and oil and gas prospecting and exploitation. The idea is to cut the red tape to economic development and the task team reports directly to President Zuma. The EEZ extends 3 million square kilometers and 98% of the entire coastline has been carved into various mining concessions. THe entire WEst Coast has been allocated for Phosphate prospecting with the intention to mine to two foreign companies. The two most destructive mining operations are for Phosphates and Seismic testing to identify the gas fields.

Deep Sea Phosphate mining has not been allowed to happen anywhere else in the world because it rips up and destroys the ocean bed. Giant machines with 11 meter wide graders rip up the ocean floor 3 meters down for 100's of square kilometers sucking up the substrate onto a ship where the phosphate is extracted. If that is not destructive enough the fine silt is then sent back down drifting for kilometers carrying heavy metals which are dispersed by the current smothering coral beds and fish nursery grounds. This is more terrifying than any onshore mining to date.

title: Da Vinci Auction
oneLiner: The recently re-discovered “Salvator Mundi,” the last da Vinci painting in private hands, is set to be auctioned in New York City on November 15, and expected to fetch over R 1.3b.
summary:
The art world is in a frenzy over the announcement by Christie’s in New York that they will auction off a newly authenticated work from Leonardo da Vinci. The painting, Salvator Mundi, a portrait of Christ, was lost for several centuries, painted over by disciples of da Vinci’s work, and only re-discovered a decade ago in the United States. Initially thought to be the work of an unknown artist, the painting was taken to art conservationists for analysis and restoration, and after peeling away years of paint and decay, they realized that this was indeed a work by the master himself. Though da Vinci is known the world over, his surviving body of work -- especially paintings -- is miniscule. Less than 20 works are in existence today, and Salvator Mundi is perhaps the once in a lifetime opportunity for private collectors to add a da Vinci to their collection. In this segment, we’ll speak to Dr. Dianne Dwyer Modestini, whose years of work with the painting ultimately revealed its true author. She kept meticulous records of her work, and we’ll delve into her story. We will also hear from Alastair Sooke, an influential New York art critic who frequently works with Christie’s. He’ll offer insight on the painting, further explaining how it was authenticated and why this is such a momentous occasion for the art world. Finally, we’ll be on hand in New York City in mid November when Salvator Mundi is auctioned off. It is estimated to fetch over $ 100M (R 1.3b), and we’ll be there to cover it.

We will reach out directly to Christie’s to secure filming access during the auction in New York, as well as interviews with the top art experts in the field, including the conservationist who restored the work.

title: Neglected Arabian Horses
oneLiner: Arabian stud horses neglected by respected breeder...
summary:
Hartebeespoort Animal Welfare has had complaints about Kobus Lombard's horses since 2004 - usually in the winter. He seems to leave the older mares roaming on an empty piece of veld, and especially in winter there is very little food. Mr Lombard maintains that the horses need to be lean and fit, but according to nutritionists and welfare workers most of the free roaming horses are underfed. On the surface Mr Lombard presents a pretty picture to the world. His website advertises prize studs for sale and for breeding, but he doesn't show the world what happens to the horses behind the scenes. In 2016 14 horses were rescued from his property outside Brits, they were all very thin. One horse had been caught in a snare and had a very bad wound. HAWS, together with a Vet obtained a court order and the horses were removed. Mr Lombard was found guilty of neglect and given a R6000 fine or 6 months in prison - this was suspended for 2 years. Since then Mr Lombard has moved his horses to a property on the outskirts of Hartebeespoort. 2 months ago HAWS removed another 2 horses. They are currently waiting for a court order / warrant giving them access to the property to see the condition of the other horses. The 2 horses are in the care of Kerry Wolter, who says they are slowly recovering. Mr Lombard breeds the horses for pleasure, and it is thought that he simply neglects the horses once they have no more real worth.

Kobus Lombard is a well-known Arabian stud breeder and was convicted of neglect in September 2016 and received a R6000 suspended fine. Initially one emaciated horse was rescued and then followed a court order to remove another 13 horses. Now a year later, Hartebeespoort Animal Welfare has confiscated another 2 horses and is waiting for a court order to access the premises in order to inspect the health of other horses. One of the horses was very thin and the other had a bad injury to the leg - it could barely move.

Economist Dawi Roodt will talk about the future of money for South Africans. Should people hedge their funds in Bitcoin to dodge a fluctuating Rand? Peter Munnings from Consensys will talk about Etherium - an alternative crypto-currency that has gained traction in the last year. A team in Stellenbosch have developed digital rights management system based off blockchain technology that could prevent piracy of digital media.

title: Arabian Horse Breeder doesn't learn his lesson UPDATED
oneLiner: Arabian Horse cruelty
summary: Already bush racing involving Arabian horses is controversial. And there are a number of Arabian Hose Studs in South Africa where these horses are sold for huge prices. You would expect tip top care for these Arabian horses. Not so with one well know breeder Kobus Lombard of Marok Stud farm near Brits who two months ago was found guilty of three counts of animal cruelty – and it as a marathon trial. We tell the story how animal welfare originations discovered his “secret” paddock where his horses were suffering. The breeder was only given 6 months and R6000 suspended sentence which outraged animal lovers and even the prosecutor. And this never made the press or even was commented on by the Society of Arabian horses in South Africa. Now two weeks ago, the same animal welfare organization (HAWS) who had the horses removed three years ago pounced again, and via court order, removed two more horses. Clearly, the horse owner has not learned his lesson. The slight twist is that the High Veld horse society did not agree with the removal but HAWS is sticking to its gun and are determined to make this latest case stick!

title: Poor state of western cape rugby
oneLiner: Some one will die
summary: Three weeks ago a young black man died of injuries sustained in a club rugby match. Rugby is dangerous enough. Rugby laws try and make the game as safe as possible but aspirant players know the risk. But it the Cape rugby scene, and its been brewing for years now, there is added danger – to life and limb - and that’s appalling violence on the field, and from spectators who are attacking the players. It’s ugly, and several clubs have been identified as being the culprits. Many believe that the Western Cape Rugby Union is not doing enough to stem the violence. It is a political hot potato as main clubs involved are colored clubs, yet across the board, white colored and black players and identifying these rouge clubs as being the chief culprits. It has resulted of referees, tired of spectator and player abuse (running away from enraged fans, dodging missiles etc) going on strike even. Many times teams have been led off the field in protest at the violence, (head kicking, eye poking etc). Club owners are furious. Recent photographs and footage show the extent. Recently spectators grabbed a player, locked him up in a bathroom at the field, and assaulted him. He had to be admitted to hospital. Prior to that game starting the coach of the Violet rugby team spat on the face of the captain of the Villagers Rugby team, which led to a fight. Just last week, a player from a new black rugby club, was attacked as he left the field. A spectator smashed a bottle over his head and he needed stitches. In this program which will be littered with videos of incidents and pictures showing injuries, we will be asking the western province club rugby management why they are not doing more to stem the flow of violence on and off the field. We will speak to a referee who has abandoned a game because of violence, we will speak to those injured to allow them to tell their stories, we will paint the picture of club rugby being the back bone of rugby in SA and how many are not

title: Hurricane Irma
oneLiner: Dozens of South Africans are unaccounted for after Hurricane Irma ripped through the British Virgin Islands
summary:
We speak to South Africans living in Tortola, the main commercial hub of the BVI. What were they doing there? Where wee they when Hurricane Irma struck? What was it like? How are they coping now?

South Africans make up one of the largest ex-pat communities in the British Virgin Islands. From accountants, to lawyers, to boat hands, to bar men, there were a few hundred of our compatriots living in Paradise when the strongest storm the Caribbean has ever experienced made landfall. Seven days later not everyone is accounted for, and the South African government has yet to react.

title: Breaking the silence.
oneLiner: Music intervention for children and young people silenced by the trauma of everyday life in the Cape flats.
summary:
Trauma makes children dis-engage, its shatters their trust in others and self. They become disconnected and unable to speak about their trauma.To children who have experienced unspeakable trauma, music becomes a medium through which they can express the inexpressible. Music for Life/ MusicWorks is a music intervention program based at the Prince George Primary School in Heideveld. The program is aimed at children living in environments characterized by poverty, violence and abuse.

An uplifting story of a music therapy program enabling two young people to escape from social isolation and the trauma of living in communities characterized by poverty and violence.To children who have been silenced by abuse and neglect, music groups provide a safe space where they can rediscover themselves.

title: Kratom (Redux)
oneLiner: The United States has placed it under “import alert” and has begun seizing it at the border, and it’s banned in Thailand. But kratom, an herbal drug made from the leaves of Southeast Asian trees
summary:
From the rainforests of Southeast Asia comes an herbal product that is finding its way to every corner of the world, including South Africa. It’s called kratom, and It’s typically sold as a green powder with pungent odor. Advocates -- and there are many of them -- claim that it can help break the cycle of opioid addiction, manage pain from chronic illnesses, and even alleviate symptoms of depression, social anxiety, and PTSD, just to name a few. While anecdotal research from case studies is plentiful, there is still relatively little clinical research on kratom and its long term effects. Last year the United States Drug Enforcement Administration moved to classify kratom as a Schedule I substance -- the same category as LSD and GHB -- but a massive public outcry and protests in Washington DC forced them to walk back that decision pending additional research. A report is currently being compiled by the Food and Drug Administration. In South Africa, there are no restrictions or regulations on the drug. It is legal to import, sell, and buy, but who exactly is using kratom, and for what purpose? In this segment, we’ll meet them and find out why, as well as speak with the MCC and a medical researcher from the US who is compiling the first comprehensive data on kratom usage and its effects. Is kratom a passing fad, a dangerous trend, or possibly a breakthrough in modern medicine?

We’ll speak with case studies currently using kratom for a variety of reasons (pain management, addiction treatment) as well as hear from a researcher in the US who is compiling the first comprehensive data from all available studies of kratom.

title: Anti-poaching dogs
oneLiner: Dogs are now parachuting from the sky to help save wildlife. Meet the canines that are training to help take down criminals in Africa.
summary:
Arrow and Giant are among 200 dogs in the Anti-Poaching and K-9 Training Academy, run by the Paramount Group. Situated outside Rustenburg the academy’s canines are bred at the facility, trained and matched with rangers from national parks and game reserves across Africa to combat the ever increasing problem with poaching of our game. The two star students have already mastered descending from a helicopter by rope, strapped to their handler, and both have moved on to the next level: skydiving. Parachuting, rather than rappelling - which requires a helicopter to be stationary and low to the ground - would make these operations more covert. “In some cases we have to insert the canine in a difficult situation where you don’t want to scare the poachers with the helicopter,” explains Eric Ichikowitz, director for the Ichikowitz Family Foundation, which helped launch the training programme for the Paramount Group. “The parachute helps engage theme quietly.” Arrow became a skydiving pioneer when he plunged from a chopper in September 2016 as part of an aerial display at the Africa Aerospace and Defence Show in Pretoria - this was a first and a Guinness World Record. Giant followed. Since then both Giant and Arrow have helped to train new handlers and instructors by demonstrating their skills. But Ichikowitz says the plan is to teach skydiving skills to some of the other dogs in the program. At the academy canine trainees specialise in detecting explosives, ammunition, or elephant ivory. Others become familiar with routine patrols so that they can immediately recognise signs of suspicious activity. Then there are the quick responders like Arrow and Giant that are temperamentally suited for rappelling and catching poachers.

Imagine this: Poachers have just shot an elephant. They’ve begun to saw off its tusks just as a helicopter takes off in the distance. On board is Arrow, a two-year-old Belgian Malinois, strapped to his handler, who’s wearing a parachute on his back. In minutes the pair float down near the crime scene so arrow can chase down the poacher and stop him in his tracks. Arrow has yet to carry out an actual take-down, but he and a six-year-old German shepherd, Giant, have jumped out of planes before. The idea is to get the dogs on the ground fast enough to sniff out and catch suspected poachers before they can vanish into the bush.

title: Fake prophets
oneLiner: Seer 1 was deported from Zambia for allegedly sexually assaulting virgins within his congregation and now he has setup a church in South Africa
summary: Seer 1 (Andrew Ejimadu) is a Nigerian Prophet who started a ministry called Christ Freedom Ministries. He has a church in Nigeria and then opened one in Zambia. He has risen people from the dead, provided miracle money and cures HIV and cancer etc.. In April 2017 he was deported from Zambia, as a whole lot of women came forward saying he had sexually assaulted them. The belief was that he needed to sleep with virgins to have stronger visions, but after one woman came forward the others realised they had been manipulated. “Prophet Anointed Seer 1 has been deported under Section 9 (ii) of the Immigration and Deportation act of 2010 which states that “an immigration officer has reasonable ground to deport any person with any conduct likely to be a danger to peace and good order in Zambia, such person shall be deported from Zambia under a warrant signed by the Minister of Home Affairs. No charges have been laid against him in Zambia, but the women are willing to speak to us. He has now started a church in South Africa and recently bragged about the new Roll Royce he just bought, while the majority of his congregation are poor and desperate. It may be a way to look at how these Fake Prophets are manipulating desperate people on the continent.

title: PRESIDENTIAL STYLE
oneLiner: We examine the leadership styles of the 2019 candidates for president - what shaped their personal command style? What will they mean for democracy?
summary: When Jacob Zuma became president he brought into the highest office an amalgamation of his personal styles as the leader of a secretive, underground military movement and that of a traditional chief. Within a few years his opposition party leader Mmusi Maimane characterised Zuma as a "broken president". Where were the seeds sown for the fruit Zuma bore in office? Perhaps it was too poorly understood by his supporters what the dual influences of the military and chieftaincy would signify for his leadership and what his personal style would signify for his command of the presidency. Perhaps we were blindsided by his engaging charm and approachable, affable personality. An understanding of Zuma's personal style and the factors that shaped it may have helped us predict that he might not see himself as someone who has to be accountable to a supporter base or even his democratically elected colleagues. Perhaps we are generally too easily blinded by the bloody political battles that allow leaders into high office, and we err in conferring the status of a hero on the victor. In this insert we go back to basics and analyse the factors that form the character, values and leadership style of the candidates that have offered themselves for the job. Where did they come form? What influenced their value system? How do they exercise authority? How do they handle money? What is their experience with success? Firebrand Julius Malema has seen his support base steadily swell -- but does his personal style contain the makings of a president. What was Maimane's CEO style shaped by and can this propel him from opposition to the presidency? What should voters look out for behind the rhetoric and fine appearances? We investigate.

title: CHROME CRIMES - follow-up of CHROME ZAMAS
oneLiner: After our expose of illegal chrome mining in the Limpopo we track the fortunes of illegal miners trying to get rid of thousands of tonnes ot illegal ore as the chrome market crashes
summary: In April we painted the big picture of how illegal chrome mining operations had sprung up in the informal residential areas of Atok, in Sekhukhune, in the process infringing on the rights and futures of formal, licensed mines on the mountain -- mines like junior miner VDH Holdings and massive multinational Samancor Chrome. After our programme the market for illegal chrome unexpectedly crashed. Overnight there were no more illegal miners swarming the mountainside. The Minister of Mining and MIneral Resources Mosebenzi Zwane ascribed the success on the mountain to the arrest of a number of illegal miners and the appearance of two men whom the prosecuting authorities described as "kingpins" last month. But the truth of the matter is that the international spot price for chrome crashed after the zamas had flooded the market in the last couple of years and the two white men who have been arrested are convenient scapegoats rather than kingpins. Also -- theres been sporadic police action for years -- nothing lasting happens, because even where there are arrests and confiscations, dockets disappear and suspects are let off the hook. The community is far from happy with the state of affairs -- they're still saying that they're simply exercising their natural "right" to the minerals in the area where they live. The deputy minister for Mining whom we spoke to in the previous insert, Godfrey Oliphant, said that they would be workshopping alternatives with the community -- and so they have...but to little avail, as there's no clear way forward and community members have been blockading access to formal mines and victimising the workers of legitimate businesses. Meanwhile a number of people have come forward to Carte Blanche to describe how they have been bullied, bamboozled and victimised by the real kingpins -- a combination of community members operating as informal miners and police accomplices who turn a blind eye, make dockets disappear, assist in hijacking vehicles of legitimate companies and help them end up in the community. So we will tell the story of two sets of vehicles that were hijacked by the "community". The first is a R7-million excavator, belonging to Selwyn Vos of Motwell Plant Hire. Vos' excavator was hired to conduct road-building in the area. The contract had nothing to do with mining. But after the job was done and Vos sent a flat bed loader to transport the excavator back to his head office in Johannesburg, the 'community" led by a woman called THERISA and her husband, who are known to run a yard for heavy equipment in their home near the Meckenburg Police Station, across from our zama mountain. A former military man, Vos kept an ops room and detailed incidence reports of how the police thwarted his efforts to get back his asset, how his drivers were threatened and victimised and how the vehicle was hijacked back from his own crew trying to rescue it to bring home. Vos only succeeded in getting anywhere when he enlisted the help of a police commander from an entirely other province to accompany his team. The story of the second set of vehicles will be narrated by Netstar Recovery manager "Willem" -- not in the business at all, but well able to explain how vehicles are appropriated by the "community" who feel it their unquestioned right to take possession of whatever resources are in the area. We will also revisit the investigations team we featured in the first story -- led by Louis Nel on behalf of VDH Holdings -- they have now, with the help of the Assets Forfeiture Unit (who contacted them through US after our story) put together an online spiders' web of how all the operations in Atok fit together. This they will present in court, in yet another effort to get true investigations into the crimes...not just scapegoating two minor players and letting the rest get away with it.

title: Kratom
oneLiner: The United States FDA has been confiscating it over safety concerns, and it’s illegal in Thailand. But kratom, a psychotropic herbal drug that’s been known to cause withdrawal symptoms similar to
summary:
From the rainforests of Southeast Asia comes an herbal product that is finding its way to every corner of the world, including South Africa. It’s called kratom and is most commonly found in powder form. It looks like green tea and has an acrid smell, but users and advocates say that its medicinal benefits outweigh the perceived dangers. It’s been used for pain relief and as a recreational drug. It’s also been used as a treatment for opioid addiction, but critics say that kratom itself is addictive and just as difficult to quit. Proponents say more research is needed and have been fighting efforts in the US and other countries that would see the plant product criminalized. Locally in Johannesburg and greater South Africa, there are no restrictions or regulations on the drug, and while some users seem to be able to keep their habit in moderation, others’ usage has spiked, as they build a tolerance to its effectiveness. Are they developing a dangerous dependency? Should there be regulations regarding the sale and use of this drug? Almost as a preemptive measure, suppliers in Johannesburg are selling it via the internet, and arranging deliveries at third party locations (in our case, a car battery shop in Randburg). Some websites even offer a discount if you pay for your order in BitCoin, the cryptocurrency that is virtually untraceable. In this segment, we’ll find out what’s really going on with kratom in South Africa, speak to active users, see how it’s distributed, take it to a testing facility to find out what exactly people are buying, and hear from experts on both sides of the issue of whether or not this just a fad herbal supplement or a dangerous new drug.

We’ll speak with case studies currently using kratom recreationally and see hidden camera footage from an exchange of the product out of a car battery shop in Midrand.

title: Long Live The Queen
oneLiner: A drag queen in Stellenbosch is using her spotlight to do a world of good and advocate for LGBT acceptance.
summary:
Enigma Von Hamburg, AKA Queen Enigma, AKA Clayton Robyn (real name) is a drag queen from Stellenbosch who has been performing for over a decade. Enigma isn’t just a performer but also an avid pageant competitor and, now, organizer. Her credo is the Miss World motto: “Beauty with a purpose,” and her goal with her pageants is to advocate the advancement of LGBTQA+ rights… and put on a damn good show in the meantime. This segment will focus on Clayton, hear his life story, and how he became a drag queen activist for the LGBT community in SA. We’ll follow him on community service projects -- serving bread and soup at a homeless shelter, helping out at after school programs, and working with disabled children through a foundation called Pebbles Project -- all done in full drag. We’ll also see exclusive footage from the most recent pageant he organized -- Miss Drag SA -- and speak to the winner, Zilin Ayoki, who will join Clayton/ Enigma in promoting acceptance and fighting against the prejudice and violence against the LGBT community that are still common in SA.

We shot exclusive footage at the Miss Drag South Africa pageant in Stellenbosch on 8 July 2017 and will be sitting down with the pageant organizer/ main case study, as well as the pageant winner.

title: Policing and new technology
oneLiner: ..how the use of bodycams and tasers can protects both the public and the police
summary:
The world over law reinforcement agencies have turned to the use of body cams and non lethal weapons in a quest to protect both the public and law enforcement officers. They have become indispensable tools in law enforcement. Body cams can record in detail what happens on crime scenes and can be used as evidence. Non-lethal weapons like tasers can save lives and can assist police officers in apprehending violent criminals without endangering themselves. Minister Fikile Mbalula has announced that SAPS will get body cams in the near future, but will it work here?

The use of new technology such as body cams and tasers can make law enforcement more efficient and protect both the police and the public against excesses.

title: NPA Silence
oneLiner: What lies behind the deafening silence of the NPA on rising pressure for the reinstatement of charges against the President?
summary:
We approach constitutional, legal and political analysts to explain the rise and fall of Shaun Abrahams. We will also ask Abrahams himself for an interview on how he sees developments of the last few months since the Gordhan fiasco and calls then for his resignation.

It’s been (another) bad year for the NPA – not only have they had their offices burgled in what seems to be an inside job in recent weeks, but they’ve been roundly trounced for selective prosecutions, turning a blind eye to transgressions at the SABC, SAA and ESKOM, and having to withdraw baseless charges against Pravin Gordhan. Some of the most experienced prosecutors have left and simmering discord has crippled those who must clean up the country. Now the opposition DA has asked the president for NPA boss Shaun Abrahams’ head. Only the president can get rid of his own appointee. But, having defended himself and vowing never to step down after the Gordhan fiasco, Abrahams is deadly silent – and this more than two months after the Supreme Court ruled that the 783 charges against the President should be reinstated.

oneLiner: Dalai lama Exclusive in Botswana
summary: His Holiness the 14th Dalai lama will visit Botswana in August to participate as an honorary guest at a conference which is exploring “Botho/Ubuntu: A dialogue on Spirituality, Science and Humanity”.
