title: Gyrocopter Deaths
summary: Needless and tragic deaths This is a tragic story and an investigation into the death of deaths of 3 young pilots, aged 21, 22, and 23 who died in gyrocopters whilst doing crop spraying. All within a year. Crop spraying is a very dangerous job because of the need for low altitude flying and sharp turns that are required. All pilots had commercial flying licenses but needed extra hours for them to get jobs on commercial airlines. Xsit, a crop spraying company offered them a chance by paying for their training to perform crop spraying. The hours they would achieve would be added to their flying time so they could one day become commercial airline pilots. Previously young pilots were trained at a company called Wagtail, and with no incidents. But Xsit fired the company and turned to a cheaper competitor called Aerotrack. Here they were only given about 20 hours training on gyrocopters, and this was for reactional flying of these machines. CAA requirements made it mandatary that for agricultural flying, there is a minimum of 300 hours required for the dangerous job of crop spraying. All the pilots who had had less than 25 hours training. Xsit knew that they were only trained for recreational flying. After two deaths the CAA wrote to Xsit saying that many compliances were not being followed. Nothing happened it seemed, and an other pilot died later. There also seems proof that Aerotrack did not have a legal AOC (Air operating certificate) to provide training for these pilots. A certificate was issued on 16. 10.2010 which was a Saturday, when the committee only convened 4 days later. Aerotrack ‘s “legal” AOC was a G3 certificate which did not cover agriculture flying. The young men who died did so because they were thrown into work without proper training. And Xsit knew that this was the case. To interview: Deceased Pilots’s families. Gyrocopter pilot. Head of Xsit. Trainer at Aerotrack. CAA

title: Action Time
summary: Carte Blanche meets up with the new Saturation Unit of the Gauteng Traffic police. They have a brand new set of super fast cars and their unit deals with home and factory robberies and hijackings. We met them the other day and were inspired by their dedication and passion. Often the police get a bad rap but here is an opportunity to show case this newly formed unit and spend an evening with them. It will give the public some confidence that there are passionate cops who can and do respond fast to crime, often in high pressure dangerous situations. We have 2 cameramen, on with the head Inspector and the other with Siphiwe Govuzela. As we film we will pick up other interviews as well. But the story will be night with his super fast response team, and action is guaranteed as they chase hijackers or respond to robberies. Action packed. title: Time for Impeachment? - Judge Hlophe
summary: An astonishing judgment by the SCA on Judge president John Hlophe. The Supreme Court of Appeal (SCA) has ruled that Western Cape Judge President John Hlophe may have been biased in a case in which he granted an order in favour of a businessman represented by Hlophe’s own attorney. This is the attorney who has been representing the Judge President in disciplinary proceedings over the allegation that he tried to improperly influence two Constitutional Court justices in a case involving President Jacob Zuma. The JP (Judge President Hlophe) should have recused himself from the matter between MULAUDZI and Old Mutual. Old Mutual by accident paid the business 48 million rand by mistake. Old Mutual tried to get it back and when the businessman refused charges were laid. The JP who was not on duty on the roster set down to hear urgent matters in court that day, allocated the matter to himself and ruled that the business could keep the money. The SCA found that his decision was legally flawed and raised questions about his impartiality. Since coming into office The JP has cut a controversial figure since 2000. There are still disciplinary hearing against him that has been carrying on for 10 years as a result of him trying to improperly influence two Constitutional Court justices in a case involving President Jacob Zuma. Carte Blanche looks at the professional career of the JP, who once called a white attorney a piece of shit We unpack the latest judgment and let viewers decide for himself. We also ask legal minds if this man should be impeached but remind viewers that the ultimate decision is dependent on a vote in parliament! To interview: STILL TO BE DECIDED Retired judge Krieglar Political commentator Legal mind who supports the JP Legal legal looking at the case

title: School Disciplinary Hearings
summary: This is the story of two enterprising UWC law students who are assisting school learners in disciplinary hearings at schools. Many learners are expelled and they were not represented because they could not afford representation or even knew that they were allowed to be represented. The students Yolisa Nocanda and Kwanda Mkalipi felt this as grossly unfair and they formed a student body of 2nd year law students. Is a story of courage as well, these law students having the strength to take on the establishment? Adding to the narrative both the founder students were expelled from their shools, and were unrepresented. title: Medic Alert Dogs
summary:
Jo-Marie recused Bijoux, a poodle, when she was 4 months old and now she is saving her life. Jo-Marie was diagnosed with type one Diabetes at the age of 19 and for the last 16 years she has struggled with the disease. Last year she had so many hypoglycemic episodes that she lost the sight in her left eye and suffered kidney failure. Living with Type 1 Diabetes means that every day is a struggle. Since the age of 2 Bijoux has not left her side and Jo-Marie realized that she could sense when her sugar levels were dropping. Now Bijoux is undergoing training with Lucy Breytenbach a dog trainer who specialises in training medic alert dogs. Bijoux is under-going scent training to alert Jo when her levels are dropping. Jo-Marie tests herself 8 times a day because her condition has become so critical, the average Type 1 Diabetic test 4 times a day. Isabel is a Golden Doodle Poodle and is Sandy’s companion. Sandy is an 11 year old girl with epilepsy. Her mother and school teachers have for years hovered over her but now Isabel is her constant companion and can bring the medication and alert people around her when things are getting out of control. We will spend time with both "case studies" in their homes as well as accompany them to their training sessions with Lucy who will explain the complexity of training these dogs

Dogs have long been known to be in tune with people's feelings and needs and have an exceptional sense of smell. They have been trained to herd sheep, track animals, find drugs and missing people. Now they are being trained to assist people with medical conditions like diabetes and epilepsy. Medic alert dogs have been available in the USA and the UK for many years and South Africans have imported them at great expense, but now there is a training center in Cape Town providing this life saving training. Dogs have an extraordinary sense of smell and can detect changes in blood sugar levels and other bodily changes way ahead of humans. They can be trained to detect minor fluctuates and alert their owner to danger either by pawing them and if they are ignored maybe barking, they will fetch the medication and bring it to the owner. If the owner does not respond or has fallen into a coma they alert their carers or parents. Much like blind dogs these dogs are highly trained and have to adapt to the “person” life style. They have to manage social situations and remain focused on their task at hand and not get distracted. It can take many months of specialised training before the dog and patient are fully independent. The biggest concern of parents of children with diabetes is that they can slip into an episode while at school, socialising or in the middle of the night. Medic alert dogs give the individuals independence and their parent’s peace of mind.

title: AMD CURES
summary:
There are currently three AMD treatment plants in Gauteng: The Western basin plant, run by the government in partnership with Sibanye Gold, the Central basin plant that has been operational for just over 2 years and the newly completed Eastern basin plant. Together, the plants can treat up to 242 megaliters of water a day. The plants have cost R2.3 billion to build and there are additional running costs. But these are only a short-term solution. The treatment plants deliver water with such high salt levels that it is unusable and it must be treated further. For this purpose, the government proposes a R10 billion long-term solution that would treat the saline through either desalination or reverse osmosis. Plants should be in place by 2020, the government has said, but experts question whether such a large-scale infrastructure project would be completed on time and on budget. A further challenge is the sludge left behind when the water is treated at the AMD treatment plants. The sludge contains most of the dangerous materials removed from the AMD water and the sludge is stored in tailings dams or pumped back into the underground voids where the AMD water was pumped from in the first place. Neither solution is sustainable. Pumped back underground, the sludge will continue to contaminate underground water. Tailings dams come with the risk of runoff or leakage from the dams, not to mention the cost involved in ensuring the safety of the dams. Even though experts commend the government's commitment, they question the methods. In a 2016 report, the Harvard Law School International Human Rights Clinic says that the government has failed to live up to many of its human rights obligations, as people and animals are still bathing and washing in contaminated water, drinking it and using it to cook. Chemical engineer John Bewsey has come up with an alternative plan - one he says will produce potable water, leave no sludge behind and generate money.

It's been 15 years since Acid Mine Drainage (AMD), the toxic leftovers of the gold mining industry, first reached the surface on the West Rand. Seven years have passed since warnings that building basements in the Jozi CBD would soon be flooded by AMD. Since then, the government has taken action to address the problem. However, the short-term solution, that consists of three treatment plants that cost more than R2 billion, is creating more problems. It leaves the treated water unusable with high levels of salt. Now, government has come up with a long-term solution to treat the saline water through desalination plants or reverse osmosis, but another R10 billion rand is needed and this solution is still at least three years away. In the meantime, the toxic sludge separated from the water when AMD is treated, is also pumped back into the very same voids it comes from, consistently raising the toxicity level of the contaminated water. Chemical engineer John Bewsey has come up with a process to treat AMD that would treat the water to potable standards and extract products that can be sold for profit. His process has won international prizes but locally, he is battling to get funding to set up a plant beyond the tiny testing plant he has built on the West Rand.

title: Sandmining in the Paardeberg
summary: I think this can be an interesting story with many layers. We then swoop in on the Swartland, the Paardeberg area which is the up and coming wine area of the western cape. Here the vineyards are more low lying, on the slopes and we describe how many overseas wine experts are beginning to make their way here. Wine manufacturers from other areas in the Cape are buying their grapes from this area. But then, from a drone shot, we freeze the camera and show a number of 5 hectare sand mines that could be the future and blight the terrain. One famer says that by granting a mining concession in this area, this could be the future. Beautiful hills which could become a thing of the past, and one farmer in particular says that if he knew that the municipality would allow mines in the area, he would not have spend the last 20 years building his vineyards to t the standard they are. Make no mistake, the western cape is running out of sand. However, the Malmesbury area has some of the finest sand but according to experts, the sand which will be provided from the region (Paardebeg) is really low quality stuff. For filling purposes. No one knows how the one legal sand mine which exists in the area got going several years ago. There seems to have been no public participation. Now 2 permits are about to be granted, with a third in the pipeline.

title: Bromwell Street Evictions

summary: The gentrification of Cape Town and neighboring suburbs such as Salt River and Woodstock are raising deep questions about how slow the city is on making good on its promise to redress apartheid spatial planning. In fact, since 1994, at the dawn of our new democracy, not one affordable housing unit has been built within the CBD district. Whilst land in these districts are being bought and trendified, it is raising an ugly spectre. 40 years ago, with forced removal, families from these areas such as District 6, were forced out to the windy barren landscape of the Cape Flats. Despite Woodtstock being relatively unaffected by forced removals in the past. It is happening to them now. Our drones will travel over Blikkiesdorp, a tin shanty town where 4 years ago, families from another Woodstock area, Gympie Street, were dumped after the properties they were renting were bought from underneath them. It might well be an idea to get a comment one of the people who were dumped at Blikkiesdorp. The proposed site to rehouse residents from Bromwell street who currently have an eviction order, is Wolwerivier. It is 30km outside of the city with some describing it as a concentration camp with no basic services and far away from any schools, shops or hospitals. We have aerial footage of this god forsaken place as well. Here is the rub of the story. A stay of execution is in place and ordered by a judge. The applicants are demanding that they be, in terms of a previous constitutional court ruling, given temporary housing as close as possible to where they live at present. They have identified many areas in the surrounding suburbs owned by the city or provincial government that can be used for affordable temporary housing.

An ex rally driver and a mechanic Heidi and her classic car have travelled 70 000 kms together and now she’s on the pen ultimate journey southern Africa. Heidi Hetzer is a petite little lady, but that belies the fact that she has travelled the world in her vintage car, self reliant and on her own. Her mechanical skills have saved a lot of time and money, managed only five kilometers, but for the border crossing, it was enough. “I don’t want to set any records, I want to see the world, quite simply,” Heidi says but simple it has not been, in Argentina her purse was stolen, In Canada she lost her finger while underneath her car fixing an oil leak. In China, the visa for Hudo – her vintage car- had expired and the border authorities took her for a rebel and they insisted on an official escort while she was driving. Her adventurous have been numerous and zany and fun but when she was diagnosed with cancer in Florida Heidi nearly cancelled her journey but after a visit to the local church she though, she still has time and if it becomes serious it was always to be her last trip so the journey continues. Hudo and her have become inseparable well Heidi has become inseparable from her car and was very concerned while Hudo was alone on the cargo ship coming out here. Whatever town or country the pair are in classic car enthusiasts come out in full force, support in any way they can. Asking Heidi if this is a dream come true she says “Nonsense, I never had such a dream I have worked all my life, I had absolutely no time for dreams I am spontaneous..”

title: Xolobeni Mine

summary: The Australian company MRC (Mineral Commodities) started prospecting the dunes of Xolobeni on the Wild Coast in 2002 and discovered what they said would be the largest titanium mine in South Africa. Form the start, the proposed mine has met fierce resistance from the local community, who formed the Amadiba Crisis Committee in 2007. Now, the chairman of the Crisis Committee has been killed after he had said he feared for his life after MRC submitted a renewed mining right application to the Department of Mineral Resources and tensions escalated as the Crisis Committee reported incidents of intimidation. The Crisis Committee and Sikhosiphi ‘Bazooka’ Rhadebe have been speaking out about the devastation that the mine would bring to their ancestral land. We investigate the forces of big international capital and state patronage, as well as poverty and the need to development, that have been pulling this royal and ancient community apart for over a decade and we recap the legal cases that they have fought painstakingly in the courts, with the assistance of the Legal Resources Centre.

title: Iranian Women's Rugby
oneLiner: It's the last sport you would expect to see Iranian women interested in playing but these women have overcome vehement opposition with courage and grace
summary: The story of women'​s rugby in Iran has been truly inspiring in recent years. The players have won international games and been placed among the top ten of the Asian championships. The women who play the game challenge stereotypes - not only because they are women playing rugby but also because they wear full body covering that me​ets the religious rules demanded by their country's leadership. Their first male coach was in the beginning barred from going within 10 meters of his team, then threatened with prosecution for prostitution, and finally banned from working with the team. More recently, the players have been forced to practice almost entirely indoors, only to be allowed outdoors when no men can see them. We explore the challenges they face by speaking with a few of the players and their families. This is a story of survival against the odds of the least likely sport you would expect to see Iranian women interested in playing. We look at their courage in the face of vehement opposition – the suffering they must deal with on a personal level at home and in their communities, and to what extent they have achieved international success .

title: The Big Fat Pet Vaccine Debate
oneLiner: So we get one jab and it lasts a lifetime but our pets have multiple jabs - what's the truth and why are some animals dying despite them?
summary: We ask why do vaccines fail and why do some animals die from annual injections? Sandra Gerber has first hand experience - she had 2 Borzoi pups die from Parvo virus withing 36 hours of their 3rd innoculation. They should have been protected. It cost her nearly 10k at Onderstepoort to save the 3rd pup. Merck paid the bills without asking questions. Sanette Gray has watched in horror as her toy pom pups died one after the other following their vaccination. The vets were unable to save them.She still has several at the vet on drips. Petro Moore lost two litters of Yorkies after their inoculations. Herman Welgemoed lost 14 Toy poms due to vaccination reactions. And stil big pharma says its isolated. Every day there are reports on social media of more and more of these events. And the research on our vaccine protocols suggest we are over vaccinating and harming our dogs. Here's some excerpts from peer reviewed docs. Dr Jodie Gruenstern DVM CVA, practicing vet from Winconsin, points out that maternal antibodies will actually block the effectiveness of vaccine when administered at young age (six weeks).nd according to veterinary vaccine researcher Dr Jean Dodds, only 30% of puppies will be protected from a vaccine given at 6 weeks of age: yet 100% of them will be exposed to disease when taken to the vet clinic for that shot. Moreover, vaccines create immune suppression for 10 to 14 days. So, choosing to vaccinate a puppy at 6 weeks means exposing him to the most disease ridden location he could possibly be in – the vet clinic – while creating immune suppression at the same time. Your puppy is much more likely to get the disease he is being vaccinating for, and all in exchange for a 30% chance the vaccine will work. That’s a pretty high gamble with a puppy’s life.

title: Fees must Fall
summary: Across the country University Students are protesting the 10% increase in University Tuition fees. Wits University students were the first to come out preventing staff and students from attending lectures and eventually preventing staff from leaving the campus. On Monday Rhodes University, and Stellenbosch joined WITS and UCT. By the end of Tuesday campuses across the country had come out including Tuks, and CUPT. Today Universities across the country have come to a standstill. Students have been protesting the increase of fees for several years now but this is the first time they have all come out at the same time across the country. State and Private funding of Universities has been decreasing over the years and poor Students and their parents are taking the brunt of the financial stress. Many students are not poor enough to get state subsidies and their parents take out loans and bursaries to pay for their fees but there is little left for living cost, transport and food making the student’s lives extremely stressful. Students are graduating with massive loans to repay. Others who have qualified and got a degree don’t get their certificate because the university withholds the awarding of a degree until fees are paid up. This insert will focus on these students and their stories with the backdrop of the last weeks drama of students and University administrations coming head to head.

title: Taxi's behaving badly

summary: It's estimated that over 1000 deaths are recorded on South African roads every month and "the popular belief is that taxi drivers’ behaviour – their aggressive driving and disdain for the rules – provides an intuitive and logical explanation for why South Africa’s roads are so dangerous." In September this year, Carte Blanche put out a social media call out to our viewers for pictures and footage of 'taxi's behaving badly'. We received a massive response with a reach of between 400 000 and 500 000 viewers either commenting on their experiences with taxi's on the road as well as hundreds of pictures and videos of the various incidents'. At face value, many of the videos and pictures that we were sent, confirm this belief. Statistics too from 2014, also confirm that taxis "account for three times more fatalities than cars". We're just weeks away from the notorious December festive season, where traffic accidents are always high and the loss of life because of them, staggering. This week, Carte Blanche takes the taxi industry to task and finds out who's responsible to put an end to the carnage and lawlessness caused by taxi drivers on our roads.

title: Fishermen threatened in the Western Cape
oneLiner: Is Voervoed alive an well in the Fishing Industry
summary: The Department of Fisheries has placed a motion before parliament to change the fishing quotas so that they are issued according to South Africa’s national racial demographics. This would result in 75,2% of the fishing quotas going to African people, 10,6% to Coloured and 10,8 to whites and 3,1% to Indians. But the fishing industry, both commercial and subsistence is mostly concentrated in the Western Cape, with much smaller industries in the Northern Cape, Eastern Cape and KwaZulu Natal. Over 95% of the trawling industry is Western Cape based, and is largely done by coloured and white fishermen, there are very very few African fishermen. The Western Cape’s racial demographics are dramatically different to the national demographic – 52.4% coloured, 16% white, 31,2% African and 0,3% Indian.

title: From Prison to Programming
oneLiner: A progressive new initiative that teaches prisoners how to programme skills Silicon Valley cannot get enough of.
summary: “Brothers for All” is a non-profit initiative, which provides technology and entrepreneurship opportunities to offenders, ex-offenders and township youth. The opportunities they offer in this growing field competes with crime, in coolness and earning potential. Last year they launched a coding centre in Langa, this year they brought coding into Worcester female and male correctional services. Co- Founder of the project is Sihle Tshabala an ex armed robber, ex in mate who spent 11 years behind bars, part of the notorious 26 gang. The success of this project to people who come from poverty, crime and desperation surprised co-founder Linda Scott: Given their backgrounds, I am often surprised by how quickly and competently they learn to code. My co-founder, Sihle Tshabalala, an ex-armed robber, is never surprised. "People in the townships have lost their dignity Ex-offenders know the struggles that take their dignity. So we can give it back. We can give hope." Linda: We planned to find work for our students. Work found us. Small township businesses and NGOs quickly began approaching us, asking our motley bunch of students to build them websites. But Sihle once again is not surprised: "Many black people in South Africa think technology is just for rich white people," he says pithily, while I wince. "They don't think they can go online."

title: Tumeric , the spice that cures Parkinsons disease ?

summary: Its been known in India for thousands of years that the powder from the white flowered plant Curcuma Longa , which produces tumeric and curcumin , could heal skin wounds and burns .Now young Celia Van Der Merwe at University of Stellenbosch has found that curcumin , has anti inflammatory properties and can renew brain cells associated with Parkinsons Disease and Alzheimers .Carte Blanche can interview Celia Van Der Merwe at the University and Professor Bardien Kruger and show their work in the laboratory with human brain cells that have been exposed to curcumin .We show graphics of human brain cells and mitochrondia which have been renewed after exposure to Curcumin .In their interviews they state that studies have found that India has less Parkinsons and Alzheimers compared to South Africa and the UK .Via a use of graphics and interviews with Celia and Soraya we show signal pathways in the human brain cells change with Corcomin .We talk to other researchers , who show Indian brain samples have fewer dead brain cells than samples from the UK . We will try and talk Mary Ganguli at the University of Pittsburgh on skype , as she found in two separate sample groups of 564 and 970 people , of Indian men and women , aged 70 to 79 , had four times lower frequency of Alzehimers , compared to Americans . At Stellenbosch they created a disease in a dish to study Parkinsons . The cells were improved at a molecular level .It seems curcumin stops brain cell death as it is a powerful anti oxidant , that decreases the toxic substances via increased mitochondrial respiration . Curcumin also impacts on inflammed parts of the body .We enlarge the shots we see from under the microscope .We interview Dr Craige Golding from his medical practise in Houghton . He prescribes Curcumin every day via tablets , combined with peppers for good absorption .He says , with many other doctors, its a powerful cancer protection too . He has case studies who have healed.

title: How social media can have you hired or fired.
oneLiner: Your social media presence can determine whether you are hired or fired. SHOULD YOUR SOCIAL MEDIA PRESENCE INFLUENCE WHETHER YOU ARE HIRED OR FIRED?
summary: If you apply for a job, you will be googled. Your online behaviour can and will probably determine whether you are hired or fired. You may not realise that these days everyone is subject to a social media audit as part of the interview process. And what you have on your Facebook, Twitter, Instagram pages can directly impact on your eligibility when it comes to employment. Just as what you post on social media can result in the termination of your work contract. Gone are the days when what you do in your private time, is your own business. Through social media big brother is now constantly watching you and what you post and what you say needs to be censored. What it all comes down to is reputation management - and it's not just your own you need to consider.. According to common law, should you bring your reemployed into disrepute you can be fired.. And more than that, your contract with your employer is to act in good faith and in the best interests of the company, if your social media posts contravene this understanding it could cost you your job. If an employee writes anything vaguely negative about their employer, including saying something as anodyne as ‘I had a bad day at work’, bosses are well within their legal rights, to sack the staff member. Around the world, palace guards, cops and teachers (among many others) have all lost their jobs because of why they have posted on social media. Recruitment agents today are even advising job seekers on how to portray themselves on social media and that you should have an online presence.

title: Honey Bees are Sick of Humans
oneLiner: Ticking time bomb - Dreaded Bee desease American Foulbrood threatens South Africa's 20 Billion Agricultural Industry
summary: In a worrying development which could threaten food production, South Africa's traditionally tough honey bees - which had been resistant to disease - are now getting “sick of humans”, with the population of the crucial pollinators collapsing. It is important to note that 70 out of the top 100 human food crops, which supply about 90 percent of the world's nutrition, are pollinated by bees. The foulbrood hitting South Africa is the American strain of the disease, The country's bees have previously coped with the European version. Since its discovery in 2009 here in South Africa, some Bee farmers have lost up to 60 % of their operations as hives die off. Foulbrood attacks the bee larvae, leading to the collapse of the colony. It is spread when bees raid the dead colony, bringing back spore-infected honey to their colony, or by the importation of contaminated bee products. While North America and Europe have battled foulbrood for centuries, South Africa's bees have stayed healthy - a resilience attributed to the country's diverse bee population, which has naturally fought off disease and pests in the past, as well as strict regulations that require any imported bee products to be irradiated. Yet today the hardy South African bees are under siege. Foulbrood has spread massively, it has now spread over a 500 by 400-kilometre area where most beekeeping operations are infected in the Western Cape. The stakes are very high, the biggest Challenge is not just the honey products that are likely to be affected but rather the R20 Billion commercial agriculture industry that requires bee pollination. The story will take a look at the what has been termed a Ticking time bomb Foulbrood disease and its impact on the Agricultural industry.

summary: We have an exclusive TV interview with Emmanuel de Merode on Friday. 44-year-old Emmanuel de Merode is an interesting character – he is a Belgian prince who was raised in Kenya and educated at Durham University before devoting himself to conservation in Africa. He was appointed Virunga’s director in 2008. His task was to rebuild Africa’s oldest national park, a white man who heads up an all-black team of rangers. He has turned its corrupt, demoralised rangers into a disciplined, well-armed force. He refused to abandon the Rumangabo compound when it was stormed in 2012 by M23, the latest rebel group to terrorise the region, and has lived in a tent there for the past six years while his wife and two young daughters remain in Nairobi. The rangers’ struggle is to balance the needs of the extremely poor population that lives in and around the park and the survival of the biodiversity and the animals. Soco is doing undercover deals with the rebel armies that desperately need money to further their cause. The head ranger was offered a bribe to persuade Emmanuel to let Soco into the park. In April 2014 Emmanuel was shot after returning from Goma where he delivered a report on Soco’s activities, and he is seen by many as the ain obstacle to Soco getting access to the park. He refuses to speculate on who tried to kill him, but his efforts to save Virunga have made him plenty of enemies: the dozen rebel groups still inhabiting the park; the poachers who have killed thousands of its elephants and hippopotami; powerful figures who have illegally annexed park land; and those who cut down its forests for charcoal, a huge industry in a land with little electricity.

BUT, THE VISION THAT PEOPLE ARE BEING SOLD IS NOT WHAT THEY ARE ACTUALLY BUYING INTO. Chances are the attacks could die down completely, but it would still be worth doing a bigger picture piece as the story would still have relevance. What has the impact been on South Africa internationally and on the home front. We look at social perceptions, global economic impact and the effect of media and social networking platforms on these xenophobic attacks. How much weight does President Zuma's comment about South Africa having a violence of history carry? Are these isolated incidents, or just the tip of under reported xenophobic iceberg?

title: The ISIS lure
oneLiner: Are young South African girls being lured to join ISIS with false promises? And we ask is this part of a growing global trend?
summary: This week it was revealed that a 15 year old South African girl narrowly escaped ISIS recruitment. She's not alone. A young PE girl was also caught by her family at OR Tambo on route to Syria via Turkey. Another young Bela Bela girl is allegedly already there along with 2 PE families who left lock stock and barrel. The Iraqi ambassador in SA is on the record stating that around 140 South African's have joined ISIS. We speak to a family member of one of the PE families, the lawyer and spokeswoman for the young PE girl and to Yusuf Abramjee who helped to locate and rescue the Cape Town girl. Then, with the help of a 19 year old Muslim girl, we explore the platforms and the recruitment process that lures young girls making it appear like they will be joining the ultimate liberated utopia. Social media platforms are used to do this - she will create a fake profile and then share the propaganda that is used to lure her. We are also able to access 20 videos that ISIS released - all these videos have been subjected to rigorous video analysis by the Florida based TRAC team. Bigger picture: we will speak to leading Muslim thinkers and clerics about the level of support for ISIS within SA within the context of who ISIS is and who they purport to represent. There was an article in today's Times alleging that Muslim clerics were being threatened for speaking out against the Islamic state terrorist organisation.

Around the world there is a growing trend with Muslims leaving their homes to join extremist groups, not only as fighters but as support staff, as administrators, medical assistants and in a range of other roles. All in the name of securing the much talked about and revered caliphate.

title: MALE RAPE - It's real
oneLiner: When a man is forced to have sex by a woman, is it rape?
summary: That's the question many uninformed South African's ask when they hear about a woman raping a man. We explore this phenomenon which, although rare, does occur. In fact, an American study (Center for Disease Control’s national survey on sexual violence) more than 5 million men in the United States have been “made to penetrate” someone else in their lifetime, whether by coercion, intimidation, or because they were incapacitated. In South Africa, according to SAMSOSA (South African male survivors of Sexual Abuse) in 2011 19.4% of rapes that occurred had male victims. It is less the one percent of females who are the perpetrators suggesting that this is a rare phenomenon. This year alone, a 46-year old Woman was arrested and charged with Rape in Limpopo after coercing a 26-year old into her home, locking him in her bedroom and then forcing him to have sex with her for hours. He was taken to hospital after the ordeal, because his genitals were so swollen. The case is on-going. In another incident, also this year and with previous cases, in Tembisa a man alleges he was hitchhiking and 3 women pulled over and offered him a lift. They offered him a drink (laced with drugs), and then when they suggested he pay them for the ride, and he said he could not, they then tied him up and forced him to have sex with each of them. He went to the police station, and was laughed at.

After more information emerged, the state asked to re-open its case, but the application was dismissed by Judge Bam. They are flying over the Standfontein area, a notorious place in Cape Town where Copper thieves burn the plastic off copper cable under the cover of darkness before they take it to scrape dealers. There are numerous uses for drones but currently the City has to apply for special permission from the Civil Aviation Authority to use them.

title: Bloemfontein Brothels
oneLiner: Recently a brothel in Bloemfontein with young sex workers was bust open by the Hawks
summary: The discovery of a brothel in central Bloemfontein with seven young women earlier in the year has led to the realisation that there might be a proliferation of brothels, victims of trafficking and under age sex workers in the city . The police and the authorities agree . With the help of the social workers the police and key NGO's , and the young women themselves, Carte Blanche looks at a problem that is growing in South Africa .Children and young adults are brought into South Africa from Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Ghana and other African countries .The pimps apparently have apps with catalogues of the trafficked people for the sex clients , who include truck drivers and older men . Grizelda Grootboom, a survivor of human/child-trafficking who is based in Cape Town is open to relate her ordeal on camera, Grizelda works for an NGO that assists victims of human-trafficking called "Embrace Dignity" . She will film undercover for us in both Bloemfontein and in Yeoville , Johannesburg at the spots where children are trafficked , and we will get footage at the hot spots where the young people , the traffickers and the sex clients are . Luvuyo Mfaku, NPA National Coordinator has agreed to assist us in this story.It has grown to become the story of trafficking in Bloemfontein , Cape Town and Johannesburg .We are getting assistance from Elbie Conradie in the Free State , Margaret Stafford from the Salvation Army and Luvuyo Mfaku from the National Prosecuting Authority.We will get information on the number of prosecutions that have occurred this year and the stats relating to people and children trafficked internally in the country and people trafficked out of the country .

title: Lammergeriers on the verge of extinction
oneLiner: Lammergeries are more endangered tan the Rhino
summary: Bearded vultures, or lammergeiers, are one of the world’s most critically endangered bird species, and in South Africa are now restricted to the Drakensberg. In the past 50 years, there nesting sites have been reduced by almost half. Just how critically endangered they are was starkly highlighted when – as part of her research for her doctorate – Dr Sonja Krüger of Ezemvelo-KZN Wildlife, attached tracking devices to 21 of the vultures. In the seven year study she conducted under the supervision of Dr Arjun Amar, of UCT’s Percy FitzPatrick Institute of African Ornithology, 10 of the 21 study vultures were killed, nine by poisoning, and one be flying into a power line.

The “loan” was part of the Arms Deal offset arrangements, after Ferrostaal landed the R5.2-billion deal to build three submarines. A recent fact-finding mission to the estates led by DA Eastern Cape leader, Athol Trollip, and DA national agriculture spokesperson, Annette Steyn MP, found the harvest unpicked, un-tended, and the workers standing idle, with many of them having not been paid. Trollip, a fluent isi-Xhosa speaker, is prepared to return to the estates with Carte Blanche and give our team a guided tour.

In 2013, 2 000 people from across the globe initially applied to go to the red planet, a voyage scheduled to take place in 2018. The candidates come from all around the world, namely 39 from the Americas, 31 from Europe, 16 from Asia, 7 from Africa, and 7 from Oceania. title: Getmeto21
oneLiner: Jenna Lowe was dying, with little chance of an organ transplant for herself she made a decision to at least save others with her Getmeto21 campaign
summary: Get Me to 21 Jenna Lowe turns 21 in October this year, a few months ago the chances of her ever reaching that age would be something short of a miracle as of this week this has become a very real possibility. This is a story about a young, dynamic girl who four years ago was diagnosed with a rare condition called Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension which simply put is the build up of high blood pressure in the lungs, caused by the narrowing of the arteries. Potentially fatal, PAH can be treated if it is caught early enough. “They thought at first it was asthma, so I was on the wrong treatment for a long time,” Jenna Jenna and her family tried everything to treat this illness and Jenna was determined to live whatever life she had to the maximum energy…the breathing machine that she was permanently attached to didn’t stop her, she became head girl, went to her matric dance ( with tubes and machine ). Gabi, her mother, gave up working as it became apparent that not only was Jenna needing more and more care but she need to direct her energies to literally saving her daughters life. Fundraising was part of it and the whole family worked at it, Jenna’s younger Kristi teamed up with Good Luck to sing a song Jenna wrote: “ I need more Time”. Towards the end of last year time was running out, as the medication was not working( mainly due to fact she had started to late) Jenna needed a lung transplant but her chances were really low as only 0.4% ( last years stats) of South African’s donate their organs and if they do lungs are not highest on the list.

summary: In 2011, businesses operating from Virginia Airport got the shocking news that their 10year leases (which they had just signed), had been rescinded and that the municipality had made the decision to move the airport from the prime piece of beachfront property it currently occupies. The city say they have earmarked an airstrip in Scottburgh as its new home. And if comments made by city manager Sbu Sithole are to be believed, it’s a done deal. But a call to the family who owns the site in Scottburgh paints a different picture. They say they have never been contacted by eThekweni Municipality. title: Central methodist church evictions
oneLiner: In 2008 the central methodist church opened its doors to immigrants following xenophobic attacks. Six years later the church is evicting hundreds of desperate refugees.
summary: In 2008 Bishop Paul Verryn opened the doors of the central methodist church to immigrants who needed shelter following the xenophobic attacks in the JHB area. At the end of 2014, after Verryn left the church, the church evicted all of the refugees who had been left there. They have nowhere to go and have been stranded. Paul Verryn is fighting the evictions claiming it is unconstitutional and desperately trying to source alternative housing for the people concerned. But there are over 500 people who need homes. They are desperate. Human rights activist Walter Sefiri has vowed to fight the evictions on the grounds that they are unconstitutional.

title: 3800 KM through SA on a tuk-tuk

summary: Seven 2014 Matriculants, from three different schools in JHB, set off on a journey that has never been done before in SA. Starting in JHB and ending in CPT they are covering a distance of 3800 KM by tuk-tuks. On 11 January they are due to arrive in Cape Town, which will mark the end of their journey. SO far, they are on track. They set out to raise R 200 000 whilst on the road for a charity in Boksburg called St Vincents, Johannesburg that provides a hospice service for adults and a home for abandoned children. Their entire journey has been documented by their own camera man. (NB - it is on 7 D) We can arrange access to this footage. Proposed story elements: Their arrival in CPT. An in depth interview on the experience and journey. With footage from them. Millennials have been accused of being apathetic, these guys turn that notion on its head. Speak to a sociologist / psychologist about the youth of SA and getting involved in making a difference. the charity - the work they do. This is not a 10'00.

title: CRIME "APP"VANTAGE
oneLiner: A community in Durban is using an ingenious cell phone app, designed by a South African NASA scientist, to bring down the crooks and save lives.
summary: Fed up with escalating crime and a court system seemingly rigged to let the crooks walk free, an enterprising group of dedicated crime busters in the upper highway area in Durban is using the latest technology to beat the crooks. And they are doing it with the help of former NASA engineer, South African Larry Hurwitz. Larry, designer of the space shuttle’s dashboard, who has donated his “revolutionary” emergency response App driven technology to SA CAN. (Larry lives in Dallas, but is in SA for the next two weeks.) Larry has already sold his My911 app to over 75 countries. But donated it free to SA CAN in the hopes it could save lives here. 3 Years ago his brother-in-law died after being stabbed and he says his live may have been saved if he’d had access to the App. His brother-in-law had lain injured, but undiscovered for more than a day, before succumbing to his wounds. SA Can (South Africa Community Action Network) started as a community call centre hotline in 2002, manned by volunteer police reservists and members of the community. They worked out of a prefab office in the Kloof police station parking lot. The system tracks users to within 6 meters of their location and can send back images and audio files to the SA CAN center which help police catch the crooks and rescue victims.

IT SEEMS TO BE HIS MODUS OPERANDI AS HE CONS WOMAN INTO GIVING HIM THEIR HEARTS AND ALL OF THEIR MONEY BEFORE KICKING THEM OUT WITH LITTLE TO NOTHING LEFT. FOUR WOMEN HAVE COME FORWARD AND TOLD THEIR TRAGIC STORIES OF HEART ACHE, DEBT, DECEIT AND ABUSE. THEY HAVE COME TOGETHER TO TRY AND PROTECT OTHER WOMEN FROM BEING TRAPPED IN GUSTAV’S WEB OF LIES.

title: Holocaust - 70th Anniversary of the liberation of Auschwitz
oneLiner: 1.1 million people were murdered in this Nazi camp, we speak to some of the people who escaped death ...70 years on
summary: Liberation of Auschwitz – 70 years anniversary On the 27th January 2015 is the 70th year anniversary of the liberation of Auschwitz. 100 survivors of the German Nazi Concentration and Extermination camp have been invited to attend the memorial. The event will take place in Poland at The Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum and will be commemorated by the world. “January 27, 2015 will be a truly exceptional day,” says Piotr M.A. Cywiński, director of the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum. “On this day of remembrance, the whole world will focus on the tragedy of the Shoah and the entire cruel system of ghettos and concentration camps. The survivors will be our most important guests.” And 4 of the survivors invited come from South Africa. I propose an insert that would flight the Sunday before or after to commemorate this day. We profile two survivors and what they went through against the background of Auschwitz. The two I have chosen are feisty and very strong characters. We also interview the Historian at the Holocaust museum, who is riveting, and who will piece the story together; “Auschwitz is not only the world’s biggest Jewish graveyard, it is also the primary symbol of the Holocaust, the biggest organized mass murder in human history. An estimated 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered in Auschwitz, in German-occupied Poland, between 1941 and 1945. Here are two peoples stories who survived:

title: #joyburg
oneLiner: No they are not crazy, this is what laugh activist Sue Jameson believes is the transforming power of Joy
summary: # Joy Burg Sue Jameson is a laughter coach, a joy activist she calls herself. She lives her life by this quote from Mark Twain. "The human race has one really effective weapon, and that is laughter. Against the assault of laughter, nothing can stand." When she read that South Africa was voted By Conde Nast Travel magazine as the unfriendliest city in the world… what could she do but take action in the best way she knew how…laughter.

title: Parliament - Fount of democracy or laughing stock
oneLiner: Parliament - Fount of democracy or laughing stock
summary: Parliament : fount of democracy or laughing stock? As Parliament’s 2014 session draws to a close do we laugh or do we cry? Thursday evening’s drama in the House of Assembly was the climax to six months tense confrontation between the ANC and opposition parties. The Speaker, Baleka Mbete, cynically tried to change the rules and override an agreement reached on the programme in the Chief Whips’ Forum that morning. She and the ANC Chief Whip crossed swords. Mbete withdrew ignominiously, perhaps fatally weakening her authority in the House. In the final debate of the day EFF MP Mashebela refused to leave the podium when ordered to do so by House chair Cedric Frolick. Mashabela had called President Zuma a "thief" during a debate on the Grand Inga Hydro Project, and refused to withdraw her remarks. Mashabela would not be moved when sergeant-at-arms Regina Mohlomi tried to escort her from the podium. The House descends into chaos. Members of the police’s public order unit stormed into the National Assembly chamber allegedly to restore order. Fists started flying when police pushed and shoved MPs from the Democratic Alliance and the EFF who intervened. …they were forcibly removed by Members who refuse to be intimidated. Members are assaulted. The officers were told they had no jurisdiction over the National Assembly chamber. It remains unclear on whose instructions the police were acting. What does that portend for the future of our democracy? An in-depth insert on this year in parliament, analyzing where to now and what that means for us.

title: Thijs's Story
oneLiner: Court papers spanning more than a decade, a damning Public Protector's report and several laws ignored in the beauricratic nit-picking of one department to deny one man his right to SA citizenship.
summary: Court papers spanning more than a decade, a damning Public Protector's report and several laws ignored in the bureaucratic nit-picking of one department to deny one man his right to SA citizenship. It's been almost two decades since Thijs van Hillegondsberg and his wife arrived in South Africa from Holland. They wanted to immigrate to the country of milk and honey to come and make a difference. Thijs first visited SA in 1983 as a MBA-student and fell in love with the country, deciding he would move here immediately after Apartheid ended. So, in 1996, he and wife, Pamela Poelman and Thijs's first-born biological son, Ludo arrived in the country. They were excited and in the same year applied for citizenship - but this was only the start of a lengthy process that would cost Thijs hundreds of thousands of rands, have him arrested several times, investigated by the government, being served with a deportation order and having to fight it in court with urgent applications and even going to the Public Protector and Thuli Madonsela in 2012 releasing a report stating that Thijs and his family had been victims of the Home Affairs maladministration and abuse of power.

title: Oliver's Odyssey
oneLiner: Oliver Sinclair is an MS sufferer and hero. He’s also the first South African to be accepted for new stem cell trials in India.
summary: Oliver’s story Oliver: “Standing on the start line at the Big Walk, a lady sternly said to me; “Should you be doing this walk? Have you spoken to your Doctor? You mustn’t walk, you are going to do damage to yourself.” I smiled and said, “Who knows if I will ever get an opportunity to walk with my family and friends again. I can’t sit at home waiting to eventually not be able to walk…” She muttered something as I turned away. In 2004 (29 years old) Oliver went for an MRI scan because the right hand side of his face was numb. 2 weeks later he had another attack and this time he lost his speech, developed double-vision and lost the function of his body from my waist down. After numerous tests, MRI scans and a lumbar puncture he was diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis. NB: I have archival footage of Oliver tracking Leopard when he was a ranger. We also have footage of him competing in various sporting events. The last was in an adapted wheelchair which he did the AmaShovashova PMB-DBN bicycle race. So we have a visual history of what this disease has done to him.

title: Afro Prep
oneLiner: What is Afro Prep and whose wearing it, a downtown Joburg trend thats gaining serious ground
summary: Afro Prep Where Park Ave meets the Motherland Afro Prep the new cool is hot in SA and its in downtown Joburg that this is burgeoning. We take walk and investigate the trend of Afro Prep and the people who wear it, curate it and sell it. Like, Andile Cele who could be South Africa's budding Ralph Lauren? Andile is one of the new breed of young entrepreneurs who are tapping into South Africa's cultural zietgeist which is challenging accepted ways of doing things whilst combining the best of the old and the new. They identify a market niche and create a brand that speaks to that market. This is essentially a light irreverent piece, very visual, very fast paced, filmed on the street, on the move. The Afro- prep feel alongside some of the oldest parts of Johannesburg will be an ideal contrast.

title: ROLLER DERBY - BLOOD, SWEAT & MASCARA
oneLiner: female accountants and lawyers like you've never seen them before.... clad in fishnets and face paint meet South Africa's National Roller Derby Team!
summary: Team ZA is heading to the Roller Derby World Cup in Dallas this December - representing South Africa for the first time. It’s fast and can be brutal at times. You might be fooled, but despite the skimpy and sexy outfits - this all-girl-sport is about the game - a full-contact women’s sport played on quad roller skates. From the Raging Warmones to the Storm Riders - these women are athletes with attitude! title: TRUCK CHECK
oneLiner: just how safe are we on our road - we see first hand just how many trucks pass basic roadworthy rules.
summary: TRUCKS ARE DEATH TRAPS! Just last month the Alberton claimed four lives, injured 28 and damaged 50 cars! Earlier in October 12 people died when a truck collided with a taxi in Mpumalanga. Last year, the Pinetown Crash claimed 23 lives. It all comes down to two elements - driver competency and truck roadworthiness. This year, we have the opportunity to exclusively go out on a Truck Check operation with transport industry roleplayers putting trucks to the test on the spot. 67% of trucks pulled off have been found to be unroadworthy! A scary statistic with the festive season traffic and resultant death toll upon us. IT's A GREAT OPPORTUNITY TO SHOW THAT WE KEEP AN EYE ON STORIES HAVING DONE WEAPON ON WHEELS AROUND THE PINETOWN CRASH - THIS IS A GREAT SCENARIO TO REVISIT THE TOPIC FOLLOWING THE ALBERTON CRASH AND BUILD UP TO THE FESTIVE SEASON.

Lucky for music lovers Alice Phoebe Lou isn’t the type of girl to conform to pre-set ideas. Her determination to stay pure to her art and her refusal to be locked into deals with music’s big guns has struck a chord with fellow musicians and fans.

title: ACCIDENT STAGING: THE ULTIMATE CON
oneLiner: we expose a syndicate that fakes accidents to scam insurance companies out of hundreds of thousands of rands!
summary: It really is an ingenious scam! STEP 1: You buy a scrap car STEP 2: You get a "roadworthy" certificate despite NOT fixing the car STEP 3: You insure the car and get it "assessed" - for an extra R500 your piece scrap passes all the insurance checks STEP 4: Then, after a few months of paying insurance premiums you have an "accident" and claim from the insurance company. THE CON? The car was never fixed, the insurance companies have just paid out twice for the same wreck! Using insiders and undercover stings, we expose a family run syndicate that's been ripping off insurance companies for years!

oneLiner: a 9 week postal strike crippling the country.
summary: We have been inundated by complaints from our viewers. This story has been largely under reported in the media. It feels like Snail-Mail has gone into reverse! The strike has been going on for 9 weeks impacting on businesses and individuals waiting for chronic medication deliveries to tertiary study materials. The chaos prevails with strikers demanding permanent employment, but the Postal Service says they just don't have the money. And the reality is they don't - the second CEO in two years has just been put on extended leave following a trial of corruption and mismanagement. Non-strikers have been targeted, being physically beaten and humiliated by their striking colleagues. (I have video evidence)

Municipalities are trying to be inventive with solutions, but experts say they are throwing good money after bad and that humans are to blame. It seems as though it's generally gotten worse over the last two years. As we move into the summer months - the rat infestation is bound to gain momentum. Surely there should be long term solutions?

title: COPS TURN ROBBERS
oneLiner: Cop fighting crime with more crime - we expose a gang of cops stealing hundreds of thousands of rands from the criminals they bust.
summary: Money Laundering is a criminal offence. It doesn't happen in fancy offices, but in back rooms at the China Mall in Bruma. At least 38 shops run by Chinese and Pakistani nationals offer a money exchange service behind a dodgy store front. A gang of cops lead by one Lieutenant-Colonel has bust 16 different illegal operations - yet all the money they confiscate from the foreign nationals doesn't get declared - it gets pocketed by the dodgy cops.

title: Toxic Trolley (Consumer Investigation)
oneLiner: Is your trolley toxic? Ongoing research says it could be. Traditionally staple foods and even items touted as healthy could be causing an increase in cancer cases.
summary: South African researchers are world leaders when it comes to the study of mycotoxins (from Greek μύκης (mykes, mukos) "fungus" and τοξικόν (toxikon) ". Basically it’s the study of cancer causing toxins produced by fungus on food. What foods? Nuts – all of them, muesli, maize, sorghum... basically anything that gets ground up. AND that is stored / dried before being processed. HOW SERIOUS IS THE PROBLEM? According to toxicologist Dr Sindeep Bhana, Northern KZN, and Mozambique score highest in the world when it comes to throat cancer. Why? Because nuts are the primary source of protein amongst poor people. Oral and stomach cancers in the Transkei are also clocking in as a world high because the people there purposely grow these deadly fungi – which they add to local beers to help the sorghum ferment.

title: Surf's up in the Shacklands (Feel Good 8Min)
oneLiner: Teenagers are finding a refuge from gangland violence by taking to their surf boards. 250 are being taught how to surf by Waves for Change, who use the sport to reach youngsters’ suffering from trau
summary: Not many teenagers would feel safer in a shark-infested sea than in their own neighbourhood, but Luxolo Ponco does. His home is in Khayelitsha, were gangland violence is an everyday occurrence. Bbut he has found refuge, a short walk down a dusty road and over the dunes, at Monwabisi beach. "When the gangs fight I come here to surf and I feel safe," he says. Safety is relative. He says recently a surfer was attacked by a Great White shark just a few kilometres down the beach. And in June, a fisherman was shot dead by robbers before dawn on the same stretch of coastline. But Luxolo, 17, is one of about 250 youths from Khayelitsha who have found a new perspective on life with Waves for Change, an NGO founded by British surfer Tim Conibear. Even with a cold wind blowing during winter, children aged from seven upwards gathered cheerfully in a scruffy compound housing an old container full of surfboards and wetsuits. The compound is surrounded by concrete walls topped with razor wire, but the contrast between their surroundings in Khayelitsha and the nearby beach is stark.

title: Transforming the face of the SA rugby
oneLiner: we explore the transformation debate of the Springbok Rugby team
summary: The South African Rugby Union (SARU) has confirmed its plans to ensure that half the Springbok team is made up of players of colour by 2019. SARU's Transformation Strategic Plan, aims to bring all of South Africa's representative rugby teams, along with domestic teams in line with national targets in five years. But the question is whether South Africa has enough good black players to play for the country. Currently in the Rugby Championship, 19% of the players are non-white, while only 12% are black African. Zimbabwean-born prop Tendai Mtawarira was the only black African player to start in the defeat to Australia in Perth, with Trevor Nyakane warming the bench. But SARU wants to make sure that by 2019 at least half the Springbok side consists of players of colour, with 60% of those required to be black African. SARU also set a mandate for Bok coach Heyneke Meyer to select at least five black players in his squad for the 2015 Rugby World Cup in England as well as include seven players of colour in his match-day squad in the lead-up to the tournament.

title: UKUTHWALA
oneLiner: UKUTHWALA is the name given to forced marriages, where underage girls are either given away or sold. Shockingly there are those who support the tradition.
summary: Topical: Human rights organisations and the DA this morning requested that the Minister of Police, Nkosinathi Nhleko, urgently deploys Family Violence, Child Protection and Sexual Offences Units to ukuthwala hot-spots across the country. According to tradition it is the abduction of young woman with the intention of forcing them into marriage negotiations often with the consent of their parents. Recent research has found that girls were often left with no choice but to marry, no matter how unhappy they might be. It found that families desperate for money were happy to accept the prospective husband's ilobolo (bride price) and might even "orchestrate" forced marriages. Girls who were married at an early age were forced to leave school and could be subjected to violent sexual abuse. Communities want it banned as a human rights crime against women.

The animals will be rehabilitated back into reserves, or to the reserves they came from when they are around 3.

title: Digital Burnout
oneLiner: Digital Burn out..and what happens when our offline and on line worlds collide, the new Star wars.
summary: Digital detox is the new buzz word. Ariannna Huffington – co- founder and editor-in-chief of the Huffington Post and called one of the most influential woman in the world – writes in her new book on the revolution that is taking place in the working world, about the need to unplug, to be able to work more effectively. Our own ‘Fluxtrends’ Dion Chang talks about the interesting tipping point we have reached. Our online and offline worlds are colliding. How do we come to terms with it and exist in two parallel universes, ‘ a physical realm were we are less present and a virtual world where we spend more and more time’ This always on, always connected, lifestyle is what is fuelling digital burn out. Sheryl Sandberg ( Facebook COO) has cut her online time after hours and in her words her productivity has increased. In California’s Silicon Valley, a new cyber, self-help industry is rising to curb digital burn out. Once it hits taking time off does not solve the problem. Some people end up in hospital, others end up in a dark hole. It is a new threat to human resources and all business’s. High profile executives are having techno free weekends and holidays its hard but some are managing. Drawing on the latest groundbreaking research on the time we spend on our devices ( more than we do sleeping) and the effects this connected lifestyle is having on our work, our families and creativity, I propose a lifestyle piece on this new conundrum. Looking at situation in South Africa talking to psychologists and researchers in the field, trend setters like Dion Chang and “technoholics’. Ideally interviewing Arianna Huffingtion either via Skype ( which would be ironic in itself) or in London if we did the Immigration piece and were flown to London. She is very vocal about what she call the Third Metric to redefine success and has written a ‘call to arms’ about the change needed.

title: Aviation Meltdown
oneLiner: Why the Aviation industry is up in arms about the new immigration policies.
summary: In 2011 the aviation industry’s annual contribution to the South African economy was valued at R 51 billion rising to R 74 billion when factoring multiplier benefits*. This is a significant contribution and rising, as tourism becomes one of South Africa’s major contributors to GDP growth. Yet the airline industry is totally disregarded when it comes to new laws pertaining to travel/immigration. On the 1st October under 18 year olds – of any nationality- travelling to South Africa will have to present their unabridged birth certificates. The premise for this new regulation is good - to protect minors specifically relating to the high volume of human trafficking. But the aviation and tourism industries have been arguing this is not only not a solution ( human trafficking is not usually into SA but out of) but there are alternative ways to better protect minors. This new policy will have a major impact on families travelling to South Africa, and coming into effect now, as tourism accelerates into the summer months. An unabridged birth certificate is not always at hand and the aviation/tourism industry predicts a huge crisis at airports on 1st October as this law comes into effect.

title: KITCHEN CROOKS
oneLiner: We expose a kitchen renovator that royally rips of clients leaving them with half finished kitchens and broke!
summary: LEKKER CONSUMER STORY - GREAT BADDIE WITH A TRACK RECORD AND A PENCHANT FOR THREATENING HIS CLIENTS! We go undercover and expose this kitchen crook!

title: Traci Morrison, FBI
oneLiner: A fake FBI agent who's conning people out of a small fortune from the comfort of the Sandton Police Station
summary: They’re not quite Bonnie and Clyde but con-artist Traci Morrison and Inspector Bruce MacIntosh of the Sandton Police have a long history of collaborating on elaborate cons. Posing as an FBI agent, Traci was able to con numerous people out of money and was even able to kidnap a 6-year-old, all the while using the Sandton Police Station, her boyfriend the cop and his colleagues to convince her victims. Traci was finally arrested in 2012, but the case against her has dragged on – meanwhile she’s out on bail and has continued conning more victims in small-time scams by posing as an interior decorator and party planner. Her partner in crime, meanwhile, is still on the job and has received commendations for his work in capturing the Rolex Gang. We follow the trail of her crime which leads from the Sandton Police Station to stolen dockets being sold in Wimpy to the leafy green suburbs of Morningside.
caseStudies: Moran Katz Heidi Poulton

title: Rhino Shock
oneLiner: 500 rhinos moved from Kruger supposedly for their safety and to protect the gene pool - but why to hunting operators?
summary: Kruger National Park no longer the jewel reserve of South Africa, rhino sold instead of protected from poachers. Peter Milton (founder of Strategic Protection of Threatened Species) Speaks Out… The news that a large number of Kruger Park rhinos are being moved to privately owned hunting farms has come as a major shock in conservation circles. Late last year, it was widely believed that SanParks, Kruger National Park (KNP) and the Department of Environmental Affairs (DEA) were considering the option to move Kruger rhinos – which are being slaughtered at an alarming rate – to “safe locations” in order to protect them from poaching and to ensure strength of the gene pool.
caseStudies: Peter Milton Conservationist kruger park insider

title: Clearing the Air
oneLiner: As smokers ditch fags for e cigarettes will new regulations
summary: In May 2014, the City of Cape Town announced that it was seeking legal opinion from the national health department on whether to limit the use of e-cigarettes in line with existing anti-tobacco legislation. The view had been that e-cigarettes could not be read into the definition of tobacco products because they did not contain tobacco, but delivered vaporized nicotine. Without national policy, the city could only prohibit the use of e-cigarettes through by-laws, or failing that, the provincial government could consider passing regional legislation. National Council Against Smoking (NGO) Dr Yussuf Salojee, executive director at the National Council Against Smoking believes that according to the Medicines and Related Substances Act, nicotine is classified as a schedule three drug when its intended use is as a substitute for a tobacco product. This means that e-cigarettes that contain nicotine need to be registered with the Medicines Control Council and can only be bought with a doctor’s prescription from pharmacies. There can therefore also be no direct consumer marketing. They do, however, believe that needs to be a test case in court to test these positions. CANSA According to CANSA, “e-cigarettes are not safe as they contain harmful substances and may contain nicotene and should therefore be avoided”. Medical Aids Sanlam chief medical adviser, Dr Pieter Coetzer, announced in May 2014 that e-cigarette users will be charged smokers’ rates for their insurance, even if clients say that they are using e-cigarettes without nicotine. Sanlam said that insurers had no way of determining whether or not these products are always nicotine-free. Liberty Life has followed suit by classifying them as smokers.

This week, fears that the deadly virus could spread globally as African immigrants travel across borders, saw many countries on high alert. Is SA at risk and are we prepared for Ebola?

title: Free at Last
oneLiner: 18 months ago tiger Corbett nearly killed maverick game ranger John Varty. Varty wanted to euthanase him - but an international outcry saved Corbett - in an SA exclusive we celebrate his release.
summary: By Varty's own admission Tiger Canyons is an experiment. It's maverick.But what drives him is that when he started the project 13 years ago there were 5000 tigers in the wild. Today there are 1000. In the next decade tigers will go extinct in the wild. His project has managed to rewild and breed tigers in an environment as close to the wild as possible. The tigers live in free ranging camps of around 1000 hectares and have access to live free ranging blesbok and springbok. But this is a story about one of those tigers - Corbett. Corbett was born at Tiger Canyons nearly 7 years ago to tigress Shadow. His birth is documented on film. As are visuals of him several weeks later spitting at the camera. He was an extremely aggressive cub. There is also video of him undergoing an operation after he was gored in the faced by a blesbuck. And visuals of his mother Shadow nearly drowning in the Orange river during the floods 4 years ago. There is also footage of Corbett next to the body of Shine a white tiger ostensibly killed by Free State hunters in a botched attempt to steal her for a canned hunt. 18 months ago - Corbett rose to fame when he attacked Tiger Canyons owner John Varty, putting him in ICU for 10 days and hospital for over a month. Varty at the time threatened to euthanaze the tiger, saying he had an aggressive gene. Several animal communicators came to see Corbett - none of them communicated the same message, which makes you wonder if they aren't all charlatans.
caseStudies: John Varty Film maker Julie-Anne Reid Du Toit Attending ICU doctor Gary Player Golfer

title: Brazouka
oneLiner: We re at the festival of festivals, behind the scenes of a dance movement that took the World Cup by storm
summary: BRAZOUKA is an M-Net sponsored show that is being brought out by Joburg Theatre It’s produced by Harley Medcalf and Pamela Stephenson-Connolly (Billy Connolly’s ex-wife and one of the great comedians), and directed by Arlene Phillips. Arlene Phillips is one of the most well-known choreographers in the UK – she choreographed the movie and stage show, Footloose, to name but a few. It is the story in dance of Braz dos Santos, the son of a Brazilian fisherman who escaped the life of poverty to introduce and popularise what has become one of Brazil’s unique dance styles-Lambazouk Baz’s “Lambazouk encourages a freedom of expression and has a joy and elegance with both feminity and masculinity. It is the style loved and practised by many of their students, followers and fans around the world – what tango is to Argentina, the Lambazouk is to Brazil. Sixteen dazzling dancers take audiences on a breath-taking journey of intense passion, sizzling sensuality, pulsing music and explosive energy. They will be at the Edinburgh Festival from August 1st to 25th and they then embark on a World Tour – first stop will be Joburg Theatre. We have been offered a trip to the Edinburgh festival to interview the producer’s, the choreographer, go back stage as the experience the festival and what I see is actually do a piece on this most iconic festival . A light hearted insert that will provide relief from the other more meaty fare.
