title: From Jail to Yale
summary: American actor Charles S Dutton, is best known for his starring role in the comedy/drama /sitcom ROC and for TV appearances he has made in The House, The Sopranos and HBO series, OZ. He has won Emmy’s for his role in The Practice and Without a Trace. But what is not known about him is his the 14 years he spent in prison in the United States for manslaughter. It was during this time he was sentenced to 6 days of solitary confinement and was allowed to take one book…the book he grabbed would change his life, an anthology of black playwrights. He was hooked and this passion changed his life. In 1984 Charles made his Broadway debut, and not only won a Theatre Award but received a Tony nomination for Best Actor. In September Charles will be in South Africa with his one man autobiographical play ‘From Jail to Yale: Serving Time on Stage’ and I propose an inspirational and humorous insert on Charles story.

title: ST LUCIA SPLITSVILLE
oneLiner: Ratepayers in St Lucia want to split from the Mtubatuba Municipality because of corruption and maladministration. They even want their own flag and racial tensions are at an all time high.
summary: SUMMARY The decision by the St Lucia Ratepayers’ Association from the tourist town has split the community along racial lines. St Lucia’s 500 residents currently fall under the Mtubatuba Municipality – a local government entity that has been under provincial administration for three years due to financial mismanagement and maladministration. (I remember someone pitching a story on lack of services in Matubatuba ... not sure if we did the story?) Ratepayers association chairman Rudi Redinger says St Lucia is in the heart of a World Heritage Site and provides the major accommodation component for visitors to the isimangaliso Wetland Park. In order to preserve it as a preferred eco-destination, the town has to be maintained with all services fully functional to meet tourists’ expectations. The ratepayers’ association say its their objective is to ensure this happens with clean municipal governance and transparent accounting for collective rate contributions. Despite provincial administration intervention that has been in place for over three years, little progress has been made with both the quality of service delivery, management competence and co-operation from the municipality.

title: CITY POWER CROOKS
oneLiner: It would seem the only way to sort out City Power’s billing crisis is to pay bribes – we expose an inefficient system.
summary: While the City of Johannesburg will tell you they have “broken the back of the billing challenge" – industrial customers have a different story to tell of sudden big account charges, overcharging and an inefficient system. President Zuma even made mention of billing crisis in his State of the Nation address - clearly there is reason for concern… We go undercover to expose dodgy “consultants” demanding bribes and City Power’s inefficiency.

title: Truck Laundering
oneLiner: 9 months after a truck ploughed through an intersection killing 22 people in Durban, it’s happened again. This time 5 people are dead. We expose yet another flaw in the licensing system.
summary: As Sandile May, the driver of the truck that killed 22 people in Pinetown in October last year prepares to go on trial on the 5th August, a 2nd truck smashed into a taxi at the same intersection last night .It’s unclear at this stage why the fresh produce truck didn’t stop. (I have footage of the scene) And this isn’t the only truck accident on Fields Hill in the past few months. There have been others. (I have SA Can footage of at least one other.) And in the past year there have been over 7000 accidents involving trucks in KZN, resulting in 70 deaths. After the Pinetown accident we showed how it was possible to buy a truck driver’s licence for a price without even making a booking to write a learners test. We also bought a COR for a truck that had been written off. At the time motoring experts criticised the e-Natis system – saying that the vast majority of traffic officers in South Africa don’t have access to the database – so they can’t check licences or pick up fakes. In fact they didn’t have much faith in the e-Natis system as a whole – calling it a system that has been riddled with corruption for years.

title: WHEELS COME OFF
summary: Motorists who drive a car displaying advertising that states ‘Drive a new car from R699’ are up in arms after the company behind the alleged scam, the Satinsky Group, said in a statement on its website that it dissolved its management agreement with media platform company, Blue Lakes Trading and Promotions Ltd. This means they will not get paid according to the two options they signed up for. An aggrieved Fin24 user wrote that "hundreds of people have been cheated out of their money" by Satinsky Group of Companies, which runs the Drive Car Sales business. In a plea to warn people “thinking of taking these cars” to be careful, the user, currently a client of Satinsky, said the only thing she can do now is to help stop the false advertising. “They are crooks and the more we drive with this false advertising the more people get trapped like us,” she wrote.

title: Goldfinger
oneLiner: it’s a scam that robs the country of billions of rands through smuggled gold and fraudulent VAT refunds.
summary: Life on the East Rand has changed drastically for former policeman Buks Jansen and his life Cornelia –they have ungraded to a multi-million rand mansion, helicopters, overseas trips and game farms. How did they get so lucky? The Jansens claim they won the lottery, but according to our insiders, the Jansens are one of handful of gold refinery owners who are profiting off an illegal gold scam that has been robbing the Treasury of billions in fraudulent VAT refunds.

title: Return to the Wild
oneLiner: For the first time in history a family of 9 gorillas is repatriated to Gabon from the UK. It's a journey of faith into the unknown...
summary: Djala’s story starts in 1982, in forests of the Congo basin where he was born as a wild gorilla. Sadly within the first 6 months of his life he had lost his mother and family to poachers. If this wasn’t traumatic enough he then had to endure mental and physical abuse caused by humans in the village of Djala, where he gets his name. Anyone who knows Djala will see how these early experiences have affected his adult life, as he becomes easily agitated by noisy crowds of people. Thankfully Djala’s life dramatically improved when a uranium prospector happened to be flying over the village, in his helicopter. He noticed a commotion and curiosity made him investigate. What he found was Djala tied to a post, he was shocked enough to buy him from the villagers. From here he took Djala home and cared for him for a couple of weeks before giving him to Yvette Leroy, a friend of his. Madame Leroy looked after Djala in her home for 2 years, during which time he grew in size and started to become a bit of a handful.

title: Illegal Greyound Racing
oneLiner: Illegal dog racing is prominent in South Africa, contributing to our on-going animal welfare crisis. The government is now suggesting that this ban be lifted to enable gambling on dog racing.
summary: South Africa’s animal welfare situation is in crisis. Yet activities that promote animal abuse, such as dog fighting and dog racing, continue to happen illegally. Greyhound racing in particular is very popular. Dog racing was banned in South Africa in 1949. Yet today it is not seen to be a major criminal offence and takes place most Saturdays across the country, it is especially popular in Gauteng and Free State. Greyhound racing has been linked to the mistreatment of dogs, dogs being kept in shocking confined conditions, terrible injuries which result in death and the injured dogs are not taken care of or disposed of correctly, insufficient veterinary care, inhumane training methods and drugging of the animals. According to the NSPCA, 50% of greyhounds die before they even reach the track. Greyhounds are also over bred and known to be used in illegal hunting. Now, in 2014, the South African government is considering legalizing dog racing. The bill goes to parliament on 23 June. The bill is being proposed by the department of Trade & Industry and would be legalized as part of the gambling norms and standards. Promoting the legalisation of greyhound racing for gambling purposes. Animal welfare organizations are predominantly opposed to the legalization of dog racing because of the risks to the animals involved. Whilst others argue that legalizing the sport will allow for it to regulate and control the sport. We take a look inside the illegal world of dog racing in South Africa to gain an understand of just how destructive this sport really is and whether it should be legalized.
experts: Mr. Jaco Pieterse Mr. Dean Bush

title: Milking the coffers see other
summary: Krynaauwslust is a 4400 hectare farm near Vrede in the Freestate. The Freestate government has committed to spend R 570 000 000 on a dairy farm on Krynaauwslust through a BEE company named Estina. Some of the expenses : *R2.6 million for the gate *R119 million for the actual dairy buildings *R2.5 million for spanners and tools *R6 million for dairy cows etc etc. According to a very glossy, drummed up report by the Freestate Premier Ace Magashule...Krynaauwslust will deliver 100 000 litres of milk per day out of the 370 dairy cows they bought. You will find some other interesting people also have offices in that block. Namely : 1. Duduzane Zuma. Our beloved president`s son. 2. Mabengela Pty (Ltd). Our beloved Gupta family`s company. 3. Thsepo Magashule. Our beloved Freestate Premier`s son.

title: Racehorse: Vercingetorix
oneLiner: Tonight on Carte Blanche the story of champion South African racehorse Vercingetorix & the grooms who raised & sold him for R1.4 million to race & win on the world stage at Meydan, Dubai.
summary: On 8th March this year the unbeaten South African bred racehorse Vercingetorix flew the South African flag high when he stamped his authority on the world racing stage at Meydan, Dubai recording his sixth consecutive win. Through his achievements Vercingetorix has become the “cause celebre” of an empowerment initiative designed to turn grooms into owners & sellers of highly-bred thoroughbreds in South Africa. The initiative supported by the Department of Trade & Industry [DTI] enables grooms from Stud Farms to participate in the annual Yearling sales across the country as buyers and sellers of valuable thoroughbreds. Initiating the project, two years ago the DTI funded the establishment of ten groom’s collectives spread across the country. There are five in the Western Cape (where 80% of SA’s racehorses are bred); three in KwaZulu-Natal and two in the Eastern Cape. Each collective, comprised of seven members, was granted R350 000 to invest in the purchase of ‘weanlings’ - four month-old thoroughbred horses that have been weaned from their mothers. These babies are then raised on the farms they work on, and are either sold at the yearling sales or as two year olds. The profits are returned to the co-ops and are used to buy more weanlings. For Abraham Carelse (59) and Floors Adams (62), having worked on stud farms in the Western Cape for almost 80 years between them, the opportunity to actually own the horses they cared for has always been elusive if not an impossible dream. As members of The Riverside Grooms Collective investing their DTI grant – Floors & Carelse bought Vercingetorix as a weanling from the farm for R 200 000-00. A year later, they sold Vercingetorix on the Cape Premier Yearling Sale for R 1.4 million. This is the story of the relationship between champion South African bred race horse Vercingetorix and the Riverside Groom’s Cooperative & their life-changing journey together from small beginnings to the world stage.

title: Dolphins and Orcas - Captive Cruelty?
oneLiner: The controversial "Blackfish", about to be screened in South Africa for the first time, shows the training of captive dolphins and Orcas to be a cruel - so we visit uShaka Marine world to find out.
summary: In the award-winning documentary 'blackfish', former Orca trainers at Seaworld in the US tell of the cruelty involved in training these massive creatures. The international world of performing dolphins and Orcas (marine mammal parks) is a billion dollar industry and a high-stakes game. The last trainer was killed by her favourite animal in 2010, the third person killed by the same animal (which happened to be insured for US $1million). These former trainers say such incidents happen because of the abuse the animals suffer. But it's not just Orcas that are abused - the trainers and pressure groups around the world claim that keeping any Cataceans (dolphins, orcas, porpoises etc) in captivity involves cruelty. They have called for an end to keeping them in captivity because of their sentient nature and renowned intelligence - with Chile, India and Puerto Rico even calling for dolphins to be afforded the status of 'non-human' pesons. Marine biologist and Two Oceans Aquarium MD Dr Pat Garrett meanwhile says that is a drastic reaction, that dolphin shows are essential, and that the industry isn't 'that bad'. We speak to former Seaworld postgraduate trainers and visit Durban's uShaka Marine world - the only place in SA where you will see performing dolphins - to find out for ourselves.

experts: Mr. Ric O’Barry 'The Cove' Dr. Pat Garratt Two Oceans Aquarium Ms. Ann Kunz uShaka Marine World

oneLiner: Carte Blanche exposes a serial crook… from unfinished building jobs, to Volksie restorations that never happened… he’s been at it for close to a decade!

title: Why weed?
oneLiner: There's a clamour for medical marijuana - could dagger oil offer cancer patients quality of life?
summary: Two weeks ago IFP MP Mario Oriano-Ambisini made an impassioned plea to parliament to legalize the medical use of can ibis oil? He, like many other cancer sufferers have discovered the apparent benefits to the terminally ill. He also tabled a Medical Innovation Bill which seeks to legalize cannibinoids for medical use, which he believes will have commercial and industrial spin offs. Apart from cancer many other chronically ill patients who have Crohns disease or are wheelchair bound with MS believe that cannibis oil has changed their lives, by reducing pain and aiding the body's healing process. Gerd Bader who has MS says his MS symptoms are greatly reduced since he started using the oil. Life is bearable again.

title: Ardmore A magical SA success story
oneLiner: From the hills of Kwa Zulu Natal to a London auction house the artists behind Ardmore.
summary: Ardmore Ceramics situated in hills of Kwa Zulu Natal just outside Pietermaritzburg is a South African success story. It began in 1985 when ceramicist and painter Fee Halsted began teaching her skills to her housekeeper’s daughter, Bonnie Ntshalintshali. Bonnie had polio, which meant she could not work in the fields. Five years later Bonnie and Fee jointly received the 1990 Standard Bank Young Artist award….. What started off as a dream soon spun into what is today the largest ceramic art studio in South Africa and with this Bonnie soon became known as one of South Africa's leading ceramic artists. Their collectors range from Hilary Clinton, Helen Mirren to Annie Lennox. A friend of mine who collects Ardmore literally sells pieces when she needs capital, it is a sure fire investment. Ardmore's artists have won numerous awards and exhibited in leading galleries and collections, including the Museum of Art & Design in New York, the Museum of Cultures in Basel, Switzerland, and the Tatham Art Gallery in Pietermaritzburg, South Africa. The acclaimed auction house Christie's has acknowledged Ardmore artworks as "modern day collectibles". The Ardmore Ceramic Art Studio has grown from a simple collaboration between two artists into one of South Africa’s most celebrated ceramic art studios. It is known for its daring mix of unusual ceramic art techniques and its bold display of Zulu colour and folklore in its designs.

title: OUR KILLING FIELDS
summary: In 1987 a hormone inhibiting herbicide, now known to be dangerous, was banned in KZN, but not before wiping out an entire farming industry in the Tala Valley. Now, this herbicide called 2,4-D, is being sprayed on fields and pastures across the country and could be causing serious illness. Carte Blanche goes digging for answers.

title: Security Company Crooks
oneLiner: Do you trust your security company when you're away? Carte Blanche catches 2 different security companies colluding to help rob a home owner blind.
summary: When you leave your house to go on holiday in the hands of your security company, you expect your house to be safe right? Wrong. Carte Blanche has video that shows two different security companies colluding to rob this man in a suburb of Johannesburg. The Video Shows: A Tactical Response Security (TRS) vehicle surveilling the houses, then later it comes back, drops off two men, who enter the house through the gate, switch on the lights to the house and in a few seconds manage to find the two alarm systems in place and disarm them. Clearly they are experts, because they would have had to know exactly where in the house the systems are. Then RSS, who is the security company that checks the house sends a vehicle because the alarm was tripped. With the two men in the house, the RSS security guard responds, but does not see the broken gate. He leaves. A white van then appears to pick up the stolen items from the house. But a neighbour calls RSS and says he thinks there is a robbery in process next door. Within seconds of that call, the white van shoots out of the driveway. (How would the white van know if there wasn’t someone within RSS security that called to tell them?) The RSS vehicle responds again. The same security guard as earlier Mpho. He spends 7 minutes walking up and down, still does not enter premises, does not see gate is broken. Leaves. The white van comes back several hours later, the two men pack up the truck and they leave. The TRS truck comes back and drops off the two men again, who go into the house to locate the video system, which means they are professionals. After a few minutes they leave the house on foot taking the VTR box with them. Then 15 minutes later, RSS trucks meet in the cul-de-sac down the driveway, and from about 80 meters away notice the gate is open in the dark, and then call in the robbery.

The tender – FOR APPOINTMENT OF OUTSOURCED AGENCIES FOR COLLECTION OF OUTSTANDING DEBTORS ACCOUNTS OLDER THAN 60 DAYS: 3 YEAR PERIOD, is not worth money, but for every outstanding amount the firm successfully collects they earn 10% of the money owed. Now the council can decide which amounts to send on the firm – R3,000 or R3 million. The source says the payments to council members is for the big amounts. FYI the debtors book for the City Tshwane’s finance department for almost 6 Billion half way through last year! This story involves the dirty underbelly of the competitive tender business. With emails, EFT transfers, sexy kickbacks (vehicles) and even setting up a fake call centre so the tender could be approved.

title: Solving Unemployment
oneLiner: We meet Sizwe Nzima, a 22 year old living in Cape Town’s Khayelitsha township, whose simple idea is transforming the lives of hundreds of needy people every day.
summary: When Sizwe Nzima’s grandparents needed medicines to treat their chronic illnesses, he volunteered to collect the medicines from the local hospital to make their lives easier. He found that hospitals were struggling to cope with the long queues of patients lining up to collect their medicines. After attending a course in entrepreneurship at the University of Cape Town’s Raymond Ackerman Academy, he hit on the idea of doing these collections for other patients, for whom the journey to the hospital was expensive and time-consuming. So not only did he save time and money for his customers, he also solved a growing problem for hospitals that could not find the solution to their growing queues. Sizwe now has some 380 customers in Khayelitsha whom he services with a team of four employees, all previously unemployed youth from the township. He bought them all bicycles, which are a convenient and cheap way to get around. Knowing the township inside out, they find the quickest way from the hospitals and local clinics to their customers’ homes using roads that are often clogged with traffic. At R10 a delivery, even the poorest customers can afford to pay. Those that work often can’t find the time to stand in long queues to collect their medicines, so Sizwe’s service is a godsend.

title: Hydrogen Energy South African Breakthrough
oneLiner: We uncover a radical breakthrough in the search for a clean, renewable energy source, and the South African team behind it.
summary: The world relies on energy, from boiling a kettle for a cup of tea to filling up the petrol tank to drive to work. No energy, our lives rapidly deteriorate and we begin to panic. Remember January 2008 when Eskom suddenly switched off the lights and we all rushed out to buy generators? Since then we have all been a lot more conscious of our energy usage, especially with petrol prices at record highs and electricity prices trebling in four years. And South Africa isn’t alone – even in Britain, there is talk of power rationing as coal fired power stations are decommissioned and new, not-so-reliable wind and solar sources of energy are introduced. So it’s not surprising the search has been on for decades for a clean, cheap and reliable source of energy that can replace our dwindling resources of coal, oil and gas. In the 1950s nuclear energy was seen as the answer, but that was before the environmental lobby started asking awkward questions about nuclear waste taking thousands of years to become safe. The technically even more complex nuclear fusion is still years away from commercial readiness. It seems hardly credible that perhaps the most likely source of energy comes from the stuff we use, drink, cook with and rely on every day of our lives – water.

title: Saving Cranes
oneLiner: There are only 260 Wattle Cranes left in SA, and the species survival depends on a team of seemingly “cuckoo” bird lovers who steal the eggs, dress up as mama bird and raise the flock themselves.
summary: Each year Wattle Cranes lay two eggs, but raise only one. Ann Burke, an international crane expert, came up with the idea of hand rearing the extra egg. Not as easy as it sounds! First the second egg had to be stolen from the nest in wild, without upsetting the breeding pair. A fully grown wattle crane stands almost as high as a man. The nests are also hidden in wetland and are not easy to spot. The first step is to ... take to the air. Using a small plane, Ann says identify the nests from above. (We have arranged a free flight to go looking for eggs). Once the location of the nests has been put into a GPS, one of The KZN Crane Foundation (KZNCF)’s members dons a “crane costume” and waddles into the wetland. After successfully impersonating a wattle crane, he/or she, snaps up the 2nd egg, which is whisked away to a waiting incubator.

summary: Rod Cassidy is a bird guide, an average guy in demand with birding enthusiasts the world over because of his knowledge. But so much does he love birds - of the amazing colours and calls that you find in the forest - that he built a birding lodge deep in the jungle on a river in the Central African Republic. Their world collapsed suring the coup earlier this year. Now they have returned to start things up again...with old friends (pygmies, forest elephants and eccentric NYC exiles included) re-emerging from their hiding places. They have a great relationship with the local community - and rebels are never too far away. But they feel the time is right. We tell the story of the breakdown and resurrection of their dream.

title: Hennops has lost its pride
oneLiner: Residents along the Hennops river live next to one of the most polluted rivers in the world - its posing a serious health threat and government is turning a blind eye.
summary: Two weeks ago Centurion resident, Roxi McCormick woke up to the most sickening stench from the Hennops river near her home. Horrified by the raw sewerage that was flowing down the river she took a sample in to the CSIR for testing. The results which came back this week were shocking 30 million parts per 100ml and streptococci of 75000 per 100ml. With the E Coli count at 30000000 and the Streptococci count at 765000 it is beyond the point where the Minister is obliged to make the information available in writing to affected public in terms of Section 145(1)(f) of the National Water Act. [any risk posed by the quality of any water to life, health or property] the Department should consider prosecuting the municipalities under Section 81(1)(e) of the WSA. The Department also neglected their duty to monitor under Section 62 and intervened under Section 63 when it was obviously necessary. There was mention that the quality of the effluent discharged water containing waste comply with by-laws but no municipality is not empowered to make such a bylaw and the municipality is further bound to comply with standards of the NWA under Section 78(b) of WSA. The directive issued by the Department does not comply with requirements of the Act. The Greendrop report of 2009 shows that Olifantsfontein sewerage works did not submit regular reports and their discharge quality was graded a G. The 2012 report also stated that the works was insufficient for the inflow . The Department should have already direct the municipality to expand the capacity of the works. And yet nothing was done about it. Given that we have an infrastructure backlog of 265 billion rand on water infrastructure can we afford this kind of disaster?

title: UNISA FRAUD
oneLiner: Experts in education are accusing UNISA of fraud. They say the state owned university is taking money from students, making promises, not delivering and then holding onto the cash.
summary: Since our story in August, we have received over 30 complaints against UNISA. It paints a picture of a once proud institution in disarray and plagued my maladministration. They complain of: • Marking errors (our poor students who got 37.4% are still no closer to solving the mystery. In fact others from the class have written n to say they also got the bizarre mark) • Taking money for remarking and not doing it • System errors and malfunctions – can’t register, no student numbers, software key to courses with errors • Not delivering materials • A financial department in chaos • Diplomas not being given even after graduation • Electives changed to non degree courses • And not registering the students after they have paid Experts in Education say UNISA is no different from other government service providers – who are letting the taxpayer down. Some have leveled charges of fraud against the university.

title: Gunned Down
oneLiner: A hit? Killed for doing his job - we look at the possible motives of the men who killed investigator Lawrence Moepi.
summary: Prominent Johannesburg auditing firm Sizwe Ntsaluba Gobodo says it hopes police will catch those responsible for the murder of one it’s directors in what’s believed to have been a hit. Lawrence Moepi was gunned down on Friday morning in the parking lot of the firm’s Houghton office. Eyewitnesses report having heard five gunshots before the gunmen fled in a Volkswagen Polo. Morphing was also involved in an investigation into Zwelinzima Vavi's controversial sale of the coasting HQ in Braamfontehin for 10 million below market value. Moepi’s been described as a hard-working man with a bright future and a loving father-of-two. The firm has alleged that the attack was clearly not a robbery, suggesting Moepi may have been killed for doing his job. He was involved in several high-profile cases, one involving the alleged looting of a fund belonging to the now dismantled Scorpions as well as an investigation into the arms deal. Public Protector Thuli Madonsela has spoken out about the incident sharing her own investigators fears and concerns that they may meet a similar fate. It begs the question - what kind of society allows this to happen and are high profile leaders behind this cold blooded murder? Police say a manhunt is underway for the suspects but will not confirm that the killing was a hit.

title: The Rhino Orphanage
oneLiner: Karen Trendler is saving rhinos one baby at a time at her first of its kind orphanage in the Waterberg.
summary: A day in the life of the Rhino orphanage in the Waterberg run by veteran wildlife rehabilitation expert Karen Trendler who started the facility just over a year ago in response to the need for specialist rhino facilities for orphaned babies in the wake of a poaching pandemic. She started with just one orphan and today the facility houses nearly a dozen babies. They are given 24/7 care and always have a volunteer carer with them who even sleeps with them at night. Most of these volunteer carers form part of an international volunteer exchange programme and are young women from America and Scandinavia. We can get beautiful visuals of a day in the life of one of these babies in the care of a volunteer - all under the watchful eye of Karen is a guru on raising baby rhinos - having cared for more than 300 during her life.

title: Kids going hungry in school
oneLiner: kids go hungry because the Education Department rates BEE status higher than service delivery
summary: For the past 55 years the Peninsular School Feeding Association –PSFA has been feeding school kids. For the past 10 years it has received a tender from the eduction department to feed 430 000 kids in 1026 school. It lost the Education Department subsidy in July and can now only feed 22500 children in 115 schools. The tender went two private small businesses which were BEE compliant but don’t seem to meet the rest of the requirements. Inyameko Trading 189cc trading as Masiyakhe Industries is based in Cape Town and Landmark Logistic is in Oudtshoorn. Since they took over the contract less children are receiving food, the portions are smaller and school teachers are having to choose who to feed. Some kids are no longer coming to school as it was the only meal they ate all day. The question on parents and educators lips is why did a small business win the tender when a charity was providing an excellent service for the past 10 years. Who runs and owns these small businesses, and at what expense to the kids who are now going hungry?

title: Sangoma Chef fights labour law in High Court
oneLiner: Traditional medicine is recognised by the medical profession but not the labour courts, 80% of workers have consulted traditional healers but this is not recognised as a bona fida medical sick note
summary: Johanna Mmoledi is hoping that her supreme court of appeal case of unfair dismissal will change the attitude of employers and Human Resources departments to traditional medicine. Mmoledi fell ill and was called to train as a Sangoma, in her attempt to heal herself she lost her job. The fight is for traditional medicine to be recognized by the labour courts and uphold her constitutional right to health. If her employer had seen her unpaid leave in the same light as a psychology student taking study leave to write their psychology masters, then Mmoledi would still have a job, and those who bring sick notes from Sangomas would not be sanctioned. Workers in this country are trapped between two paradigms that of African Traditional Medicine and Western Medicine. 80% of workers have consulted sangomas and although there is a register for sangomas and they are recognized by the government their sick notes are not recognized by most employers.

title: Pushing Paper
oneLiner: The Johannesburg paper pushers look like poetic ecological heroes, but behind the facade the motives and operations of these men are much more sinister.
summary: All over Johannesburg, the paper pushers can be seen on our roads, navigating their way through streams of traffic at all hours of the day and night. They haul heavy loads up hills, free-wheel at speed downhill and loiter on the streets in the wealthy suburbs. How did these people come to be doing what they do? On the surface they appear like some sort of poetic ecological heroes. However, behind the facade the motives and operations of these men can be much more sinister. Rather than recycling waste materials, they could very well be planning to recycle the valuables in your home. We will follow and interview a number of case studies. See where they come from, who they deliver to and discover the clandestine truths. Already I have interviewed two case studies, one revealing he is a double murderer on the run. His main motive for doing what he does is that it is the only way he can survive and stay out of the hands of the law. Both case studies have admitted that their work is not all that it seems.. they get paid for information that helps others identify properties they can burgle and the logistics as to how. The paper pushers also admit to carrying out opportunistic robberies themselves. How does the general public feel about such revelations and will they alter how they feel about the paper pushers from now on? Do the police recognize the situation and what are they doing about it?
caseStudies: Paper pushers SAPS Home owners

title: Lucas “Twister” Sithole, Another African First
oneLiner: Fame & acclaim has come as a surprise to Lucas Sithole, the first African to win a US Open tennis title. Physically challenged, he sets the bar high for himself, not only in tennis but also in music.
summary: Lucas Sithole is the first African in history to win a US Open title in tennis. The win took him to world number two but a driven and ambitious Sithole wants to be number one. Twenty six year old Sithole knew this moment would come but expected it to take ten years. Sithole is an inspirational figure, he lost both legs and his dominant right arm at the age of twelve. He was helping a friend who was a freight train worker to adjust a railway track “and then the train started to move slowly, and I tried to jump away, but I fell on the tracks.” He was lucky to survive, but had to fight depression. His mother and three sisters feared that he would take his own life. They kept telling him that it would be ok. Although physically challenged, Sithole is achieving firsts and is driven to hit the top spot, not only in tennis but also in music. He is planning to release a maskandi album with the band Amathalante Amahle (the beautiful talents) in November. I would like to profile Lucas in training, at the tennis court and in the music studio – to tell of his unique journey to success.
caseStudies: Lucas Sithole Holger Losch Kgothatso KG Montjane Sithole Keith Brebnor

title: The concept of forgiveness
oneLiner: Who is able to forgive murderers?
summary: This is a pre-proposal to find out if Carte Blanche might be interested in such a story. If it is then I will provide a more detailed proposal with interviewees. This story explores the concept of forgiveness and sometimes the healing of this act. Over the weekend we read that Dina Rodrigues, "the baby killer", has submitted another plea for her sentence to be reduced. It makes interesting reading. The grandfather of Baby Jordan, a devout Catholic, responded that for all he cares she can rot in hell. Whilst the truth and reconciliation commission provided a platform for perpetrators of heinous crimes to ask for forgiveness with its aim at national reconciliation and allowing victims to gain some form of 'peace', what systems are in place for the families of loved ones who may have been brutally murdered? We know that at times family members of loved ones are given the opportunity to face a , at times, remorseful perpetrator in a prison setting, sometimes with positive results. But in 99.9% of all murders, this process does not take place and the closest contact will be in court. So how do families of victims cope? Some lives fall apart, sometimes there is divorce in the family, sometimes even suicide, sometimes a deep sadness and bitterness that pervades the family of the victims life forever. Yet there are some people who find it within themselves to forgive the perpetrator. Not immediately, obviously, but in time. And through forgiveness they are freed of deep anger which could become a destructive force in their lives. Forgiveness is not only the domain of the deeply religious person. Agnostics and atheists also forgive. Just who are able to forgive? Do you have to have come form a particularly grounded background to forgive? Does the severity of the crime have an impact on our ability to forgive? Are we able to extend forgiveness to a psychopath for example?

title: Placement Agency Scams
oneLiner: THe Department of health uses placement agencies to fill locum positions at their hospitals and clinics but what recousre do medical practicioners have when the agencies dont pay up?
summary: Dietician Mariam Forgan was contacted by Tygerberg hospital to apply for a locum position but as the Department of Health does not employ locum staff directly, she was supplied with a list of Agencies. The first on the list, and the cheapest, was of NBE Placements owned by Kenneth Ratshisusu. Although the NBE website was basic, it promises payment within seven days. It took three weeks for Mariam to get her first payment after much nagging and after 5 weeks of work she is still waiting for R5700. Kenneth now refuses to take her calls and is getting abusive. Mariam has discovered that she is not the only victim and that there are 4 other doctors and two dieticians still waiting to be paid, some of the cases dating back for two years. It appears that NBE Placements just keeps the last few weeks of what they owe you and then threatens you, knowing that it’s too costly to take on lawyers. But its not just the medical professionals he is not paying, his secretary finally threw in the towel after not being paid for two months’ and the NBE office is closed due to rent arrears. The Department of Health say there is nothing they can do because services have been rendered which they have paid for and so it’s not their concern. But NBE Placements is not complying with basis agency requirements like supply medical practitioners with IRP 5’s and having an office from which it operates. His former Secretary has all the paperwork and evidence of NBE’s administrative fraud and is willing to talk, as are the other doctors and dieticians who have been scammed in a similar manner. Agency registrations with the Department of Health get renewed in November, perhaps NBE Placements should be exposed so other medical professionals don’t suffer the same fate.

title: Pirated security bars
oneLiner: Imagine paying thousands for burglar bars only to discover that cheap pirated plastic parts were used?
summary: This could make a great reality style 8 minute scam piece. Darren Taylor and Mia Malan have just bought a house in Melville and one of the first things they decided to do is to put up burglar bars for security. But thats when they got scammed by a company called Beautiful security. This ocmpany installs cheap inferiot poly carbonate burglar bars which add no peace of mind whatsoever to home owners. They are supposed to sell Multisafe bars which are patented and safety tested but thats not what consumers are getting. Darren Taylor and Mia Malan discovered that they are not SABS approved, break easily and that the company has a long history of ripping people off with these cheap and nasty imports. They are currently trying to get their money back and have had no success - Darren is planning to go and challenge them at the Decorex expo this week at Gallagher Estate to demand they either replace them with security bars that will protect his family or refund his R11000.

title: Suffer the children while the politicians squabble
oneLiner: How can they ever their exams?
summary: This is a story with many layers showing how the odds are stacked against school children who live in gang infested communites: Mannenberg - A Case Study. This is a hotspot of the gang war. Please see uploaded onto the FTP site camera footage of gang shootout recorded by children. I understand we can have access to many more snippets from cellphones. Mannenberg is bracing itself for the release of Hard Living gang leader, Rashied Staggie, who has spent the last 11 years in prison for orchestrating the rape of a teenager. Incidentally just in the last few days, the rape victim and her boyfriend were attacked. The boyfriend was killed and the rape victim is in a coma. Commentators are suggesting that this rise in gang warfare between the Hard Living gang and The Americans is a turf war in preparation for Staggie's release. Gang violence is at its height in the Western Cape. In the first weekend of July this year 44 people were killed in the Western Cape. The papers are full of stories of children and innocent bystanders being killed in the crossfire and through all of this the ANC and the DA are fighting with each other, accusing the other of inappropriate relationships with gang members. There has also been a call for the army to be introduced into the Western Cape but the President has denied this request. And whilst this political bickering is taking place, with no solution in sight, there is one group of innocent victims who are bearing the brunt. Earlier this year, a Grade 12 pupil, Glen Rico Martin of Spesbona School in Mannenberg, was shot and killed by gangsters. The very next day was the June exams. 70% of Grade 12 pupils failed their exams. This is an example of how post-traumatic stress is taking hold of school children who are expected to do well in school. Not only that but it seems that pupils in the playground are separating into two groups, perhaps out of fear, those supporting The Hard Living gang and The Americans.
caseStudies: Valda van Reenen Headmaster - Spesbona School DA and ANC Spokespersons Department of Education Spokesperson Hopefully one or two gang members children who are suffering post traumatic stress one or two victims

title: Being held abroad
oneLiner: We speak to families fighting to be heard by the South African judicial system, why are drug mules being left in foreign prisons with no further investigation by South African officials
summary: Patricia Gerber has been fighting for South Africa to create a prison treaty with Mauritius since 2005, when her son was arrested for smuggling heroine. She started an organisation called Locked up and is now helping other families try get their people home. Even though the drug mules are guilty of a crime, they are not the people controlling the drug trade in South Africa and by keeping them locked up in foreign prisons, they are not able to help the South African officials track down the big guys. Patricia opened a case with the IPD after the South African police went to Mauritius in 2006 to investigate her sons case, but did not take a single statement. The questioned being asked in this story is why are the South African officials scared to bring these people home and why are the drug mules not being used to catch the people in charge of the drug trade in South Africa. South Africa is one of only two countries in the world without a single prison treaty, the other Country is Ghana.
caseStudies: Patricia Gerber Thandie Wembewu Margaret Preston Shaun Bernard Honjiswa Mbewu
experts: Mr. Paul Ramaloko

title: Greyhound Investigation
oneLiner: The grey areas surrounding Greyhound racing.
summary: To many people there is something enduring about watching these magnificent, streamlined and intelligent dogs, tearing around excitedly after a mechanical hare on a racetrack. After all, this breed is the second fastest accelerating animal in the world, after the cheetah. Here in South Africa there is a push to have Greyhound racing legalized. Once a month a group of Greyhound enthusiasts get together in the Orange Free State to race their dogs against each other. They say it's all in good fun and there is no gambling involved. But is there? Carte Blanche investigates this, as well as, the rise in popularity of the Greyhound being bred and used in some communities as hunting dogs.
caseStudies: Dean Bush JBM Hertzog
experts: Dr. Jan de Wet Prof. Banie Penzhorn

title: Taking back the landscape
oneLiner: Defusing RPG's is now accessible and safe to the war ravage communities across Africa
summary: Unexploded landmines, bombs and RPG’s litter the worn torn landscapes of Africa, a legacy that haunts the survivors of war long after peace has returned and people begin to reconstruct their lives. But it was not Africa that initially grabbed Paul Richards attention, but Britain, when they began dredging the Thames and discovered 500 pound undetonated bombs from the 2nd World War Blitz of London. The first device he developed was called the Mineburner, which Carte Blanche did a story on, which safely defused bombs but it was expensive and heavy to transport, and required specialised training. Richards has now developed the RendSafe a much cheaper, more easily transportable device that has numerous advantages over his original creation. The RendSafe burns through 22mm steel casing in 1 second, defusing the device. It’s low cost, cheap to transport and requires minimal training. Richards hopes that his invention will empower local people to take control of cleaning up their communities.He is off to Misarata to deliver 200 devices and has offered us his footage of his trip in which he will be filming the training and defusing of RPGs that plague this community.
caseStudies: Paul Richards

title: WHOONGA
oneLiner: Originally associated with poorer communities the drug “Whoonga” is now claiming addicts in affluent areas. No one group is immune and it’s fuelling violent crime. The problem is being ignored b
summary: Violent Crime in South Africa is being fueled by a drug called “whoonga”. A deadly mix of heroin, rat poison and steel wool, the poisonous concoction is being peddled, in some cases,by grandmothers. Even children are getting addicted. And at R25 a hit the addition is spreading rapidly. And it’s not just poor communities being affected. Whoonga addicts are found in affluent suburbs and victims of these violent gangs come from across all communities.

title: Show Us The Money
oneLiner: It's estimated that since thino poaching escalated in 2008, over 280 new conservation NGOS have been formed in the rhinos name - we show the ease with which such operations can scam the public.
summary: Sanwild is a wildlife sanctuary in limpopo that has long relied on public funding to keep it running. Its owner, Louise Joubert, harnesses public sympathy - and the media - to good effect. She has even had CB produce an insert on a fight she was having surrounding the Sanwild property. She sends her pleas global, and whether about lions or, increasingly, rhinos, funds often arrive from the likes of the US, UK and Australia. But she doesnt only get money from overseas - she also gets volunteers, a number of whom have claimed they were brought out under false pretences. Like the French soldiers and young americans who came to go on a 'rhino anti-poaching course' but ended up doing manual labour - and ended up being kicked off the property when they complained. But Louise has also 'hired'local anti-poaching types to help out - and when they experienced similar problems - like appeals for funding an anti-poaching patrol that didnt exist, they thought they had to take action.

title: Post Traumatic Stress and the Police
oneLiner: Our cops are suffering
summary: Against the backdrop of two Marikana policeman commiting suicide and 116 police suicides in 2012, Carte Blanche investigates the levels of stress that our police services work under and whether policeman suffering depression seek professional help that is offered to them. We tend to forget the often difficult situations the police work under - not only from dealing with criminals and dealing with their bosses - but also the distrust they continually face from public. Whilst we must be concerned about 116 police committing suicide, we also need to be concerned about the fact that there are probably tens of thousands of policeman who are suffering in some way. The flip side is that their apathy perhaps due to depression results in a less effective police force. Finally Carte Blanche investigates all the pressures that the ordinary policeman has to deal with in his life. We should interview a top psychologist and get two or three policeman who suffer post traumatic stress on the programme.

title: Organ donation gone wrong
oneLiner: In a country where only 1% of the population are registered organ donors, you’d think living donors would be appreciated. But in Gauteng, one man's willingness to donate turns into a fiasco.
summary: Two years ago Reggie Segran Nair decided he wanted to do “something good.” His father-in-law had died waiting for a kidney transplant. As a man who kept himself healthy and fit, Reggie decided he would become a living organ donor. He approached the Organ Donor Foundation. Eventually he was matched with a 5 year old girl. The transplant would take place at the Red Cross in CT. But the process took so long the little girl died before the operation could happen. In the process however Reggie was approved as a living donor. (He has all documentation – both physical and psychological from that period). Demoralised, Reggie decided it was not meant to be. But in October last year, while surfing the net, he came across a website based in Israel responsible for pairing recipients and donors. (According to Reggie the ODF have approved this website. We wil have to check this.) Here he was put in touch with a Jewish woman from Cape Town whose father (living in JHB) was in need of a kidney transplant. Reggie met with Raymond and the two have since formed a friendship. They are also a match. He says it should have been smooth sailing. But instead the transplant has been derailed by what he believes is anti Semitic prejudice on behalf of Netcare and the ministerial medical council responsible for giving transplants the go ahead.

title: Get- A Home Take 2
oneLiner: Its your home but if you move in your life is in danger,
summary: In our last story on RDP Home Owners -who apparently without prior knowledge had their homes sold from under their feet and on the other side of the coin new home owners - who had bought homes and then not been able to move into them because of the ‘previous’ owners belief the home was still theirs ….We opened up a can of worms. Promises made from Get-A- Home that they would not carry working this way, from Tokyo Sexwale that he would step in to try and sort things out have not materialised, the situation if anything has become worse resulting in a march last Friday in a desperate attempt for East Rand residents and home owners to get some action and help to a situation which remains dire. In a follow up programme who re look at the situation, profile new home owners like, Sgt Majwede, who was been attacked by the community to prevent him and his family taking ownership of their home. Or Emma Dladla who sold her house in Soweto for around R150 000 back around 2007. Then she saw a Get-A-Home advert and she used the R150 000 to pay cash for the house in Katlehong. The said house in Katlehong was already lived in by the children of the mom who had lived and passed away. Emma is instigating criminal proceedings against Get-A- Home. We question why nothing has been done on the Human Settlements side, Tokyo promised to talk to Banking Council on behalf of the Community and go with Tokyo to visit Community – which he will do at the end of this month. For a company like Get- A-Home the business model is simple buy re possessed homes cheaply and sell for a handsome profit but for home owners and people caught up in the problem there are dire consequences and they need to answer to why they are still acting without full disclosure to both new home owner and previous home owner,

title: The Lars Maersk
oneLiner: We take a look at a remarkable working vessel conducting scientific research on the effects of climate change on the oceans.
summary: Maersk Line, the world's largest container shipping line, which will be docking one of its Flagships, The Lars Maersk in Cape Town this June. The Lars Maersk is not only a working vessel but has been specially fitted to conduct scientific surveys on the north-south route between Europe and South Africa, monitoring the effects of climate change on the world's oceans. Changing climate and ocean conditions present real risks and challenges for the shipping business. The effects of climate change on the world's oceans have led to greater volatility, and accurately modelling and predicting these effects is essential to shipping all over the world. With container shipping being a key facilitator of global trade and an integral part of the global economy, it was essential for Maersk to take important steps towards sustainable growth. A visit to the Lars Maersk will provide a rare glimpse into how the strategy is being implemented at sea. Lars Maersk takes the twin goals of achieving business sustainability and reducing environmental impact even further by functioning as a research vessel that provides vital data for managing the environmental impact of human activity on the world's oceans. Equipped with cutting-edge equipment installed and maintained by the University of Las Palmas. This programme aims to assess the expected consequences of rising CO2 concentrations in the atmosphere, and to guide the reduction of emissions produced as a result of human activity.

title: Angelo's Ashes ?
oneLiner: Angelo the blind white Bengal tiger is worth more dead than alive from a breeder`s perspective - we watch one man's fight to prevent him being shot by hunters.
summary: A gamekeeper at a Mossel Bay wildlife facility-Jukani-has been fighting for four years to prevent two white Bengal tiger cubs in his care from being shot by hunters. The people he's fighting are the same that initially asked him to care for them - a widlife breeding facility in the Free State that imported the tigers from a Zoo in Canada (because the Free State doesnt allow the import of exotic species). The deal was that Jukani takes the 4 month-old tigers - angelo and mitch - on loan, with any progeny going to the owners in FS Province. In July 2009 Angelo was diagnosed with Progressive Retinal Atrophy, a genetic transferable and incurable disease that will leave him permanently blind. He now needs specialist care, from a team led by Jurg, who has developed a strong relationship with him. When told of his condition, the owners told Jurg he could either buy the two animals - demanding a sum of R250 000-00 each - or sell them to somebody else. He was given a deadline. Options? Limited. Because Angelo is going blind, provincial authorities could grant permission to have Angelo euthanased - in a trophy or canned hunt. Angelo is worth more dead than alive from a breeder`s point of view. But help arrived unexpectedly, with two benefactors helping to raise the money. It was slow. Two days before the deadline, the anonymous benefactors provided a bridging loan for the entire amount to buy Angelo and Mitch. More help arrived: the owners of Monkeyland and Birds of Eden outside Plettenberg Bay offered to buy Jukani and relocate the facility to a much bigger, more suitable property. The relocation is planned for next month. Jurg says Angelo has changed his life. We tell his story.

title: Cape Town's Dog Whisperer
oneLiner: The story of a girl who gave it all up to save the most abused and unwanted animals.
summary: In 2011 in Aandskof, Cape Town, a puppy was thrown into a fire by a 3 year old child. The young puppy endured 2nd degree burns over 90% of her little body. She was rescued and had intensive treatment and care – but died a few days after a rescue. (Picture 1) Just a few months later - a dog was rescued in Aandskof that had been burned with acid. (Picture 2) Earlier this month,in the same area, a 6 month old puppy was found stuffed in a braai, suffering in agony from horrendous injuries inflicted as a result of children pulling her teeth causing her gums to be ripped from the bone and rotting away. (Picture 3) Just last week a stray dog was rescued in Cape Town that had such a bad case of mange that it had no hair left on its body – it was starving and its body was covered in sores from being stoned by local kids (Picture 4 and 5). These are just a few of the horrific cases that the Lucky Lucy Foundation sees on a regular basis. The lucky Lucy foundation was founded in 2010 after Richelle Graham (Picture 6), then a 23 year old aspiring model and actress, found a dog who had been tied to a railway line. Trains had repeatedly gone over her, her leg was severed and she was heavily pregnant (Picture 7 and 8). Lucy was rehabilitated back to health and became the driving force behind the Lucky Lucy Foundation – a Non-Profit, Pro-life animal rescue that relieves the plight of severely neglected and abused township and street animals, but also socially uplifts and educates destitute and impoverished children and people in and around Cape Town (Picture 9). They believe that by providing people with the needs to care for themselves, and the knowledge of how to correctly care for their animals, we will reduce the abuse and cruelty that is so prevalent in these communities. They take in “no hope animals’ that would normally not be given a chance and run mass sterilization projects thereby preventing unwanted litters and ending the cycle of abuse.

title: Should we care?
oneLiner: Is it possible to rehabilitate a gangster who has killed 7 people?
summary: Brian Alexander murdered 3 people in 1996 and then a few years later fatally stabbed a man in front of his mother. Today he is in a new venture, an especially equipped lock up rehab centre for gangsters. The gangsters are carefully screened. Those gangsters who show potential to be rehabilitated and reintegrated into society are chosen to be part of the program. The rehab centre has already had a rocky start. The program, founded by gangster turned pastors, Albern Martins and Ivan Valdeck, made headlines recently after Matins was murdered and Valdeck was wounded in a drive by shooting. There are obviously rival gangs who want to try and kill rival gang members who are trying to rehabilitate themselves. Security has been increased at this facility. How and why the centre came into being, the admission criteria and social workers working in dangerous conditions, will be the glue to the story. Terrifying interviews which show the depravity of some gangsters will certainly jolt the senses. But there are other questions to be answered.

title: Sweatshops
oneLiner: South Africa is clamping down on Sweatshops - who is paying the price for ethical threads? The garment industry has already lost three quarters of its jobs in the past decade to cheaper imports
summary: (Reuters) - It's not luxurious, but Goldfinch Garments, the Chinese-owned South African factory where Sindisizwe Zwane works nine hours a day, is far from a sweatshop: the ventilation is decent, the lighting is good and basic safety measures are in place. South Africa says its garment industry is better regulated and workers are better paid than in ultra low-cost Asian producers like Bangladesh, where the collapse of a factory killed more than 1,100 people last month.The ruling African National Congress (ANC) government, with close links to labour unions, wants to go further by enforcing a wage agreement that would guarantee Zwane and her co-workers a raise. But the garment industry has already lost three-quarters of its jobs in the past decade as cheaper imports have flooded the local market. Zwane, 28 and one of only two wage earners in a family of 14 people, fears that efforts to win her a raise could cost her livelihood. "Of course I want more. I want a whole loaf of bread instead of the half I am getting. But half a loaf is better than nothing," said Zwane. "If I lose the job, we lose everything." Zwane is one of about 250 workers at Goldfinch, one of a cluster of clothing factories in the hardscrabble industrial town of Newcastle, 260 km (160 miles) southeast of Johannesburg. Goldfinch is spartan but appears safe and clean. The factory has rows of sewing machines where a workforce of mostly women spend hours stitching together clothes. Workers often bundle up on colder days and some cover their faces with cloth to protect them from dust. Zwane can earn as much as about $220 per month, with her income depending on how many orders come in.

title: Fafi - "Mo-China"
oneLiner: Fafi- by far the most popular for of informal gambling. Punter's bets & winnings are drawn from a luxury car with tinted windows, driven by a 'chinaman' - we unveil the mysterious "Mo-China"
summary: Fafi is the most common form of gambling in Gauteng townships. Originating in China a brought to South Africa in the early 1900's, it was first played by miners in the old Transvaal. It is a mobile form of lottery in which punters place numbers from 1-36 - Mo-China drives a luxury car that cruised the streets twice a day and the car even is spotted in wealthy northern suburbs of Johannesburg during the daytime taking bets from domestic workers. The 'chinamen' or Mo-China is extremely wealthy through running the operation- it is illegal but this hasn't stopped the big black car. A participant stated that Fafi gave better returns than any financial institutions he knew - Mo-China pays out the winning number at a rate of R28 to R1. We try and meet Mo-China and find out where he lives - in order to reveal his lifestyle. We will try and get an interview with him -

title: June 17th - Forgotten in History
oneLiner: While we commemorate those who died in Soweto in 76, there are other communities who feel they have been forgotten in history
summary: June 16th falls on a Sunday this year and whilst we have always done something on it, I propose we shift our focus to an equally tragic day, which seems to have been lost in the history books, June 17th, the day the protests and killings spread to Alexandra Township in northeast Johannesburg. In Alex Township, this year I know there will be a remembrance march to the graveyards of those who died, planned by family members of the dead and the community – in what you could call another act of protest that they too suffered but have been largely overshadowed by their compatriots in Soweto. Fourteen schools, six thousand children were affected. 21 people died in Alex that day and many more in other townships around Johannesburg. The first victim in Alex was Jappie Vilankulu Mogotsi, his sister Sinah says her brother was shot seven times by the police and died a cruel death that still haunts the family to this day. Relatives who went to identify her brother told them how he had died with his hand outstretched. "His decomposed body was found amongst a pile of other bodies. We put apples and pineapples in his coffin to mask the horrible smell when we buried him." Peter Magubane was also there: “The next day was the 17th, I went to Alexandra Township. Now in Alexandra Township it was a different story from Soweto. The police went in there with the aim of killing people for they did not use any teargas nor rubber bullets. I saw a man being hit who was right inside the toilet, who had done absolutely nothing. He was sitting in the toilet relieving himself. He was shot and killed.”

title: The world of Sex and Teenage Trafficking- Can we Help
oneLiner: Brought to the City of Gold which false promises, Can these girls ever go back to their youth
summary: In 2000, Mam’ Khanyi, a successful business woman in her own right, took in 5 girls, who had escaped from one of Hillbrow’s brothels. Their stories were horrific- brought to JHB by agents who have promised them and their families schooling , jobs….. and then once here abandoned to thugs and pimps. Word of the refuge spread and soon, more girls escaped into Mam’ Khanyi’s care. Their stories were frightening, most arrive from the rural areas or neighbouring countries of South Africa. They are promised jobs or schooling in the big city. But once they arrive and the agents are paid, they are abandoned and left at the mercy of the ruthless gangsters who hold them captive. They are told they have to “work” to pay off the money the gangsters have paid the agents to recruit them. Their ID documents are taken from them to make escape more difficult. As Mam’ Khanyi’s personal funds ran out, she formed a committee and Khanyisile Motsa (Mam’ Khanyi) became the founder and co-ordinator of the Berea Hillbrow Home of Hope who look after and try and rehabilitate these girls Their mission – “We bring hope to girls without. Choices to those with none.” Her story and those of the girls she looks after give a shocking insight into the world of Sex Slaves and human trafficking. Mam’ Khanyi is not a sucker for a hard story. She has a nose for the truth, and an eye for potential. Her standards are high and she doesn’t see herself as being in the business of giving handouts to people who don’t deserve them. She would like to be a lifeline for those who otherwise slip through the gutters and disappear into the growing underbelly of Johannesburg society. She was recognised for her tireless contribution to her community at the Feather Awards ceremony held on 25 March 2010. …And nominated as the Nedbank Hero of the Month in November 2009 for Community Building.

title: Perlemoen Poaching in PE
summary: After years of watching perlemoen poachers brazenly going about their trade along Marine Drive in Port Elizabeth Dewald Barnard and a handful of others formed themselves into citizens watch to stop poaching. However, their activism is not without a price, Dewald has had his motorbike set alight in front of his home, his wife was been forced off the road by the poachers and he receives death threats on a regular basis. After months of living in fear his wife has now moved away with their new born son because she fears for the safety of their child. Dewald has filed reports at the local police station after every incident but every time he follows up on the case he discovers the dockets have disappeared. Despite losing his wife and child, Dewald is determined to keep at it.

experts: Mr. Dennis Mostert Mr. Brig Koll

title: Organ donation: A fight to survive
oneLiner: With organ donations in SA dipping as low as two per million people many don't live long enough to find a suitable match. Can the odds be improved.
summary: In July the World Transplant Games will be held in Durban. NB: I see this story NOT as a report about the games but as a way to talk about the issues of donor transplantation in SA. It makes the subject topical and current. The story can be flighted prior to the games kicking off on the 28th July. Story Each organ donor could help give up to seven people a new lease on life; donating kidneys, heart, lungs, liver and pancreas. Soft tissue, bone and corneas could improve the quality of life of up to 50 more people. Mathew Legemaate (14) People like 13year old Matthew Legemaate who is currently waiting for a heart and lungs transplant. Matthew was born at the Morningside Medi Clinic and had his first operation at the age of 36 hours. He was born with ‘tetralogy of fallots’ with pulmonary artresa. Basically his heart had 3 chambers with no divisions and no pulmonary valve. There was no blood flow from heart to lungs. But he doesn’t let it slow him down. With a backpack of oxygen and tubes permanently feeding into his nose, Mathew is determined to go to school and get on with being a teenager. His philosophy is, “It’s not so bad .... there are others worse off than me.” Obviously he cannot participate in sport, but is determined he will one day lead as an active a life as his healthy mates and friend who have had their transplants.

title: Mark Strydom
oneLiner: Why is an alleged thug who served time in jail for violent attacks still being allowed to beat people up while he's on parole?
summary: In 2010 producer Paul Nel produced an insert for Carte Blanche about a prison rehabilitation project. One of the success stories was Mark Strydom a notorious thug who had been terrorising people in the South of Johannesburg until he was eventually put away in jail for 13 years for brutally attacking a woman, knocking her unconcious and then kicking her until he shattered her ankle. This was one of dozens of incidents. But due to the programme and the fact that he professed to be a reborn Christian he was let out on good behaviour after serving just three years. That was 2010, but now stories have started resurfacing that nothing has changed and if anything he is worse than ever. A few months ago he broke a woman's nose at the racetrack by head butting her, he beat a man unconsious at Lusitoland last wednesday and he goes around threatening people and picking fights. He called boxer Brian Mitchells wife a whore and a bitch in a posh restaurant and then spat on her. Mikey Schultz who is now his sidekick joined in and she has laid charges against them. His ex girlfriend says he tried to kill her on more than one occassion when she refused to let him go and buy drugs from prostitutes in Rossenville. She says he takes a killer cocktail of drugs and steroids which puts him into a rage and when he drinks he loses control. And afterwards he cries like a baby and begs forgiveness. But what no-one understands is how he manages to violate his parole conditions and why he is still walking the streets despite the fact that there are several cases open againgst him?

title: From Saharanpur to Saxonwold
oneLiner: Last week, billionaire Gupta brothers, “flew in the face” of international border protocol when they landed a jet full of wedding guests at an air force base. But they weren’t always part the j
summary: Saharanpur A stray dog scavenges for food in a dark passage leading to a nondescript apartment block in Rani Bazar, Saharanpur - a dusty, fly-infested city in northern India, nearly 200km from Delhi. Several window frames are in dire need of a coat of varnish. Old towels and saris are draped over a wrought-iron balustrade. Until 1989, this 30-room building was home to the Gupta brothers - Ajay, Atul, and Rajesh - who are now super-rich South African residents. And while in South Africa there’s a concern about the Guptas' cosy relationship with President Jacob Zuma and unjustified manipulation of the country’s affirmative action policies in order to rake in tenders - in Saharanpur, locals sing the praises of a "hard-working" family and their dad, Shiv Kumar Gupta. The family's patriarch, who died in 1994, and his wife, Angoori, lived in the building in Rani Bazar with their three sons, and daughter, Achla, and various relatives. It’s Achlar’s daughter, Vega, who got married in opulent style last week at Sun City.

title: The Paarl Paper Fire
oneLiner: Its been four years since the Paarl Paper fire killed 13 why do the families still have no answers
summary: This story has the most incredible, video footage of the fire that has never been seen. Together with the families personal stories of what happened to them – if they were injured- or their loss it will make an impactful programme together with the looking why the Dept of Labour refuses to release the findings… what is happening. It has been four years since the devastating fire that killed 13 people and injured 10 at the Paarl Print works in the Cape. For families devastated by loss, answers were needed. For factories and industrial sites answers help prevent future catastrophes of this nature but while the statutory enquiry into the fire was held and the Occupational health and Safety Act was completed in 2010. To date the findings have been released to the Dept of Labour and no-one has been held accountable. Families have no idea what happened in that fatal fire, Human Rights Lawyer Richard Spoor who is acting for the families finds the Department of Labour’s refusal to release findings inexcusable…In his many investigations into the mines there is a totally different scenario. The Mine Health and Safety Act makes the disclosure of the report of the enquiry compulsory, the Occupational Health and Safety Act (which applies to industry does not). This Richard says, is plain stupid. The Department of Labour refuses to release the report on the basis that it is confidential. This totally defeats the purpose of the enquiry which is to establish the causes, to recommend precautionary measures and to determine if any one can be held accountable.

title: Time bomb Koeberg
oneLiner: Koeberg is a time bomb waiting to happen
summary: “Koeberg, it’s a time bomb waiting to happen” says Johan Jooste, former Koeberg employee. “All maintenance should be under a magnifying glass - it’s an old facility and anything can go at any time.” Koeberg’s Nuclear plant is 25 years old and basic maintenance is not happening because Koeberg no longer has the skills internally, so all the major repair work is outsourced. Sadly the companies employed to do the work don’t always have the necessary skills either, as was illustrated when a contractor tripped the 400Kw electricity line tripping the major transformer. Jooste says that’s a basic mistake that should never have happened. It cost R14 Million in lost revenue because the plant was down for two days.

experts: Mr. Clive Le Roux Mr. Houston Carstens Mr. Michael Julie

title: Breaker Morant - The Retrial
oneLiner: History lives on, Harry “The Breaker” Morant to be re-tried after 110 years.
summary: This is a story about living history. One hundred and ten years on, the Boer War comes to life in the re-trial of Harry “The Breaker” Morant. It involves national pride and historical retribution. Nick Bleszynski was featured on Carte Blanche 10 years ago when he wrote Shoot Straight, You Bastards!: The Truth Behind the Killing of 'Breaker' Morant. Today he is in South Africa filming a documentary “Breaker Morant The Retrial”. New legal and historical evidence is at the forefront of the campaign to resolve Australia’s longest-standing military controversy, the execution of Harry Morant and Peter Handcock, who were shot 110 years ago by the British under Lord Kitchener, during the Boer War. Carte Blanche will get the opportunity to go to the National Archives in Pretoria with Nick Bleszynski and expert military lawyer Jim Unkles, as they quest to uncover crucial historical documents from the archives there. They hope the found documents will add legal weight to Colonel Sinclair’s statement that Kitchener did in fact give orders to Morant and Handcock to shoot Boer prisoners. Therefore, they should not have been court martialled for their actions. Boer descendants in South Africa are unhappy about this campaign as they fear the objective of a re-trial is to clear the name of those who murdered their ancestors.

title: Dying for Generics
oneLiner: South Africa is paying through the nose for patented medicines because SA Patent law has not been updated to protect the public from unscrupulous drug companies evergreening their products
summary: A landmark Supreme Court ruling in India earlier this month ruled that Novartis, one of the top five global pharmaceutical companies would not be allowed to extend the patent for the cancer drug Geelvec. This ruling is a massive break through and is a culmination of a high profile, seven-year legal battle. It protects the availability of cheap generic drugs for poor patients, but sadly not for South Africans. India updated its patent rules which prevents drug companies from getting monopoly protection on updated drugs that don’t represent a major advance over previous versions — a practice known as “evergreening.” The Gleevec case is the first big test of that principle. This is a major issue in South Africa and the ruling highlights the paltry state of the SA patent legislation, which is currently under review. Coincidentally Gleevec or Imatinib’s patent expires in SA this month, have SA Generic drug manufactures managed to negotiate the rights to manufacture a generic? Oncology drugs are the most expensive item for SA medical schemes and these exorbitant costs are crippling both medical schemes and the public. Treatment Action Campaign and Médecins Sans Frontières / Doctors Without Borders have been campaigning for years to get South Africa's weak patent laws revised. They are not against patented medicine, but believe the South Africa government could be doing far more to safeguard against unscrupulous pharmaceutical companies and create access to affordable generic alternatives. The insert will focus on three drugs to illustrate the issues. Imatinib or Gleevec the oncology medication which the Indian ruling pertained to. Linezolid, a drug used to treat multi-drug resistant (MDR-TB) and extremely drug resistant (XDR-TB) and Yasmin a new generation of contraceptive and the generic equivalent Ruby
