title: The Epidemic of Male Rape in Prison
oneLiner: Does anybody really care if a person is raped in prison?
summary: This story is set against a backdrop of increasing litigation against the Department of Corrections regarding rape in South African prison. The latest case to be heard is a man suing for 1.7 million rand for a jail rape that left him with HIV. He was apparently placed in a cell with known 28s gangsters with a warder shouting into the cell "Hier is die gemors" (Here is the rubbish). Historically nothing has been done to adress this issue but leading the fight to make a difference is Sasha Gear of Just Detention International. Six years ago she and other NGO's provided a paper to correctional services on how rape should be dealt with in prison. Although well received this working paper has been floating around with nothing being done. One of the reasons is because there are changes in leadership at the Department of Corrections. Whilst there have been pockets of good people within the prisons trying to do their best to curtail rape - these initiatives inevitably fall flat because they are not sanctioned by the Department of Correctional Services. Recently Sasha held a training session with concerned wardens regarding rape in prisons and these wardens admitted to her that this was the first time ever that they has been trained. There is a bigger picture obviously and we know that the majority of South Africans will say 'they deserve it'. It is for Carte Blanche to show the short sightedness of such thinking. It seems that for men to be men in prisons they have to resort to violence in order to protect themselves and of course often brutalized prisoners can express their anger when they are released back into society.

title: Oscar Chalupsky - Human Machine?
oneLiner: He's trying to win the world's toughest surf ski event in Hawaii for the 13th time - but at age 50, just how does Oscar Chalupsky beat Olmpic athletes in their prime?
summary: On May 19 Oscar Chalupsky will aim to win the brutally tou8gh Molokai Challenge in Hawaii for a record 13th time, in the year that he turns 50. Last year Oscar won the race, beating a 25 year-old Olympic paddler in a sprint finish. The Molokai is an ultra endurance event that requires surf ski paddlers to navigate a tricky 50 mile channel crossing notorious for tough sea conditions. Swell, extreme heat and variable ocean currents are just some of the challenges participants face. It is widely regarded as a de facto surfski world championships The unique angle is that it should not be physically possible for an athlete aged 50 to compete with - and even beat - endurance athletes in their physical prime. Overweight as it is, there is strong support for the fact that Oscar, who enjoys the odd beer and donut, should never be competitive. However he wins year after year. In no other sporting code are athletes in their 50s able to compete on an equal footing with athletes in their twenties. Prof Tim Noakes says Oscar is a freak of nature, and is sure that he will win it again. We accompany Oscar as he trains outside Durban, wearing three sweat suits and paddling 50kms - which he does throughout the punishing Durban summer heat. We then take him to the brand new Prime High performance sports Science Centre at the Moses Mabida stadium in Durban and put him through a battery of tests with sport scientists to work out why he is able to do what he does.
caseStudies: Oscar Chalupsky Veteran Surf skier
experts: Dr. Craig Roberts Springbok team doctor Prof. Tim Noakes

title: Low Cost Airline Carrier my ass!
oneLiner: Cheaper to fly to Thailand and back with accommodation than to fly locally.
summary: We all thought that low cost airlines was the answer to most of us who needed to fly for an urgent meeting. However its not uncommon now to pay just under R6000 for a return flight to JHB from CPT. Okay we know that 1Time and Nationwide have disappeared but this has been manna from heaven for Kalula and I guess that old adage applies - supply and demand. South Africans are really smarting at the cost of Kalula flights often these flights are full and we have to pay up to R4000 and R5000 for a one way ticket to JHB. Actually its outrageous considering the fact that the other day i saw a return flight to Thailand with 5 days accommodation being advertised for R6500. We tackle Kulula about their air prices - also mindful of the fact that one goes into business to make profits. We also speak to the major role players who are introducing two more low cost airlines into South Africa in the not too distant future. But also we look again at this disturbing phenomenon of overbooking local flights.

title: Witch villages
oneLiner: We show you the village of the damned
summary: In the hamlet of Helena, outside of Bochum, in Limpopo, those who have been accused of witchcraft are forced into exile, in peril of their lives. While South African law forbids the accusation of witchcraft, the rural areas of Limpopo abound with tales, of witchcraft, of witches being stoned, burnt, and killed. The authorities began to relocate those in danger of being accused of witchcraft to 'safe' villages of which Helena is but one. We investigate what is is like when your neighbour is your scariest nightmare

title: Collision Course (Science Discovery)
oneLiner: An asteroid strike over Russia was a chilling precursor to the devastation scientists believe could occur in just 16 years. Can we avoid oblivion?
summary: We live in the middle of a cosmic shooting gallery. There are about a million asteroids that orbit near the path of Earth. Of these, NASA has estimated that perhaps 20,000 can one day pose a direct threat to Earth. In 2012 a new consortium of EU researchers began exploring options for dealing with an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The European Commission have invested €4 million ($7 million) in the NEOShield project. Plenty of ideas are already on the table, such as deflection with projectiles or explosives and using gravity to pull it off course.

title: Food Safety
oneLiner: How dirty is our meat really, first our boerewors and now our biltong has been falsely labeled! We speak to international laywer about our rights and what we can do about food fraud
summary: The recent scandal about our meat and what's really in it has been scandalous - what has been done to ensure consumer safety when it comes to our food - and does the consumer have a leg to stand on when it comes to food fraud in the country - we speak to International attorney Bill Marler - whos's visiting South Africa for the Food Safety Network's Symposium in October. We go shopping with him - check out whether our deli's are that hygienic - find a case study - someone who got a foodborne illness and take him to the city centre where carcasses are chopped up, transported on a trolley and braai'd in the street near taxi ranks or under freeways. Should this be allowed. How dirty is our meat really?

title: WERE THE WRIGHT BROTHERS BEATEN TO POWERED FLIGHT? Myth Busted
oneLiner: For years the Wright brothers have had iconic status in aviation circlers as the first to fly i...but is this true
summary: An insert with old footage, black and white pictures, lovely over top interviews with aviation writers can have a fun way of investigating Myth Bust!!!!! In an extraordinary rewrite of history, the 100th anniversary edition of Jane's All the World Aircraft says Gustave Whitehead was the first to fly a heavier-than-air aircraft. "... more than two years before the Wrights manhandled their Flyer from its shed and flew a couple of hundred feet in a straight line..." They have now found more than 80 press articles about Whitehead's flights prior to the Wrights’ first flight. "Today, it seems impossible that a vast cache of documentary evidence, such as those newspaper reports, can be overlooked by the world at large," According to Whitehead, the machine flew a distance of half a mile for one and one-half minutes during its second test flight before crashing into a tree. In the lead up to the claimed successful 1901 flight, Whitehead also tested an unmanned and unpowered flying machine, towed by men pulling ropes, of which a good photograph exists. A witness said the craft rose above telephone lines, flew across a road and landed undamaged. The distance covered was later measured at approximately 1,000 ft. This led to the August 14 1901 flight, where Whitehead flew his No. 21 ‘Condor’ for about half a mile, and to an altitude of about 40 feet. This was over two years before the celebrated so called first flight of the Wright Brothers on December 17th 1903!

title: THE ART OF ILLUSION (Kurt Wenner - 8min)
oneLiner: Eye popping and brain boggling, Kurt Wenners 3D street art is like nothing you’ve seen before. Take a leap with us into his world of grand illusion.
summary: His art has been described as “trippy” because of the illusions he is able to create. While the surfaces he works on are all 2D, the effect is 3D. His specialty is the centuries-old practice of street painting. This tradition is supposed to have started in Italy in the 16th century, where artists would use chalk and pastel to create images on the ground. They were originally known as “Madonnari”, since many of their images were of the Madonna. Passersby would throw coins, which is how the artists would make their living. But what sets him apart from other artists who cover swaths of public space with their work is that Wenner's work is 3D. It appears to drop deep beneath the ground into another world--one often filled with characters from Greek mythology or a fairy tale. Kurt Wenner is in South Africa and has said he’ll give us an exclusive interview on the 4th April. I’ve asked him to paint a piece specifically for Carte Blanche. Besides getting to know the artist, we’ll see firsthand how he creates his larger-than-life installations and what it's like to be an artist working in the midst of a crowd. (Thinking of erecting ago-pro and recording the process from beginning to end, utilizing slow mos etc) EG of the visual devices we could use: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wR_PSSswP0c We are also going to be able to get footage of him doing international installations. title: Robohand
oneLiner: A devastating accident, a cross continental friendship and the magic of 3d printing combine to create a groundbreaking invention in the world of prosthetics.
summary: Two years agp, Richard van As, a master cabinet maker, sliced the fingers off of his dominant right hand with a circular saw. In that moment, he made a clear decision to find a way to repair his hand and continue his trade. With the severed fingers in his apron pocket, Richard began a journey into the technology of prosthetics and robotic that has resulted in device he calls robohand. Today, using 3d printing technology, Richard prints lightweight digits and is able to construct working hands for less than R11 a finger. He offers this device free of charge, happy to share what he has learnt so that others have a shot at normal functioning.

title: THE AFRICAN CHIEFS AND THE VISCOUNTS
oneLiner: A true story that has returned to haunt Zimbabwe's leadership.
summary: This is the true story about two Vickers Viscount passenger airliners that were shot down over the African jungle nearly 35 years ago, a seminal moment that contributed to the birth of a nation and why those horrific events are now embroiled in controversy. Little did the 56 holidaymakers and crew of Air Rhodesia flight RH825 know of the horror that lay in store for them when they took off from Kariba airfield, on Rhodesia’s Riviera, on a sunny September afternoon back in 1978. Forces loyal to guerilla leader Joshua Nkomo had positioned themselves beneath their flight path with a Soviet supplied Surface to Air Missile and just ten minutes into the flight they shot the plane out of the sky. Remarkably, the pilot was able to make an almost controlled landing in a field but before he could bring it to a halt it struck a ditch and cartwheeled back into the air and exploded. 38 of those on board died in the crash and subsequent fire. Miraculously, 18 people survived but their nightmare But their ordeal wasn’t over... While some of them escaped the wreckage and ran to summons help, ten more crash survivors, including children, were murdered at the scene, shot and bayonetted by the guerillas! Three survived by hiding when they saw the fighters arriving. FIVE MONTHS LATER a second Viscount was brought down in the same spot, this time all 59 on board perished.

title: The Year The Elephants Died
oneLiner: Hunting, contraception, relocation - we've heard numerous alternatives to culling elephants. But when nothing is done, as witnessed in Zimbabwe's Hwange national park, the results can be tragic.
summary: Years of drought and man's mismanagement mean that thousands of elephants and other species are dying of thirst in Hwange. We join a young film-maker - previously met while filming 'Shark fin Soup' for Carte Blanche - as he tells the story of the factors that have resulted in a situation last seen over 30 years ago in Kenya's Tsavo National Park. It's a story of searching for a solution that will help to ease the suffering of these incredible creatures - a story we tell by following a team of pump attendants in their daily battles to keep the animals alive.

title: The Cove Guardians
oneLiner: A group of South Africans have dedicated themselves to working against the dolphin slaughter at The Cove in Taiji, Japan - revealing footage never seen before, and putting their own safety at risk.
summary: Former 5fm DJ GRANT NASH has just returned from Taiji, Japan, where he campaigned against the annual slaughter of 20,000 dolphins, porpoises, and small whales. But he's not the only South African involved. The publicity surrounding the recent film of The Cove resulted in the establishment of a global campaign called The Cove Guardians - which has attracted people like former financial manager Rosie Kunneke and Nicky Botha to devote their lives to the organisation working most to save dolphins and whales from ultimate extinction - Sea Sheperd Conservation Society, the international non-profit marine conservation organization. The Cove Guardians is a global Sea Sheperd initiative, and every year they make their way to Japan to protest the slaughter - that's what it is. In this insert Grant, Rosie and Nicky share their experiences - accompanied by visuals - of being followed and threatened by police AND Japanese citizens - and explain why they do it.
caseStudies: Grant Nash Cove Guardian Rosemarie Kunneke Cove Guardian
experts: Ms. Nikki Botha Cove Guardian volunteer Mr. Paul Watson Sea Sheperd founder

title: Golden Lions Club
oneLiner: A Russian athlete and her gymnastic starts in drug ridden west of Joburg
summary: The Golden Lions gymn club in drug and gangster ridden Newlands in West Johannesburg looks like nothing much on the outside but walk through their doors and the future looks bright. Its here that a group of young gymnasts are literally soaring above the drugs and gangsterism that plague the neighborhood. Coach Natalia von Willigh, is from Russia and she has been coaching at the club for the last six years and its possible because of her background that a high premium is placed on discipline. Golden Lions is not one of those world calss high performance centres that churn out champions. It’s members don’t ring wealth and resources, but they do have incredible talent and In 2014 a selection of their gymansts will be sent to the World Gymanistic Championships- held in France. They perform at malls wherever to bring in the necessary funds. A small but impossibly sweet story about children ( aged from 5 to 20 year) of Newlands (and also from the city) who have a sanctuary, a place where hard work, discipline and the freedom of being airborne are paramount.. A story that will profile some of the gymanists, to the parents who have found an antidote to the realities of their area to the coach herself and her dreams ,the challenges she has had to train star gymnasts in the making.

title: Bloodhound Part 2
oneLiner: Land Speed Record Andy Green and how fast is fast enough
summary: Blood hound SSC the super sonic car that plans to break not only the land speed record, but also exceed the low altitude speed record for aircraft is right on track. While the car is being created back in the UK - the potential first human to reach 1600kmh on land, albeit in a car, will arrive next week. Wing Commander Andy Green, the holder of the last land speed record (at 1 228 kmh), the future Clark Kent is gearing up to hurtle down Haksteen Pan at nearly twice the speed of sound next year. “As a Royal Air Force Fighter Pilot, I like to think that I’ve got a reasonable understanding of aircraft and how they work. However, the more time I spend on Bloodhound, the more I learn about just how amazing airplanes, and fast jets in particular, really are. Bloodhound SSC is aiming to do over 1000 mph, which is faster than any aircraft – even the Royal Air Force’s latest Typhoon fighter – can travel at ground level. If we’re going to go that fast, then we’ve got to do this better than any aeroplane, and that’s a huge task.” Building a car faster than a fighter jet is an iconic adventure that will push technology to its limit. In trying to set what research suggests may be the ultimate land speed record, a team of British engineers, designers, mathematicians and technologists hope to tell a new story of science that will fascinate and inspire all those who hear it especially future generations. And Andy will be here next week as the guest of Sci Bono next week to do just that. Here in South Africa 198 schools, from the richest to the poorest have become involved in Bloodhound’s education programme, and every week they bring more schools on board, initiating projects inspired by Bloodhound. They have also launched Bloodhound Education Centre in Kimberley.
caseStudies: Andy Green Land Speed Record Holder

title: LAWLESS COPS
oneLiner: Police Brutality is out of control. It’s been a long time coming with little or no reaction from authorities. We ask why cops have been allowed to act above the law.
summary: The country is outraged following the horrific video of a Mozambican taxi driver being handcuffed and dragged behind a police van - he died as a result of his injuries later that day. Nazneen and her mother were strangled and sat on by two cops in Robertsham in December 2012 2. Bruce Swart was beaten up in front his fiancé, and two children aged 2 and 4. The intensity of the assaults and brazen attitudes of the cops has escalated dramatically. Physically abusing civilians out in the open with numerous witnesses. Cops have become a law unto themselves. The Independent Police Investigations Directorate handles cases involving police, but it seems their hands are tied and cases are taking ages to finalize. The result is that there is very little or no accountability in the police. In both our cases, the names of the officers are known to us, they are still working as policemen despite the video evidence.

title: MALAWI-SIMON'S HERITAGE RETURNED
oneLiner: 42 Years after Tony Ridgeway's grand Lake Malawi hotel was taken away from him, his son is getting it back - from the President herself
summary: Simon Ridgeway spent his childhood years in Malawi - because his father, Tony, had eloped to Africa with a young woman named Valerie. His father had worked with wildlife, and moved to Malawi after the imposition Of a severe quarantine system in the UK. After running the Blantyre Zoo - where he saved a lioness from death - he bought the Golden Sands hotel on Malawi's beautiful Cape Maclear peninsula. He became friends with the chief of the local Chembe community, being given the name of 'bwana tony'in the process. He established a trading market for the village, and then expanded the hotel, which saw a rapid growth in visitors to the area - but the roads were often washed away by the sub-tropical African storms. So Tony got the local village to help him build an air field for light transport aircraft - to bring in visitors. And they came in relative numbers. This set the scene for our narrative character, Simon Ridgeway - then a young boy - to meet 'Mr Solomon', his Dad's manager and confidant. But it was a short-lived association, as the Malawian government took Tony's hotel and land from him at independence. Having lost his three brothers, father and mother, Simon - who describes himself as an author and a poet - decided a few years ago that he now wants to return to his heritage in Malawi. After 'spending years' staring at a beautiful map of the old Lake Nyasa, with its hand painted depictions of the life he had remembered as a young boy, he has set in motion a series of events that will see President Joyce Banda hand the land back to him (with Carte blanche present). This is her statement about re-attracting investment to Malawi - a classic failed African state. The hotel may have been in ruins, but after reconnecting with 'Mr Solomon' - now 80 but in good shape - Simon is already working on his dream, with big plans for his old house and vicinity, and the rest of this life..

experts: Ms. Joyce Banda President:Malawi Mr. Mr Solomon Hotel Manager Mrs. Lovat Carnelly Lake Malawi resident

title: Green Designers
oneLiner: Meet Stephen Lamb and Andrew Lord who have turned Green exhibition design into an art form
summary: Stephen Lamb and Andrew Lord have turned exhibition design on its head. Their business “Touching the Earth Lightly” says it all, they create beautiful exhibition spaces completely out of recycled “living” material which are architecturally totally functional and aesthetically pleasing. Stephen and Andrew built the City of Cape Town's stand for the World Cup Soccer out of 1000’s of milk crates. Then they won the best design for the City of Cape Town’s COP17 stand and on the strength of that they were invited to build entrance to the Shanghai Biennale. This breathtaking entrance was created with bamboo supports that where split and fungi spores planted in them so that by the time the exhibition opened they where covered with the most beautiful orange fungi. This whole process is well documented.Go to http://www.touchingtheearthlightly.com/projects/default.asp?proj_ID=46 for images of this incredible architectural space. Their next big one is coming up this week and is the “Green Shack” which they will built at the entrance to Design Indaba - THE trendy design event on the Cape Town Calendar. Eco Designers Stephen Lamb and Andrew Lord have taken their Cape Town based sustainable architectural designs onto the world stage. Having won several local design awards for the Cop 17 Stand and the City of Cape Town Stand on the parade during the World Cup in 2010 Stephen was invited by Illac Diaz the founder of “Litre of Light” to design the entrance to the Shanghai Biennnale festival.

title: Attachment parenting
oneLiner: The woman who breastfed her 3 year old son on the cover of Time Magazine
summary: A new trend in parenting is sweeping the US and the rest of the world at the moment. It is called Attachment Parenting, and while the idea is not that new, they way it is being propagated and practiced make it quite a phenomenon. AP is the theory that says of the bonding between especially a mother and child is not deep enough and thorough enough the child could be scarred for life. And this bonding should include things like extensive breastfeeding, co-sleeping and something called baby-wearing. It is controversial, but interesting.

title: Kruger Elephant Population -" Control by Starvation"
oneLiner: We've seen culling, contraception, relocation and now starving calves to death is Kruger National Park's newest mode of population control. We tackle this issue head on
summary: According to research by SANPARKS elephants have reduced the number of top canopy trees in the Kruger Park more than 95% since the 60's. And this figure increases annually. But the scientists who are dictating the elephants management programme in the Kruger argue that this is a perception and is false. The situation is farm more complex. A couple of years ago SANPARKS did away with artificial water holes forcing the animals the animals to live close to rivers this occurred before the 'no culling' policy but instead they lowered animals by starving them to death. The plan stipulates that no animal be culled - they will be allowed to multiply doubling every 10-15 years in time stripping the riverine habits of all vegetation in order to stay alive. The elephants will be forced to walk greater distances to and from the rivers in search of food. In Botswana elephants walk 50km a day in order to find enough food to stay alive. The plan is expected to have three effects - the age that that elephants heifers will possibly increase from 12-18 years. The interval between calves will increase 4-6 years. Lactating mothers will gradually stop producing milk and their calves will not have enough energy to keep up with them in the daily trek. Mother elephants will have to make long journeys everyday in order to stay alive and so their calves will be abandoned, starve to death or attacked by predators. Scientists believe by restricting plant nutrition levels in the park through a system that staves baby elephants to death they will stabilise elephant populations they say naturally.

title: Once Upon a Town
oneLiner: Falko, A Cape Town Graffiti Artist, is giving small towns in the Western Cape facelift with a twist.
summary: In recent years Graffiti has earned it’s stripes as a recognized art form. It’s come a long way from unruly teenagers inconsiderately marking their territory by spray painting silly nicknames on private property. Today urban spaces have become canvasses for young artists creating incredible 3-D pieces with just a spraycan. Cape Town Graffiti Artist, Falko, has created a living galleries by graffiti-ing whole residential areas – giving the entire town a new funky look, ridding the community of the dreary old low cost housing units they were stuck in. Darling, Pella and Mamre are the first little “one-horseshoe” towns that have been transformed by Falko’s off the wall designs. The works have uplifted communities and are drawing tourists to these usually forgotten towns.

title: Uncovering Breasts
oneLiner: we enter the world of breasts
summary: Florence Williams is a science writer and her interest in breasts was piqued when she did a piece on toxins in breast milk because of pollutants in the environment. She decided to get her own milk tested. And found that it's packed with toxins—specifically, chemical flame retardants—that Williams is funneling directly into her baby. This sends her down a rabbit hole in search of deeper understanding of her own anatomy— into the evolutionary history of mammals, to Peru to investigate nursing and weaning, back to the first breast augmentation surgery, and all over the world to interview more boob experts than you can shake a bra at. With Florence Williams as our guide we set out to explore the strange and unexpected world of breasts. Informative, fun and entertaining. Did you know that breasts are bigger than ever? That breast milk contains substances similar to cannabis? Or that it’s sold on the internet for 262 times the price of oil? The proposal was accepted last year, but due to hurrican Sandy I could not go to the US at the time. I will be in the US in April.

title: SA Dog Breeders - Money or the Dog
oneLiner: South African dog breeders are doing it all themselves, from breeding to their own vetinary backroom practice. Puppies are sold to their new owners very sick pushing puppy costs through the ceiling
summary: This story has three very strong case studies from one Yorshire puppy breeder in Pretoria. The first case study, Jannie bought his Yorkshire puppy, Chloe last year for R6000-00 rand (indluding, registration and inoculations. However when they took Chloe home she became very ill and nearly died - their medical bills escalated to R16 000-00 after managed to save her life. At present their are two more puppies who are also very ill from the same breeders. The breeders does their own inoculations and administers medication without veterinary qualifications - completely illegal. The Vet couldn't even determine what the meds were that were given to the owners from the breeders. Jannie has taken his case to Rick Allen at the NSPCA and dept of health.

title: The Worlds toughest Mountain Bike Race
oneLiner: The word's most renowned and toughest Mountain Bike race is 10 years old, we look at the story of its peaks and problems.
summary: The Cape Epic since it started ten years ago has become the world’s premier mountain bike race. It surpasses 2500 hours of global TV hours to become the most televised mountain bike race of all time. It’s a race that’s challenges the world’s fastest mountain bike riders across some of the most rugged and remote terrain. But how got to be so renowned has been an epic in itself and the result of one man’s driving force. South African, Kevin Vermaak’s passion is mountain biking and before the Cape Epic he had ridden on mountain ranges in all four corners of the globe but the landscape that truly inspired him was South Africa’s vast tracts of untouched wilderness and mountain ranges. It was whilst he was living in London that he came up with the idea to create an ‘ Untamed African Mountain Bike Race’ a race in which every serious amateur mountain biker desires to participate and every professional mountain biker aspires to win. This for Kevin - despite the cliché – is a dream come true. CONT BELOW

title: A story of survival
summary: More people have been to the moon than people completing the adventure Davey du Plessis took on to attempt a solo Source to Sea journey of the Amazon in July last year. His journey was divided in three parts: a hike to the 18 000ft Mount Mismi, a 800-km cycle through the Andean mountains, following the Amazon river's main tributary - the Apurimac and a 5700km kayak paddle downstream towards the sea in Brazil. He successfully completed the first two stages and was halfway in the third when he was shot 22 times with a pellet gun by two youngsters on the bank of the river. Having done no other television interviews about his story of survival, he wants to share this with us.
caseStudies: Davey Du Plessis Adventurer Robyn Wolff Davey du Plessis's mother

title: Obesogens
summary: In 2010 GlaxoSmithKline conducted a survey and found that 61% of South African's are overweight. Apart from lack of exercise, and a poor diet there may be another reason for our increasing waist lines. Prof Bruce Blumberg is a developmental biologist at the University of California, Irvine. He conducted a study exposing mice to Endocrine Disruptive Chemicals (EDC) at birth. With no genetic difference,raised in the same lab and given the same food and chance to exercise. The mouse that was exposed to the EDC's was considerably fatter than the normal test mouse.

title: Darwin Doubters shunned
oneLiner: Described as the "Shocking Truth about killing careers of Darwin Doubters" Dr Bergman documents the strategies anti-Christians use to suppress intellectual freedom in universities.
summary: If Ben Stein's 2008 documentary film Expelled: No Intelligence Allowed was the tip, then Dr. Jerry Bergman's Slaughter of the Dissidents is the rest of the iceberg. With clarity and thoroughness, Bergman provides detailed accounts of 17 of the over 300 scientists and educators he has interviewed, all of whom have advanced degrees. Though their views range from creation science to intelligent design to evolution, all of them expressed some doubt regarding neo-Darwinism, observing that selection of mutations is not creating life's diversity. And all of them have received some form of discrimination. Dr. Bergman has observed that evolutionary elitists incorrectly lump all "Darwin Doubters" into one group, "creationists," who are then categorically ridiculed. Though highly qualified, these scientists and educators are verbally and physically threatened, lose privileges, lose opportunities for promotion, and lose jobs and whole careers, just for expressing some measure of doubt about the standard evolutionary story.

title: Teaspoon Slide Guitarist - Hannes Coetzee
oneLiner: How does a man from Mossel Bay that plays guitar with a teaspoon land up being nominated for a Grammy Award - for his tune called "Chocolate Drops"
summary: Mossel Bay's Hannes Coetzee has been nominated for a Grammy Award at the age of 69 for a number called "Chocolate Drops". Described as humble and kind, a man that lives for his music, Coetzee's song Mahalla went viral on You Tube and in no time - he plays his guitar in what is called a 'pick-up and pinch' style sliding out a melody with a teaspoon in his mouth. He has played with David Kramer at the Karoo Kitaar Blues - now everyone is hoping that the album will be a Grammy winner at the awards in about two weeks time on the 10 February.

title: All fired up
oneLiner: As bloody violence and anarchy erupts in Sasolburg we look at the political engineering and corruption that has fuelled the strikers.
summary: As the stakes get higher it seems the violence intensifies as politicians stake their claims in municipal areas. This week the people of Sasolburg took to the streets to fight against their municipality being incorporated into Parys. Their main concern is corruption and a lack of service delivery which they believe will make impact on their own living conditions. They say ANC Stalwart Ace Magashule is behind the move. The rumour in Zamdela (Sasolburg) is that because Sasolburg municipality has more money than Parys, Magashule plans to put his family and friends in charge of stuff in the enlarged muncipality with ostensibly more money available and the ability to move people to the top of housing lists and tenders, for example. People in Sasolburg don't like Ace. That seems to be at least one of the reasons they are so angry. Also, government should have learned from the same kind of thing around Carletonville and the Gauteng borders previously. The people in this area have come to certain conclusions that drives the anger and violence. To them it's totally rational given their lack of real power and that no one seems to listen. But is it all conclusions or is the anger fueled by political agendas of people who stand to loose cash cows? Also, Zamdela is one of the many hotspots of resistance from the 1980s where this kind of protest is still seen as the only way to get people to listen. These strikes it appears are because people have had enough. They have reached a boiling point and their tolerance levels are at all time low. We need to try and get in on some action and then also explore the reasons, political and social, that are catalysts in the strike.
caseStudies: Papi Mafubedu Parys Community leader Sandile Msibi Municipal manager Parys
experts: Mr. Ace Magashule ANC Mr. Community leaders Sasolburg Mr. Dept Local Government

title: I Dreamed A Dream - Les Miserable's South African connection
oneLiner: We bring you the story of the Kroonstad boy who's just won big with Les Miserables at the Golden Globes and is expected to be collecting an award at the Oscars...
summary: Herbert Kretzmer was born in Kroonstad. Arriving in London via Paris and New York - as an entertainment journalist - he wrote the English lyrics for Les Misérables. The world’s longest-running musical, and having already won a Golden Globe - it's tipped to do well at the Oscars. Kretzmer's song - Suddenly - is in line for 'Best Original Song'. We speak to Kretzmer at his London apartment asap - with a supporting interview cast of London West End afficianados and / or local critic Barry Ronge lending testament to Kretzmer's quiet talent. We could add a supporting interview with Susan Boyle, the unglamorous Scottish singer who became an overnight sensation with her rendition of I Dreamed A Dream - in so doing reinventing an already remarkable musical. Or we could make it a bit broader, as seen below in suggested treatment of 'Option 2' below.
caseStudies: Herbert Kretzmer Songwriter
experts: Mr. UK Musical Afficianado Mr. Barry Ronge Film Critic Ms. Susan Boyle Singer Mr. Wayne Thronley Director 'Zambezia'

title: Zambezi Wave
summary: About 1000km inland and a short distance from Victoria Falls, lies a hidden natural wave that breaks only twice a year depending on rainfall in the Zambezi's tributaries. One of the world's most experienced Kayak adventurers South African-born Steve Fisher discovered the wave on his travels on the Zambezi almost 15 years ago. Steve himself, just completed a death-defying adventure to conquer the rapids of the Inga River in the Congo - the largest river in Africa. Steve will be taking professional surfers including South Africa's No.1 Jordy Smith, American Jamie O'Brien and local junior champion Michael February up to surf the wave. Jordy Smith released his first DVD last year called 'Bending Colours' and is set the world tour alight this year with his aerial flai and hopefully attain his first world title after coming runner-up (to surf legend Kelly Slater) in 2010. The wave only breaks twice and year and there are many variables determining when the wave will break. We've named the project Nyaminyami - the name of the Tonga Zambezi River god who controls life in and on the river.

title: Uranium Teeth
summary: In 2007 I produced a story on the Wonderfontein Spruit, and it's contamination due to heavy metals from the gold mining industry. Part of the focus of the story was the uranium rich water and the risk it posed to people who lived along the waterways and depended on the water. For the first time in South Africa, we tested cabbages that were grown using water from the Spruit near Potchefstroom and they were found to have uranium in them.

title: Tweeting - Legal and Illegal
oneLiner: What you didn't know about tweeting.
summary: Facebook, Tweeting , Instagrams …. Whilst social media in a sense have freed up communication with it has come a sense of annonymity the tweeter etc feels they can say annything, however controversial without repercussions. How wrong they are. We explore with case studies the personal and professional ethics and legalities of social media. How what you tweet can have you fired or sued or even jailed.
caseStudies: Emma Sadler

title: I failed matric, but how?
oneLiner: With disctinctions and high grade through out gr 12, but a matric certificate that indicates three subjects and therefore matric was failed...How is that possible and who needs to take responsibility?
summary: With the majority of 2012's matrics already starting their new lives and enrolling at universities across the country, a group of 713 matrics dreams are shattered. After achieving distinctions or very high grades through out 2012, many have failed their main subjects or are indicated on their final marks as being absent when the specific subject was written. This group of learners studied matric through the home schooling organisation "Impak" - the largest home schooling supplier in South Africa, with more than 5000 learners. Impak provides parents with the products and services to educate their children at home or at an Impak learning centre, from gr.0 to gr.12. Impak has contact with the National Department of Education's Coucil for quality assurance - Umalusi - through a third party - SACAI (South African Comprehensive Assessment Institute). SACAI is responsible for administering and monitoring the gr 12 Impak-learners, as well as sending the learners' year marks to Umalusi. These year marks count 25% of the final mark. And this is where it seemed to have gone all wrong.
caseStudies: Biancha Greer 2012 Gr 12 learner Michael Greer Biancha Greer's father Marcelle Mattheys Impak 2011 Gr 12 learner Maggie Mattheys Parent and Impak learning centre headmaster
experts: Mr. Stefan Botha CEO: Impak Mr. Gustav Niebuhr SACAI Director Mr. Lucky Ditaunyane Umalusi: Coomunications Manager

title: Baby Born Without Ears
summary: Naleyah Tibbetts is 6 months old and was born with out ears. Not only does she not have outer ears, but her inner and middle ears did also not develop. In the middle of the year she will have an operation to become the youngest recipient of an auditory brain stem implant in South Africa performed by South African doctors.

title: White Farmer Brutality
oneLiner: Justice for Flippie
summary: In 2010 a colored man worked for a prominent farmer Johnny Burger in Roberston. He gave two weeks notice because he wanted to go and work elsewhere. When he finished that two weeks he asked to be paid. Instead he was assaulted by the farm owners (two brothers). At the time of the assault - witnessed by his one son and wife - his other 15-year-old son arrived having come back from school in a bus. The farmers brutally assaulted this boy by ramming his head into a wine tank and then throwing him into the wine tank. It took a couple of days before the parents could get him to hospital to treat swelling in his brain. Just prior to that (i.e. after the attack) he started to develop seizures. There was more drama to follow because at the hospital there were complications. There are reports that a student doctor operated but the net result was that Flippie become blind. He has been suffering epileptic fits every day since leaving hospital and being blind as well he fell into a fire which resulted in both his hands having to be surgically removed. Three times this poor family tried to report the matter to the police. Twice the farmers were interviewed and police told the family that they would lose any case. In addition the farmer gave R5000 to the eldest son to say that the farmer did not assault Flippie. That boy is willing to tell the truth now about the bribe. The cold facts are that we have a boy who's life for all intensive purposes is over because of a brutal attack by a farmer which went unpunished. Carte Blanche investigates and helps bring justice for Flippie by putting on pressure on the police and the NPA to re-open this case.

title: Does your face tell a story?
oneLiner: Ever thought those wrinkles on your face that you hate so much are just a sign that you are aging?
summary: "All of these lines across my face; Tell you the story of who I am; So many stories of where I've been; And how I got to where I am...", sings Brandi Carlile. And these words seem to ring true if one starts to talk about Physiognomy, or face profiling. The lines, structures and shapes on a face - the deep wrinkle next to your mouth, the shape of your eyes or your forehead, how your eyebrows are shaped - represent aspects of our personalities. Our faces change according to the changes which manifest in our personality. Changes in our personalities will affect the appearance in our facial features and changes on the outside (physical change to appearance like plastic surgery, scars will affect the personality. Your face is divided into different sections and each section represents aspects of your personality and shows some of your preferences.
caseStudies: Derek Watts Carte Blanche presenter Juanita Du Plessis Singer Chad le Clos Olympic swimmer Marilyn Ramos Miss SA 2012
experts: Ms. Marthie Mare Face Profiler

title: What are the police hiding?
oneLiner: What are the police hiding?
summary: The incidents of mob justice in Khayelitsha is disturbing to say the least. Horrific images are broadcast around the world. The Social Justice Coalition NGO persuaded Helen Zille to institute a commission of inquiry in an attempt to try and find out the reasons behind these dreadful killings and it seems that culprit no. 1 is the South African Police who seems to be completely ineffectual in the townships. People call for the police when somebody has been raped and the police dont respond and the frustration of the community boils over and hence the mob justice. But the national police commisioner did not like the idea of his police being under the spotlight at a commission of inquiry and took on Helen Zille in the high court believing it was unconstitutional for Zille to include the police in such a commision. Bear in mind that this is the first time that a province has set up a commission of inquiry. Not surprisingly and probably many millions of rands later, the police lost in the high court this morning (14/01/2013) and the delayed commission of inquiry can now go ahead.

title: Recycled Loo Water
oneLiner: Plastic, glass and tin products are soon to be joined with a natural resource - our drinking water. Within the next few years Capetonians will be drinking recycled loo-water
summary: Durban and Cape Town residents will have to start looking seriously at drinking recycled water from the local sewage works within the next few years. Water supplies are running out and there is not enough time to build big new dams. Gauteng would also have to start diluting large volumes of acidic mine water within the next three years to avoid unacceptable pollution of the Vaal River system. While it was technically feasible to desalinate sea water to solve the shortage in these cities, the cost of desalinated water was around R12 per kilolitre, whereas recycling domestic effluent to tap water quality cost about R7 per kilolitre. The conference is investigating and promoting the recycling of domestic and industrial waste-water into drinking quality tap water in the 30th most water-stressed country in the world. Durban: 2 years to go. A government water planning graph suggests that Durban would need to start using some recycled water within the next two years, despite construction of the new Spring Grove Dam near Mooi River. Gauteng would face similar pressure to reuse more effluent as it would cost about R17/Kl to transfer water from the uMzimvubu River in the Eastern Cape or R35/Kl from the Zambezi River.

title: Vineyards are blazing
oneLiner: Violent strike action has again erupted on Western Cape farms - farmers say the strikers are not their workers - so who is behind it?
summary: Temperatures are rising and attitudes hardening in the sleepy hollow of De Doorns, a small table grape and wine farming settlement in the Western Cape, hemmed in by mountains. As the violence of striking workers intensifies and spreads, farmers allege their workers face increasing intimidation from the strikers. But where did the volence erupt and why?
caseStudies: Phillip Jonker Wine and Grape Farmer Oubaas van Zyl farmer Farm workers De Doorns area
experts: Mr. Gerard Van Rensburg MEC Agriculture Mr. Tony Erenreich Cosatu Ms. Sikule Sonke Woman on Farms

title: Goodsnet Trading Scam
oneLiner: They sold cut rate electronics, lured their victims and then ran off with hundreds of thousands of rands.
summary: This is a classic scam. Two businessmen from Alberton Mark Calvin and Clevelin Dunn cashed in on the growing demand for electronic goods. They recruited sales people to work from home selling these goods which they claimed to get through a contact at Massmart for half price. Robyn Fischer's children go to the same soccer club as Clevlin's children. He asked her if she'd be interested to buy some cheap electronic goods and she bought a couple of items. These were promptly delivered and she was hooked. He asked her to act as an agent and she started taking orders totally R649 000. But none of the goods materialised and Clevelin stopped taking her calls. We she started asking around she found many other people in the same boat and when they contacted Massmart they said there was no deal with Mark and Clevelin. Some of the disgruntled clients and sales people hired a private investigator who has dug up years of dirt on the duo and their dodgy deals dating back to 2004. In November Clevelin resigned as a director of Goodsnet (the co the two registered together) and shortly thereafter he was arrested on charges dating back to a labour issue in 2006. Mark continues to run the Goodsnet office from home in Albertong along with his sideline company - which bizarrely does debt collecting! Disgruntled clients who have lost millions have started a facebook page: Goodsnet Trading Scam.
caseStudies: Robyn Fischer former sales person Tersia Loe
experts: Mr. Theuns Jonker PI Mr. Massmart Forensics team Mr. Mark Calvin ALLEGED FRAUDSTER

title: Rogue Broker
oneLiner: A rogue broker has stolen millions, been disbarred and had judgements against him - how does he keep slipping through the judicial net?
summary: Frank McCarter and his wife are one of many investors who received bad advice from rogue financial adviser Andre van der Merwe. In 2008 the McCarters were advised by Van der Merwe to invest their life savings into Garek and a Sharemax-promoted syndication. Both schemes failed. McCarter laid a complaint against Van der Merwe with the Fais Ombud Noluntu Bam. The Ombud ruled in McCarter’s favour on November 4 2010. Van der Merwe was ordered to pay McCarter R660 000 with interest of 15.5%, beginning from October 2008. Van der Merwe failed to comply with the ruling. In fact, Van der Merwe has treated the Ombud and other regulators with contempt. Despite losing his Financial Services Board licence in 2009, Van der Merwe has continued to peddle unlisted shares in worthless companies. See: Garek broker unfazed, unrepentant. McCarter’s difficulties in enforcing the Ombud’s ruling may be a common theme for other victims of bad advice.
caseStudies: Frank and Adeline McCarter Victims of fraudster
experts: Mr. Noluntu Bam FAIS Ombudsman

oneLiner: A rogue broker has stolen millions, been disbarred and had judgements against him - how does he keep slipping through the judicial net?

title: BURRY STANDER (Topical)
oneLiner: Last week top cyclist, Burry Stander, was killed by a taxi. The tragedy has pitted cyclists, who want new laws, against authorities and motorists who say cyclists also need to take responsibility.
summary: Burry is just one in a list of cyclist killed on our roads in the past months. • Vuyani Havi was knocked down and killed just 2 days after Standers death while riding with 2 friends in Port Elizabeth. The driver of the vehicle had no driver’s licence. • Last year father and daughter cyclists Charie and Lauren Van Heerden were run over by a taxi on Fields Hill in Durban. They were not killed, but both suffered serious injuries. The driver got a R 500 fine • 14 year old Michael Ramsay had his head crushed by a truck that ran him over during a cycle race in hillcrest. They driver received a R 5000 fine and a year in prison, that was suspended. • Two years ago, another leading South African cyclist, Carla Swart, died when she was hit by a truck while training in the Free State. There are at least another 5 in Durban.

title: The Underground World of Johannesburg Graffiti
oneLiner: On Carte Blanche tonight... is it vandalism, or art? We expose the secret, underground life of the graffiti artist.
summary: You see it everywhere, on side walks, on walls, on bridges and highways, sometimes it looks just plain ugly and annoying because it's vandalism, but other times you may stop in awe and wonder at who may have created it and even give that bit of credence and say, that is a good artist. It's graffiti and it has become a symbol of city landscapes all over the world. Each city has it's own legends and characteristic graffiti. We have the unique opportunity to go underground with some of Johannesburg's top graffiti artists and experience with them, what it means to be a graffiti artist. What they are trying to say with their art, what is their message - if any; what it means in their social group and why they do it. They have footage of their 'bombings' (which is when they go out at night and paint and tag) and some of their experiences, which they will give to us. We will interview them after a night of 'bombing' and they will give us a first hand account of their expeditions into the dark and their lifestyle. There is the obvious controversy which rages of art versus vandalism, and we will explore this through the graffitists. Many of these 'artists' have a day job and they lead dual lives. One of the respectable - and the other of the rebel: creating, defacing, trying to become notorious in this underground world. Some have achieved respectability as legitimate graffiti artists and have moved to the world of legal graffiti, but often in amongst their peers they are seen as sell outs, even if they were once revered, because the illegal graffiti artists will tell you that there is something about illegal graffiti that makes it exciting, it puts you on the margins of society, it allows you to protest and have your say and make statements that would not otherwise be relevant. They like the role of the social outcast.
caseStudies: Reaper aka Big R illegal graffiti artist Cose 27 illegal graffiti artist Mars illegal graffiti artist Taps illegal and legal graffiti artist Tripz illegal graffiti artist EDK crew illegal graffiti crew
experts: Mr. Ryza Legal graffiti artist Mr. Rasty Legal graffiti artist

title: Graffiti Art Activist
oneLiner: From the back streets and alleys Graffiti comes to the fore and one of the top art activists of this kind is South African Rikki Lee Gordon
summary: Rikkie Lee Gordon aka FreddySam is an art activist, who was named in the wrap up of 2013 as one of the world’s 10 graffitti artists to watch (a list that includes the iconic, English, Banksey whose works of political and social commentary have been featured on streets, walls, and bridges in cities throughout the world and came to fame in the award winning documentary ‘Exit through the Gift Shop’) . Rikki or FreddySam’s been profiled on CNN and National Geographic -incredibly visual inserts showing his artwork all over the streets of Cape Town, Baltimore and Chicago. Ricky has painted on the streets of Istanbul, Morocco, Berlin, Basel, Barcelona, Amsterdam and even the Transkei. He lives in the gritty, creative suburb of Woodstuck Cape Town and just by walking the streets you can see building size examples of his art all over -some very street art others awe- inspiringwork …..it’s every where on warehouse, the flyovers, deserted buildings crumbling walls. Rikki aka FreddySam: “ I choose to paint murals because I want the man in the street to enjoy my work.” This is a programme where we will integrate the emergence of graffitti as a commercial art form, the social work Rikki does in communities , with some of his international work, woven into a walk in the streets ofWoodstuck where his graffitti is all over, highly visual, young and new.
caseStudies: Rikki Lee Gordon Graffiti Artist

title: Upset in Potch
oneLiner: Ptoch may be a sleepy North West town but its politics is anything but as a new Mayor is elected in the middle of the night.
summary: Midnight in Potchefstroom. Ex Rector of Potch university and DA councillor Annette Combrink is as surprised as the ANC that she nabbed the position of Mayor by a single point in a midnight standoff in Potchefstroom. Now her challenge will be to stay in and try and clean up the municipality. But the next couple of months may be rocky as she will likely have to survive a further vote of no confidence by the ANC who are startled by the events of 22 November.
caseStudies: terence Mombe Auditor General

title: Zama Zamas in the City of Gold
oneLiner: Zama-Zamas - in search of eGoli's riches
summary: As the era of gold on the Witwatersrand enters its twilight years, the big players are easing out. Yet much gold remains hidden under the litter-strewn streets and patches of veld that dot the reef. This earthly treasure has drawn prospectors, from across Southern Africa and beyond to take their chances. Some break through the concrete of the urban jungle to follow seams of pitifully meagre gold, and others risk their lives to enter the now closed and flooded shafts of defunct mines. These are the new pioneers, the men who live in hovels and under tree roots, to find the gold that made eGoli. We speak to these prospectors about their dreams of striking it rich, of survival and of their backgrounds. These are linked to footage of them working, with the backdrop of Johannesburg and other reef towns; and of how they survive, when police want to arrest them and tsotsis want top steal the little they garner..

title: Bizos' Last Great Show
oneLiner: George Bizos Marikana Commission
summary: Veteran human rights lawyer, George Bizos, will bring sixty years of experience to bear in the marathon commission of inquiry ino the Marikana Massacres as he tries to prevent a police cover-up of the shooting of over 122 striking miners.

title: Foced Marriages - Ukuthwala
oneLiner: Girls as young as thirteen are forced into marriage called Ukuthwala tradition or an excuse by parents to sell their children
summary: Bergville, KwaZulu-Natal - Twenty-two girls in the Bergville district in KwaZulu-Natal were abducted and forced into marriage in a practise known as ukuthwala according to a report on Saturday. The Weekend Witness reported that this was revealed in an investigation conducted by the Commission for Gender Equality (CGE). The CGE on Friday hosted a debate on ukuthwala in Durban and presented its findings, including how various government departments responded to ukuthwala. The CGE's Nomusa Kunene said the probe identified certain areas as ukuthwala hotspots. She had heard of one case where a 13-year-old was abducted and tied to a tree to prevent her escaping from her prospective 'husband'. Kunene said some religious groups saw the practise as a measure against the spread of HIV, because it promoted early marriage. Some parents were complicit as they viewed their girl children as “cash cows” because they wanted money or cattle in exchange for their daughters' forced marriages. CGE researcher Taryn Powys said: “We should not confuse the traditional practice of ukuthwala with the criminal activities being perpetrated by young men and the parents of young girls who force them to marry... “This is a crime, pure and simple”. - Sapa

title: The Hunts off in Botswana
oneLiner: Botswana's president has recently announced that trophy hunting will be banned in a years time. They say that hunting goes against preservation of flora & fauna but hunters are having a fit
summary: Botswana to ban trophy hunting. President Khama has announced that hunting will stop in Botswana.President Khama of Botswana has announced that Botswana will ban trophy hunting by 2014. In his 2012 State of the Nation Address, the President of Botswana, Lt. Gen. Ian Khama, announced that Botswana will stop commercial hunting of wildlife in public areas from 2014. Wildlife Extra, and no doubt thousands of others, applaud President Khama and, as a result, we encourage as many people to visit Botswana as possible. Part of the State of the Nation address, given on 5th November 2012, stated: "Of additional concern is the rise in cross border and domestic poaching incidents and trafficking of live predators, which are the subject of our new and evolving National Anti-Poaching Strategy. At the same time we have reached the decision to stop the commercial hunting of wildlife in public areas from 2014 as the shooting of wild game purely for sport and trophies is no longer compatible with our commitment to preserve local fauna as a national treasure, which should be treated as such." Botswana Kills Trophy Hunting - Ian Michler reflects Predictably, many hunting outfits and hunters are up in arms, and many of them seem to think, (from studying their blogs etc) that some hunting will continue, especially for elephant as they are so numerous. They also believe that it will be a dark day for wildlife as poaching will take over and wipe out much of the game. Reading between the lines, the statement above says that hunting will be banned in ‘public areas', which we assume includes the Okavango Delta, Chobe & Kalahari National Parks etc.

title: JPO in Crisis
oneLiner: Should a City be responsible for their Orchestra
summary: The Johannesburg Philharmonic Orchestra will be closing its doors unless it gets an urgent injection of funding. The JPO is the successor to the National Philharmonic which folded in 2000 ( when SABC could no longer afford it), and while it wasn't easy the new orchestra managed cutting costs by employing musicians on a seasonal basis and keeping to a tight budget. In 2006, Shadrack Bokaba became MD and times were good corporate funding and sponsorships and the in 2010 they got the lottery funding a three year commitment to the tune of 46 million rands. Now with the Lotto not committing to a further injection of cash and the JPO running at a serious loss this lost year with international and first rate local musicians not being paid, their permanent staff having had no salaries since August the JPO will have to face the music and and possibly close its doors. It is a fact that Orchestras around the world do not rely on ticket sales for their survival, instead more often than not on company funding and corporate sponsorship but the accusation is that the JPO has relied too heavily on the Lotto that the JPO needs to tighten its belt to survive. Is a city of world class without a world class orchestra? Why does Cape Town and Durban cities fund their orchestra and not JHB,?
caseStudies: Shadrack Bokaba MD JPO

title: AVIATION ALERT
oneLiner: Trouble is brewing in the South African Civil Aviation Authority. So much so that by next year we might have to travel by ship to the UK and the USA.
summary: The CAA have are losing ground in aviation circles fast after two years of dodgy decision making and a concerning a lack of qualified and experienced inspectors and managers.

title: Patrick's Personal Walk to Freedom
oneLiner: A film school whose own hero to zero stories are made for the big screen
summary: Lighting Gaffer Patick Vrieslaar’s employment on the set of the international feature film ‘ Long Walk to Freedom might have been his crowning achievement in terms of his career but it was also at times a little too close for comfort! Why? Because in the shooting of Mandela’s Robbin Island years the Prison cell, prison courtyard and surrounding cell block were painstakingly rebuilt at the Cape Town Studios, bringing back memores of Patrick’s former home for 7 years. Patrick is a former Pollsmoor prison inmate whose zero to hero story is one of the many success stories of F.I.L.M- the Film Industry Learner Mentorship- which was born in 2005, when the burgeoning feature film industry saw the need for a coordinated industry skills development platform providing disadvantaged trainees with hands-on experiential learning on feature film productions under mentorship. Seton Bailey, with a small team, runs this non profit programme which in its seven years has given hundreds of people a new start in all aspects of the film industry from commercials right through to electronic and digital media, training them as gaffers, sound engineers, production grips etc. They have their fair share of inspiring stories – the stuff which movies are made. Like Hajra Cassim, who from having nothing, stepped on to the international stage last year, in Geneva winning the Not-For Profit Digital Innovation Award at the ITU Telecom 2011 Conference – She brought a camera and edit suite with the prize money and is directing (She recently directed the hugely successful Let’s Talk Mental social media campaign www.letstalkmental.co.za )

title: The Green energy showdown
oneLiner: As energy costs rise and water dwindles a report paints a damning picture of South Africas future.
summary: Recently Greenpeace activists were arrested for picketing outside Megawatt Park to force the power utility to use more alternative and green energy sources. Thats because of the cost they see us paying down the line if we don't - esspecially when it comes to our water resouces. An environmental report has found that the use of water in electricity production is having a negative impact on the water resources for the country and may have long-term detrimental effects. The Water Hungry Coal: Burning South Africa's water to produce electricity report produced by environmental organisation Greenpeace argues that the use of coal to produce electricity has resulted in an unsustainable outlook for South Africa's water. "Ironically, burning coal to produce electricity is an incredibly water intensive process, with a number of serious implications for both water quantity and quality," Greenpeae said. The Greenpeace report indicated the new power stations could have a serious negative impact on water availability. "If new coal-fired power stations are built, this will reduce the availability and quality of South Africa's water, create stranded assets in the form of coal-fired power stations with limited or no water availability, while also accelerating climate change, which in turn will reduce water availability," the report says.
caseStudies: Mandla and Loren living off grid
experts: Ms. Kirsten Olsen Wits researcher Mr. Brian Dames Eskom Mr. Kumi Naidoo Greenpeace Mr. Representative Dept of Water Affairs

title: Corpses on display -- plastination in Cape Town
oneLiner: an exhibtion of human corpses has just opened inCape Town. Any onjections?
summary: Dr. Gunther von Hagens has devised a way to plastinate human bodies so that they can be dissected and put on display. The exhibition has just opened in Cape Town and is an amazing way of experiencing the human body. More than 13 000 people, including many South Africans have donated their bodies for future plastination. But some religious organizations have objected. We see what the fuss is all about and how South Africans feel about corpses on display. It is quite controvertial and has been criticised. Others say it is fabulous and a once in a life time experience. We investigate
caseStudies: Nokuzola Mndende Nabeweya Malick
experts: Ms. Donovan Wilson

title: National Department of Water Affairs dams up payment
oneLiner: Why has the National Derpartment of Water Affairs not paid a small service provider the millions it owes this company 20 months down the line?
summary: When the Minister of Water Affairs, Edna Molema, proclaims on national television that the department of water affairs follows a strict 30-day payment policy to its service providers, it begs the question as to why a small service provider whose company organised a Water Week carnival has not been paid in 20 months? Business-owner and entrepreneur, Billy-Guy Bhembe from Black Child Productions is owed R7.4 million for the carnival he organised in March 2011. Promises and apparent commitments from the department to pay him turned out to be false. He is now suing the department for the money. Three small service providers he used had to close their doors due to the non-payment.
caseStudies: Billy-Guy Bhembe Owner: Black Child Productions
experts: Mr. Pat Twala MD: ERWAT Mr. Mava Scott DWA: Chief Director Communications

title: James Bond for a Day
oneLiner: "Watts, Derek Watts"
summary: Derek - James Bond for a Day Skyfall , the twenty third movie in the James Bond Series, which celebrates it’s 50th anniversary of the series which started in 1962 with Dr No, will be released in South Africa in November. There is huge media hype. Already the sale of “Bond type” suits has increased at Asda in England. Navy and pinstripe suits are up 68% and ties up 76% in the wake of the suave Bond look. Not ground breaking journalism (which I have come to be known for – NOT), a light look at being “James Bond for a day with Derek. We could find a car for him, teach him to mix the perfect martini, shoot like James Bond, dress like James Bond, practise saying “Watts, Derek Watts”. Tail a car, do surveillance with high tech surveillance gear, learn a martial art/self defence or find a stunt double for him. Set up a stunt? Then there is the question of the leading ladies……

title: How full are our Pantries - Are SA Household's food insecure
oneLiner: What is the state of South Africa's Pantries - are they half full, half empty or bare?
summary: South Africa is over-dependent on markets and retailers for its food needs, Agriculture Minister Tina Joemat-Pettersson said on Tuesday.Addressing the National Assembly during a debate on the effectiveness of food production schemes, the minister said that when this system failed it resulted in food insecurity, specifically at household level. Food security remained a problem, specifically in rural and peri-urban areas, where unemployment and poverty rates were high. “While food prices have generally increased, it remains an anomaly that a basket of basic foodstuffs in rural areas is more expensive than in urban areas.” Joemat-Pettersson said that while as a country, South Africa was food secure, millions of poor households could not say the same. “We produce enough food, but it does not always get to where it is needed, or at a price that can be afforded by those who are unemployed or on social grants.” She told MPs food production schemes, such as school and community gardens, and co-operative production schemes, were the best solution for poor communities. “They are effective in terms of growing food, which is the first priority, but also effective in creating work and even local markets.” She praised the Food Bank SA for preventing food from being dumped, and for ensuring it reached the poor. She blamed labour unrest for soaring food prices. “When prices rocket because food is transported long distances, and even held hostage to violent labour action, we all suffer, but the poor suffer the most because they spend the highest proportion of their small income on basic foodstuffs.” Joemat-Pettersson deviated from her written speech to attack the opposition and the media. She said they would never be allowed to “run the agenda of transformation in agriculture”.

title: Testing the Limits
oneLiner: With proposed new legislation slashing the levels of drinking and driving in half yet again we test how much our viewers can consume.
summary: MOTORISTS will need to keep a much closer eye on what they drink if government’s proposed amendment to the National Road Traffic Act is passed. The Transport Department wants to cut the current legal alcohol limit for motorists by more than half – dropping it from 0.05g to 0.02g of alcohol per 100ml of blood, and the breathalyser limit from 0.24 to 0.10mg per 1 000ml. The proposal also calls for a zero-alcohol limit for taxi, bus and truck drivers, as well as for drivers who have had their driver’s licence for less than a year. We ask our 4 presenters (or 4 viewers) of varying sizes to put the new proposal to the test to see how much they could consume before hitting the limit.

title: Sangomas and sick notes

summary: Johannah Mmelodi applied for unpaid leave for a month because she was tormented by her ancestors who wanted her to attend a Sangoma course for a month. The employers declined the application, but Johannah nevertheless went away for a month, but submitted a sick note by a traditional healer who diagnosed her with “perminisions from the ancestors”, and booked her off for a month. Her employers dismissed her when she returned, but last Thursday in a landmark ruling the Labour Appeals Court ruled in Johannah’s favour, effectively legitimizing sick notes by Sangomas. It is a legal can of worms.

Candice has agreed to spend time with us in New York – to get to know the woman she has become and what it takes to make it in world of high fashion. She is keen to show us her favorite places in the city and give us an idea of what her day to day life is like.

title: Warning Bells
oneLiner: Politicians and economists are all sounding the alarm - they say our dream rainbow nation is in jeopardy if we don't put on the brakes and take action.
summary: This week the Economist published an article called Over the Rainbow in which they claimed SA was going backwards due largely to a failure in leadership. These sentiments were echoed by former President Thabo Mbeki during a speech made at Fort Hare University on Friday. Jacob Zuma has come out defending himself and his government but it seems the facts may get in the way of his arguments. From a global standpoint it seems the world is watching and they are not happy with what is happening in our country. Moodys, an international credit agency cut SA's sovereign rating recently citing a declining government, growing social stresses and worsening investment conditions. Marikane is seen as a turning point in our democracy and in our country's history - its symptomatic of a deep seated malaise and it may spark the African equivalent of the Arab Spring according to analysts. Now as we approach Mangaung the discontent within civil society is reaching boiling point and according to some politicians and economists its just a matter of time till we reach boiling point. Using the upswell in civil society as a hook we piece together analysis on the way forward, issuing a warning to government that if they don't act it may be too late. Carte Blanche hosts a meaningful and intelligent commentary on what needs to be done to save our country from a meltdown.

title: Liggie Huis -- House of Lights
oneLiner: how 50 000 lights are bringing the Christmas Spirit to Danville -- one of Pretoria's poorest suburbs

People stream from all over to see it, and on Christmas Eve the Danville family (who started this, and funds it from their own pocket), also gives out more than 1000 foodhampers and gifts to poor families, children and the elderly, ensuring that those families at least have food in the table for Christmas. title: CENSEO Insurance Investigator Bully Boys
oneLiner: When your insurance claim goes badly wrong and you are accused of committing the crime
summary: When your home is burgled, or your factory burns down - beware. The insurance policy you have been paying for years amounts to nothing and instead, you are treated like the criminal and arrested for fraudulently claiming or committing arson, and your claim Repudiated. Santam one of the larger Insurance brokers, holding 22% of the South Africa short term insurance market uses CENSEO Insurance Assessor to investigate their claims. CENSEO which does the majority of Santam investigations is 37% owned by them, and receives performance bonuses from Santam. What happened to independent investigations? CENSEO have been challenged by Steward Woodhead a Public Insurance Adjustor and forensic investigator Dr.David Klatzow on numerous occasions for using illegal bullying tactics and extremely underhand methods to get claims repudiated. Insurance companies regularly use “Material Non Disclosure” to repudiate insurance claims which the client only discover what these are at the “Point of Claim” i.e. when the assessor comes to your properly to investigate the claim. Insurance companies are exploiting dysfunctional State departments to delay settling claims, for example Life Cover Policies, Toxicology reports take between 6-7 years from state laboratories and no claim can be settled without it. In motor vehicle claims, if there is any hint of alcohol involved a blood test is required and result can take 3 to 4 months to they used to take 3 to 4 years.

title: Man Up
oneLiner: Its called Movember Month and we bring you Marius Barnards personal battle with cancer
summary: It is time to break the silence of Prostatic Cancer At the age of 69, Dr. Marius Barnard, was diagnosed with prostatic cancer. At that time Dr Barnard, known as a member of the medical team (led by his brother Chris) that performed the first human-to-human heart transplant, was ironically travelling the world as spokesperson for the Critical Illness insurance policy that he had initiated and helped to create. His initial prognosis gave him no more than two years to live. The cancer had been discovered when it was already very advanced, and this man, who had saved thousands of lives in his magnificent career as a heart surgeon, had only himself to blame . . . Today, nearly fifteen years later, after endless treatments and major surgery, he is 85 and still living with his wife Inez to whom he’s been married to for sixty years. Now the couple have decided to break the silence around the devastating effects of prostate cancer in an attempt to prevent other couples suffering the same fate as they did. Their message is: This need not be.

It's had its first hijacking, and women of all colours have been targeted in violent crimes. Apparently with no help from the police. In asking why and how this came about, we learn that the crime emanates largely from Genadendal, an historical Moravian mission station that has developed beyond its intended religious purpose of spreading the word. Petra Vandecasteel has appeared on CB before encouraging her then Gordons Bay community to plant waterwise gardens. In Greyton for two years now, with young children of her own she is concerned that if gangs of 12 year-olds arent reigned in the future is bleak. So she's reaching out, and with the cooperation of the local Red Cross, school and security heads, she's hoping they can turn the trend around. Would you spend your next holiday or retire in Greyton if you knew?

But it was a fake document with a fake swift code and he lost 32 million We know that Lolly Jackson was money laundering with Radovan Krejcir. If Louka comes into this country he'll be dead in a matter of hours. Louka also says he told Mabasa who the real killer

Cowley, 21, went missing on Thursday after he went to meet a potential buyer for his car in Century City. He had placed an advert on Gumtree to sell his BMW. Cowley’’s aunt Anita Hanekom said his mother and girlfriend panicked when he did not return home and alerted the police. “My sister’’s only son wanted to sell his silver BMW and advertised it on Gumtree and he got this guy’’s number. This guy contacted him to set up a meeting and pay some money on the car, so he went to meet the guy and never returned,” said Hanekom. “His girlfriend had an ID number of the guy that wanted to buy it, police traced it to somebody they knew. They went to the guy’’s house in Mitchells Plain, they found Olwyn’’s ID there and then the guy confessed to shooting Olwyn and where they dumped the body.” Police spokesman Captain Frederick van Wyk said three men had been arrested and will appear in the Mitchell’s Plain Magistrate’’s Court today on murder, hijacking and kidnapping charges. Criminals, however, appears to be using Gumtree to target unsuspecting sellers and buyers.
