title: CSIR and stem cells
summary: Gene Expression and Biophysics Group, headed by Dr Musa Mhlanga and Human Geneticist Dr Janine Scholefeld at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR in Pretoria East) have become the first in Africa to generated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Pluripotency means the multiple potential in or ability that stem cells have to become any other kind of cell. The ability to grow these stem cells, a complex skill found exclusively in a handful of institutions across the United States, Europe and Japan, has revolutionised the way that researchers are able to investigate and understand diseases in order to find cures. Their view is to use this technology to finding cures to some of Africa’s most significant diseases. In March 2012 they generated the first iPScells from skin and programmed them to become heart cells. Dr Janine recorded video footage of rhythmically beating cells through a microscope. The beating pattern is distinctive, easily recognisable as heart muscle cells VIDEO LINK http://mhlangalab.synbio.csir.co.za/movies/induced_pluripotent_stem_cell.mov. This is the basis of iPSC technology, which induces adult cells (like skin cells) to revert back into stem cells, which are cells at the earliest stage of life. These early stem cells can then be programmed to become any type of adult cell, such as skin, heart, brain and blood cells. They will do this for us and use the cells to investigate HIV resistant genetics.
caseStudies: Janine Scholefield Human Geneticist

title: Hot for Words (Sexting)
oneLiner: New studies reveal that teenagers who engage in sexting are also more likely to engage in risky sexual behaviour.
summary: Wary of getting your child a cell phone? A new study shows that teens who “sext” aren’t leaving it to just that. The study of nearly 2,000 teens found that those that sexted – sending explicit pictures or text messages – were more likely to engage in sexual activity, raising their risks for sexually transmitted diseases. “No one’s actually going to get a sexually transmitted disease because they’re sexting,” Dr. Eric Rice, a researcher from the School of Social Network at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, told Reuters. “What we really wanted to know is, is there a link between sexting and taking risks with your body? And the answer is a pretty resounding ‘yes.’” The study showed that 15% of teens in grades nine through 12 who were a part of the study and had a handheld device said they sexted, while 50% admitted to knowing someone who has or does sext. Not only can sexting ruin reputations but it can also get teenagers arrested for distributing teen pornography. What does this mean for parents? Take the opportunity and use sexting as a way to discuss more difficult subjects with teens. Explain to younger children that inappropriate photos or texts can be considered pornography and against the law. Safe practices now may lead to better phone etiquette in later years. But some parents are taking a more extreme route and they are buying spyware for their childrens mobile phone - all available online.

title: Bush Boyes
oneLiner: A NatGeo society explorer-cum-zoologist says within ten to 15 years we could lose the last wilderness in Africa, and with his wife and brother set out in a wooden canoe to find it.
summary: People cried everyday on this expedition. Steve Boyes is an ornithologist at UCT's Percy Fitzpatrick Institute...and he's a zoologist. He's the only South African member of the National Geographic Explorer's society - and supported by that organisation he's on a mission to get the Okavango delta declared a World Heritage site. Because despite what people think, it isn't. With his brother and wife - a PhD zoology - they poled traditional wooden mokoros (canoes), which is bloody hard - 300km across the delta. They were in search of what they call 'literal paradise', untouched wilderness. They were followed at a distance by a 20-strong support and film crew - with 'octocopters'(plus GoPros and under-water cameras), cranes and local bayeyi polers - travelling thru places that according to Bayeyi guide, Gobonamang Kgetho - probably havent seen by humans before. The visual background of the story features leopards, lions and fighting hyenas in camp, close encounters with black mambas and 5m crocodiles - and people crying, often, either from exhaustion, elation or depression. Medical help is a world away on the trip - and everyday consequences can be lethal.

title: Wonky Tusk
oneLiner: Every year at the same time a family of wild elephants walk thru the reception of a lodge in Zambia - it's a visit that has been witnessed around the world.
summary: This is a unique wildlife story, involving wild elephants like viewers will never have seen - no controversial training, just fascinating behaviour and beautiful co-existence. Every spring, for over a decade, a family of elephants have walked through the reception of a lodge in Zambia's south luangwa national park. They come for the mango trees in the grounds - walking thru reception rather than around the building. Led by a matriarch dubbed Wonky Tusk, they harm noone - occasionally peeing on the polished, tiled floor. They even sleep in the lodge (not the beds!), they enter the curio shop, the spa, eat the Christmas tree, steal tea bags, etc. A children's book has been written about them - Wonky & wellington. They've made YouTube news. They've been filmed by many tourists who fly in specifically from London and elsewhere just to see them - and it's not a short flight. But it's the locals who know them best - owner (originally a PE boy) Andy Hogg, whos been living there for almost two decades, the reception staff, and he who's been watching Wonky Tusk since 1989 - the longest serving ranger and former warden in the valley, seventy-something Phil Berry. With a crinkly grin and twinkle in his eye, he has the stories and pix to tell and show it. No-one has told the story of the people who found the story...and the global impact that this family of elephants has had, like tourists, professional photographers and even Jonathan Scott of the BBC's Big Cat diaries flying in. As you see in the link...

title: Failed by the State
oneLiner: Crime victim Andre Jordaan died in a state hospital because an essential operation wasn't done. Is the State failing its citizens?
summary: Relatives of a Muldersdrift man who died of gunshot wounds sustained during a robbery last week want to know why an operation which could have saved his life did not go ahead. André Jordaan died at the Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital on Saturday night, where he was being treated after being shot seven times during a robbery on Thursday. On Sunday, Gauteng’s Department of Health confirmed that some hospitals in the province are experiencing backlogs in surgery because of budgetary constraints and a shortage of staff. Spokesman Simon Zwane said the department was doing its best to address the situation. This follows the acknowledgement by the Health Minister, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, in an interview with the Pretoria News, that public health facilities in the province are failing to deliver. The Pretoria News had reported that patients were being turned away from Steve Biko Academic Hospital and operations postponed because of a lack of staff and working equipment. One mother had to resort to approaching the courts to get attention for her son at the hospital so he could have excruciating pain in his leg alleviated. Jordaan’s daughter-in-law Jeanine Jordaan said Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital had told them that his operation was scheduled for Friday. However, he did not have the operation, and they were not told why it had changed. Dr Nita Soma, senior clinical executive at Chris Hani Baragwanath, asked for time to consult the family, the doctors and nurses before commenting on the death. Zwane also said he could not comment yet on the Jordaan case. “We’ll follow up to find out what happened” and should know on Monday. Motsoaledi confirmed that hospitals in Gauteng were running out of essentials due to huge deficits in their budgets, and that efforts to rebuild the system could take time.

title: Larry joe - Facing the Music
oneLiner: A criminal on the Cape Flats to a composer /singer performing for Royalty
summary: In 2008 Larry Joe was living on the Cape Flats, a gang member getting by through crime. Then in Feb 2008 he was caught and sentenced to five years 6 months for housebreaking and theft. Douglasdale Correctional Centre in the Northern Cape was Larry’s new place of abode; it was here his life changed. He started writing and composing and learning to play the guitar (always musical Larry had previously played the guitar by sound) but in prison he took advantage of lessons offered in rehabilitation. It was here that Aron Turest – Swartz co-founder of Freshly Ground recognized Larry’s potential…a musical collaboration between the two followed ( after approval by relevant authorities). Eighteen months later “ Crazy Life” was released on the same day as Larry walked free 13th December 2010 But this would be an old story if it was all, Larry has proved himself no mere flash in the pan but gone from strength to strength -on the 21st of this month he will perform at a fundraising event in Holland in front of Her Royal Highness Queen Beatrix; Larry Joe and his band have been booked to perform at the Royal Carre Theatre on the 24th September. title: Parks officials failing our rhinos

It has now emerged that the rhino were poached while the entire compliment of park rangers were off celebrating World Ranger Day and that they were all ordered off the park leaving the rhino as easy pickings for poachers. It's tantamount to leaving your car in Hillbrow unlocked and with the keys in the ignition. Clearly the parks officials are either complicit with the poachers or they have little or no regard for our rhinos and are doing little or nothing to protect our precious assetts. At the very least they were reckless and negligent. Now the North West Parks authorities have decided to move the remaining rhino off Borakalalo reserve onto a tiny 5000 hectare provincial reserve called Botshalalo. The problem is that this goes against the advice of their own conservationists who tabled a report saying that the reserve was overstocked, the timing was wrong and that they should rather be moved to Madikwe and Pilanesberg. Despite these recommendations the CEO who is a former primary school teacher has sanctioned the move to Botshalalo. Bear in mind that there are only two waterholes on that reserve - the poachers have easy pickings every day when the rhinos arrive at the waterholed - not much guessing or risk involved for them at all. Add to this scenario the fact that officials at North West Parks have failed polygraph test questions on their involvement in rhino poaching,last years scandal where Thai prostitutes posed as hunters and parks officials did nothing and the current Hawks investigation into NW parks officials and we have a ticking time bomb. It also links in perfectly with a new report released by TRAFFIC's Tom Milliken on the rhino horn trade, syndicates and complicit wildlife officials.

title: The God Particle
oneLiner: A South African team from Wits University were integral in the revolutionary discovery of the God particle - or Higgs Boson.
summary: A Wits team, who plays a visible and strong role in the search for the Higgs boson at the ATLAS detector, is part of a team of researchers at the European Organization of Nuclear Research (CERN[1]) who on 4 July announced that they have observed a particle consistent with the Higgs boson. The announcement is hailed as the birth of a new era in the field of fundamental physics. According to the Wits team, tantalizing hints of a new particle with a mass around 126 GeV were reported in December 2011. The ATLAS experiment has confirmed this excess with data taken in 2012. This is consistent with reports from the CMS experiment. The observed excess is consistent with the existence of a Higgs-like particle. The statistical significance of the measurement is 5 sigma. The size of the statistical significance makes it unlikely that the excess observed is due to a statistical fluctuation (by less than a one in a million chance). "More data will be required to understand if this particle corresponds to the Higgs boson of the Standard Model or whether it is connected to new physics. Regardless of the outcome, we can say with confidence that a new era in the field of fundamental physics has just begun. The study of this new particle, its properties and its interactions, will last for decades and will be connected with the development of new technologies to face the new challenges posed by this endeavour. We are happy to see a solid involvement from Wits in this amazing experience," says Wits team leader, Dr Trevor Vickey. The Wits team comprising of lead physicists Dr Trevor Vickey and Dr Oana Boeriu (who both relocated to South Africa to lead the University's involvement in the ATLAS experiment), includes several Wits staff members, postgraduate students and post-doctoral scholars. They will soon be joined by Prof. Bruce Mellado who will take up the position of Associate Professor in the School of Physics.

title: Kumi Naidoo takes a stand

summary: At the end of last week a team of Greenpeace International activists - including Executive Director Kumi Naidoo - boarded Gazprom’s ‘Prirazlomnaya’ Arctic oil platform to demand that the Russian company abandon its dangerous Arctic drilling plans. At 4am local time the activists set off in three inflatable speedboats from the Greenpeace ship Arctic Sunrise and scaled the platform via mooring lines. Six climbers have taken up positions on the structure and have interrupted the platform's operations. The activists are out of reach and have enough supplies to last them for several days. This is the second time Naidoo has engaged in direct action to oppose Arctic oil drilling. The South African human rights activist boarded a drilling rig operated by British company Cairn Energy off Greenland in June 2011. It coincided with scientists at the US National Snow and Ice Data Center predicted that Arctic sea ice would soon match 2007’s lowest ever recorded extent before setting a new record in September. The chemicals sprayed on GM maize in the past were glyphosate –based. Now the maize is getting resistant to glyphosate so DOW want to grow, in the USA, a type of new maize that will be sprayed with a pesticide called 2.4-D – essentially agent orange with many health side effects documented already. Use of 2,4-D just as a pesticide is banned in a few SA provinces because its used in other types of agriculture and the spray drift ruined other crops and there were court cases about this and it was banned. [2,4-D was used to devastating effect during the Vietnam war. Exposure to 2,4-D has been linked to non-Hodgkin?s lymphoma, a cancer of the white blood cells. Epidemiologists from the National Cancer Institute in the USA regard this link as the strongest association yet found between a pesticide and a disease. Dozens of human and animal studies have shown 2,4-D to cause birth defects, neurological damage, and interference with reproductive function. The use of 2,4-D in Sweden, Norway and Denmark is banned because of these well publicised links.]

title: The Princess Project

summary: The Matric Dance were fortunes are spent every year to get Matriculants kitted out for the big night. But what happens when you can't afford even the most basic dress for the big night, Michellle Lissoos's domestic worker approached her for help a few years ago...Michelle not only helped her domestic's daughter but sent an e-mail to some of her friends and colleagues and was amazed at the incredible response. Not only was she able to dress her domestic worker's daughter, she was able to provide dresses and outfits for her entire class. And the Princess Connection-Matric Dance Project was born - an organisation which collects used matric dance dresses and accessories to transform township pupils into glamorous princesses for their big night. Each year Lissoos and her friends call upon networks and colleagues and collect dresses, shoes, scarves, jewellery and the like for the project. It is incredible what a difference a dress can make not only to the students big night but the confidence factor that launches her into the future. They set up shop at the offices of the Core Group, allowing each girl the full experience of shopping for that perfect outfit. Donated dresses are laid out according to size and colour and volunteer stylists help each girl through the process of finding their perfect ensemble, from advising on styles to pairing suitable accessories to complete their make-over. Last year thanks to a network of friends, colleagues and family, Lissoos was able to outfit more than 300 girls from Alexandra, Tembisa, Vosloorus, Soweto and Katlehong, for their dances. This was more than double the girls dressed than the previous year. A feel good programme tying in with Matric Dance Fever where we take past matriculants, what this experience did for them and how they have passed it on and we take prospective students who need a dress. title: Secret London activists "Anti-Apartheid's unsung heroes"
oneLiner: In the late 1960's South Africa's hated regime thought it had crushed all resistance when a motley group Londoners packed their false bottomed suitcases, to bring the propoganda war to the enemy
summary: Ken Keable, editor of London Recruits. Keable explains why he decided to tell his story after all these years and how the idea for the book came about. He also recalls accidentally setting off a charge in a Durban hotel room, an incident that has haunted him to this day. Ronnie Kasrils, former Minister of Intelligence and author. The Unlikely Secret Agent, joined Keable in an intriguing discussion and recollection. Dutch activist, Klaas de Jonge, whose “footprint in our history is rather large.” He and his wife, Helen Pastoors, brought weapons into the country from Maputo over several years, burying equipment in dead letter boxes, and providing sketches to incoming MK cadres. The book, which was first published in the UK by Merlin Press, is a collection of narratives written by those who served the anti-apartheid movement, mostly recruited from the Young Communist Party. Dennis Walsh showed the patterned inside of the false-bottomed suitcase that deceived the eye in order to conceal its contents. It was one of some 200 similar pieces of luggage that were constructed to serve this purpose. “It worked brilliantly,” said Walsh. “It was a small contribution but we were very proud to have made it.” Tim Jenkins unpacked a shopping bag which contained “a real live leaflet bomb”. Initially conceived of as the “bucket bomb”, the design that Kasrils had taught him to create. However, “a nice white boy like me would never be seen carrying a bucket around town” so a modified plan permitted him to wander around town undetected carrying a supermarket packet instead. “Beneath my green tea, facial tissues and poppadums,” said a grinning Jenkins, as he unpacked his groceries, “is this big fat battery, the timer, the explosives…”

summary: In Africa, these fire survival strategies are largely confined to the Cape Floral Kingdom where many species have no other fire survival mechanism. Plants may take from 3 to 15 years to flower for the first time. title: Elephant Birth Control
oneLiner: The African elephant population explosion can finally be put to rest - no more excuses for culling baby elephants as pigs eggs prove to be the perfect pill
summary: Porcine zona pellucida - or PZP is controlling populations of wildlife species such as elephant, dee and zebra. It's a non-hormonal vaccine derived from pig eggs. It works by producing anti-bodies which block the reproductive process and prevent pregnancy. It's been used in South Africa to manage reproduction of 230 elephant cows in 13 parks, including Thornybush, Makalali, Phinda and Temba. The first trials were undertaken in KNP in 1996 and there's no physical or behavioral side effects. This finally addresses the impact of elephants numbers on water resouces and vegetation and offers an alternative to culling excess elephants.

title: GREEDY BANKS

People are falling into heavy debt, suicide is on the increase and more homes and cars are being repossessed. The National Treasury says unsecured lending, which is riskier for banks, but much more lucrative, has increased from R23 billion to R50 billion over the past financial year. Finance Minister, Pravin Gordhan, has called banks 'greedy monsters' and the National Credit Regulator says it's investigating the reasons for the increase. Consumers are attracted by constant phone calls and ads, promising easy loans with easy terms. We look at the spike in this kind of lending and the impact it's had on two South African families. We also look into whether some advertising for loans breaches the Consumer Protection Act by being 'misleading, fraudulent or deceptive'

title: Thandi Sibisi

summary: I would like to do a five minute interview with Thandi Sibisi, the first black woman to open a major art gallery in South Africa at Melrose Arch. She is 25 years old. Thandi Sibisi, a daughter of farmers in the Zulu heartland, remembers arriving in the big city for the first time. "The bus dropped me in Gandhi Square in Johannesburg," she recalled. "I was 17 and had never even seen a double-storey building in my life. I looked around and it was like, 'I'm going to own this city'." Eight years later, she has not yet quite conquered it all. But on Thursday she became the first black woman to open a major art gallery – named Sibisi, naturally enough, for someone so ambitious – in South Africa. It is a sign, she believes, that anything is possible for the country's "born free" generation. "All I have to do is look at myself and my background," she said. "Growing up, I would never have thought I'd be exposed to so many opportunities. South Africa is free. "I go all over the world and people are closed up and they can't express themselves. South Africa allows you to be you and to be whatever it is you want to be." She is young and very attractive and trendy, I really believe she will be inspirational to our viewership

title: Fraudster on the Run II
oneLiner: We've exposed him for millions lost with his "brilliant trading skills" in 2009. He was arrested, found guilty on 2 charges, spent 2 years in prison and released. Surprise - he's at it again. at it a
summary: In 2009, Servaas Louwrens walked into the Carte Blanche office and asked us to do a story about him. He wanted to tell people he didn't steal R80 million of their money; he lost it on poor trading investments. At the time, none of us knew who he was. But after googling him, we soon found out there was a snake in the grass. In our interview with him, he had an answer for everything - he didn't want to hand himself over to the police, because he was told by the investigating officer he wouldn't get bail and even Zuma got bail; his company Equilibrium failed because of the interference of the Reserve Bank and SARS; he didn't disappear with the money invested in Equilibrium, he lost it and he didn't want to go to prison, because he would like to have the opportunity to trade again and regain the money "lost" to give it back to the people. Well, the R80 million "lost" in Equilibrium is still gone. In the same week that our story aired, he was arrested with information we gave to the police. He appeared in court the same day. At first the state refused bail, but after he appealed the ruling, bail of R75 000 was granted. He couldn't pay it and stayed in prison until the end of his trial. He stood trial on 30 charges, but was only found guilty on two charges of offenses of the Law on Insolvency. He got a suspended sentence of five years and is not allowed to register a new company or be the director of a company until 2016.

title: Where's our DNA Database?
oneLiner: But on a scale unequaled on earth, hundreds of thousands of children’s lives are sacrificed because of the failure to act by politicians to integrate the justice system and a DNA database .
summary: Raped in their school toilets a young girl and her brother aged 8 and 6 respectively have pointed out their alleged rapist, who is also a teacher at their Grahamstown. But despite this they are still living in fear of going back to school and being victimised again, after the alleged rapist was let off due to a lack of evidence. It's reopened the debate on why South Africa does not have a DNA database integrated into our judicial system. How many more children's lived need to be sacrificed on the alter of political indecision? You can have the best, most advanced laboratory system in the world, the most rigorous quality assurance procedures, and send specialized crime scene analysts to every crime scene – but those factors mean little if the law does not allow you leverage the full potential of the technology and the evidence. Nowhere is that dynamic more tragically clear than in South Africa.

Siphiwe was very lethargic and just lay around not wanting to play or interact. He was not very communicative and very whiney. By Tuesday, 14 February 2012, my husband and I took the decision to fetch Siphiwe and another baby boy, Desmond, from the home and take them to the Witkoppen Clinic for TB and HIV testing. It was then that we were given Siphiwe’s clinic card and it showed he was in fact 13 months old (born 17 January 2011).

title: Peter Knights - Wildlife Warrior

summary: This is a five minute interview with archive footage from Peter Knights, Wildaid. In comic books and movies, masked super heroes always sense when there is trouble afoot, and they swoop in to save the day. Real life, of course, is different, unless you know Peter Knights. He is a co-founder of a group called WildAid, which among other things travels all around the globe helping local governments catch poachers and bring them to justice. A ruggedly handsome Englishman, the aptly named Knights used to work as an investigator exposing illegal trade in endangered species. Then in 2000, he helped found WildAid when he became convinced that exposing the problem was not enough. Funded primarily by private foundations, WildAid assists governments in training and equipping anti-poaching patrols. But the group also employs non-traditional maneuvers, such as posing as buyers and infiltrating poaching rings. Shark fins, bear bile, pelts from rare animals; whether the items are taken for fashion or old-fashioned health or fertility rites, Knights goes after poachers of every stripe. It is dangerous work but he is the kind of man who does not shrink from such challenges…no matter where he finds them all over the globe.

title: Tea Cup Pets Scam - Micro-porkers & Bull dogs
oneLiner: Tiny pets the size of tea-cups are the latest craze but when these micro-porkers turn out to be super-sized pets who's there to save their bacon?
summary: With their wrinkled little snouts, tiny trotters and oversized ears, they are irresistibly cute. But while these micro pigs may be minuscule, their price tag is anything but - this reseller in Somerset West, sells her teeny tiny pigs from breeders in Bloemfontein for anything between R2500 and R4500 each. Her name is Carmen and she's been featured on Pasella promoting her tea-cup piglets misleading people to believe that they will not grow bigger than 40cm. However, these piggies are so small because they get taken away from their mothers from as young as 11 days and not 4-6 weeks as stated. And not too long little piggie grows up to supersize pot belly and has outgrown their pet owners home. With no where to go they are ending up at shelters that aren't geared to handle pigs and soon are sent to pig breeders who are now following in the footsteps dog mill breeders.

title: Magaliesburg Clash of the Titans - Biosphere or Mining
oneLiner: Magaliesburg is just about to be prolclaimed a UNESCO Biosphere with international significance but at the same time 4 applications to mine Gold and Uranium have been tabled. The Clash of the Titans
summary: Magaliesburg lies at the interface of two great African biones - the central grassland plateaux and the sub-Saharan savannah - with remnants of a third, Afro-montane forest. The landscape accommodates species from each of these biomes which result exceptionally diverse flora and fauna. The range has Protection status since 1977 but next month it will be official The Magaliesburg will receive UNESCO Biosphere status. Today there are 580 designated biospheres in 114 countries. In SA we have Kogelberg, Cape West Coast, Waterberg, Kruger to Canyons, Cape Winelands, Vhembe and now Magaliesburg.Which is good news for farm owners, lodges and the town itself. But now the Battle line has been drawn - after the 4th mining application has been put forward to mine gold and uranium - apparently the land in and around Magaliesburg is rich in minerals and Mining companies can't wait to get their hands on the land. So far Mariette Lieferlink, the eco-warrior featured in Carte Blanche inserts before is rallying townsfolk to raise their flags. The town is full of eccentric charcters like Vincent Curruthers - who's written a number of books, he's an environmentalist and historian - speaks really well... we've got John Wesson - knows the in's and out's of mining and is against it. An italian ice-cream factory been around more than a 100 years - supplies the country with desserts.. the pollution of ground water will put them out of business etc. We aim to exploit the dramatic visuals that surround us - waterfalls, wonderful wildlife as well as the history angle, the Battle of Nooitgedacht was fought in the mountain cliffs just in front of us. There's also the 2nd largest colony of Cape Vultures... and with most lodges booked every weekend. This is the clash of the Titans - we aim to bring interviews from UNESCO to see what they have to say about the newly acquired Biosphere status - will this put an end to the lure of gold and uranium from mining magnates.

title: The Protein Crunch (Maggots)
oneLiner: The common housefly could be the answer to saving our Seas-at the helm the Drew Brothers and their fly factories - aiming to feed the small fry with protein made from abattoir waste
summary: We meet Jason Drew, international businessman, serial entrepreneur. He says the rich are already consuming the water of the thirst, eating the food of the hungry and burning fuel of the cold. Now the Drew brothers have a solution to solving our fish stock crisis as well as feeding the poor. Jason collaborated with the University of Stellenbosch and a team of international scientists to develop a renewable and natural replacement for 'fishmeal' which is fed to farmed fish and chickens. Most of our fish stocks are used to feed animals and accounts for over half of the global marine catch. The secret to the fishmeal replacement is billions of industrially reared larvae - recycling existing and potentially harmful organic waste. Maggots might just save the oceans from over-fishing. To make one ton of the meal, about five tons of maggots are required. The larvae are dried and then processed into a fine rich brown powder - solt to farmers in 50kg bags. In terms of nutrient value the product matches that of fishmeal and is superior to soya. The Drew brothers have included some facinating facts from their latest book "Protein Crunch" like it takes 30 000 litres of water to make a cellphone. 150 litres of water for 1 pint of beer. Countries like China and Russia are buying huge tracts of land in Africa for their own consumption. China has 2.8 million hectares in the Congo alone. These facts could supplement the insert as well as getting hands on with the filming of the process in the fly factories. Next year they hope to produce 28 tons of dried maggots a day - 2000 tons a month.

Delmas farmer, Peet Bezuidenhout has gone to the Blue Scorpions to get the big guns behind him. title: SA Dumping Ground
oneLiner: It's called Dumping first Tyers now Chickens - how does flooding the market with cheaper products really impact the consumer?
summary: Following an investigation the ITAC found that Brazilian companies were dumping chicken goods on the SA market for up to 60% less than in their respective markets. Now the government is going to enforce a section of the Customs and Excise Act of 1964 - to combat dumping products in SA. We will examine viewpoints for and against anti-dumping - Some say an anti-dumping law poses one of the greatest threats to trade liberalization. The rationale for anti-dumping is based on a theory that a foreign producer, reaping super-normal profits in a protected home market could sell at a loss in SA for a pro-longed period, driving it competitors from the market and eventually raising their prices in absence of competition. We will look at the recent case study of chickens as well as tyres being dumped, flooding the market. There's been a strong reaction from consumers some saying that the biggest losers will be the consumers and loss of import tax revenue for SARS. If Brazilian producers were willing to provide a product at a price more affordable to the poor, why shouldn't the consumer have a choice? If Brazilians, Namibians or Europeans produce and distribute chickens for less than SA - why superficially boost prices to 'protect' local industry...

title: Shark Angels
oneLiner: 14 Tiger Sharks were caught in a single KZN shark net in one morning. Global outrage has ensued, Sharks Board is under fire from none other than the SHARK ANGELS
summary: Shark Angels co-founder, Julie Andersen, who frequently leads groups of people on diving trips with the tiger sharks of Aliwal Shoal, clearly illustrates the irony of using shark nets to increase tourism, noting the number of tourists who come to South Africa each year specifically to dive with sharks. Over the last three decades, more than 33,000 sharks have been killed in the KZNSB shark nets. And if that's not alarming enough, consider the 2,000+ turtles, 8,000+ rays, and 2,000+ dolphins who were also ensnared and killed. In addition to the countless deaths of sharks and other species caused directly by the shark nets, their impact on our collective psyches is damaging to shark conservation efforts worldwide. The very existence of shark nets perpetuates the myth that sharks are bloodthirsty man-eaters, and that humans require some form of protection from them. The installation of shark nets reinforces our misguided and often irrational fears of sharks by legitimizing these concerns as valid. This in turn fuels the biggest issue faced in shark conservation: the public's apathy, or even loathing, towards sharks. It could be said there was once a time and a place for shark nets. Perhaps decades ago, when the public knew little about sharks, the fear of shark attacks was running high, and shark populations were far healthier than they are today. The practice of installing shark nets in South Africa began in 1952, when little was known about sharks, and humans had yet to spend the next 50+ years ravaging our oceans, causing irreparable damage and the collapse of species after species. The public wanted "protection" from sharks, and shark nets served this purpose.

title: Toxic Facial
oneLiner: Women in Tudor Shaft informal settlement have a toxic secret to their skin care; Radio active soil from their backyards.
summary: Women in Tudorshaft informal settlement in Krugersdorp have discovered a cost effective and readily available solution to their facial skin care problems. This solution is yellow cake mine tailings soil found on their backyards. While it may look harmless, The National Nuclear Regulator did a report on the Upper Wonderfontein Catchment Area, where the Tudor Shaft settlement is located and found that thousands of residents of Tudor shaft are exposed to potentially dangerous levels of radiation. The tailings contain high concentrations of cancer-causing heavy metals as well as radio-active uranium which could leave people susceptible to birth defects and brain disorders. Of the thousands of families exposed to the high radiation levels, only 24 were moved, the rest remain settled on what has been described as a time bomb. Pregnant women in the settlement eat the yellow soil under the assumption that it is good for their babies while others use it as face lotion. The Federation for a sustainable environment has described this as an impending disaster that needs urgent attention. Tudorshaft is only one one of close to 400 mine dumps and slime dams that are posing a serious risk to poor communities that have settled n these areas. The story will focus on the severe health threat that the radio active soil poses to these people while seeking answers as to why despite the reports available, only 24 out of a few thousand families have been moved from this radiological hot spot.

title: Sudden Sporting Deaths
oneLiner: An alarming number of professional and school-going sports-people are succumbing to sudden heart-attacks, but a South African specialist says it's something we should be prepared for - as it c
summary: A little under two months ago, two top European football stars suffered cardiac arrest on consecutive days, on the football pitch - their hearts had stopped beating. An athlete died in the London Marathon last week, an Italian player on the soccer field the week previously, and Alexander Dale Oen, a Norwegian world champion swimmer and medal hope for the London Olympics, collapsed and died in the shower during a training camp. Both athletes had a condition now known as a “channelopathy”, which can cause sudden collapse in anyone – whether fit sportsman or apparently healthy child. It is caused by a genetic abnormality in the heart, such as a medical condition known as a “long QT syndrome” and - being hereditary - may occur in several members of the same family. According to a report published by the University of Washington, sudden death in athletes occurs approximately once every 3 days in the United States. Yet it needn’t be related to sport. In recent times South African children have also succumbed because of this condition, with some dying on the sports field or even on the couch while watching TV. The above-mentioned football stars are alive because they both received immediate cardio-pulmonary resuscitation (CPR) – from team doctors on the pitch - and their heartbeats were restarted by a life-saving electrical shock provided by an automated external defibrillator (AED) at the scene. South African emergency medicine specialists say most such deaths can be easily prevented - and we show how.

title: Mining Ripoff
summary: ANC bigwigs Zola Skweyiya and Aaron Motsoaledi, and top businesswoman Wendy Luhabe are among several people who invested millions of rands in Lontoh Coal – some of whom now claim they've been misled by the company. The names of these high-profile people were allegedly used to lure more people to pump money into Lontoh Coal with a promise of huge returns once it listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Investors are now accusing Lontoh Coal of duping unsuspecting people into buying shares in the company, which said it had a shareholding in mining companies. But an investigation by investors and responses from the mining houses showed that Lontoh Coal did not own stakes in any mines. Investors claim that Lontoh Coal chief executive Tshepo Kgadima promised them a 5% commission if they brought in new investors. But Kgadima this week was adamant that the company – which was started in 2006, owned shares in mines – adding that he had a fleet of 70 trucks and employed 140 drivers. A list of Lontoh Coal investors shows that more than 90 people invested R11m in the firm. Skweyiya (the South African ambassador to the UK), and his family invested R3.6m, while Luhabe pumped in R160,500 and Health Minister Motsoaledi put in R1,000. Angry investors said Kgadima would meet potential investors, sell them the idea of buying shares and promise that Lontoh Coal would list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Dr Nkululeko Skweyiya, the ambassador’s nephew, said the veteran politician and his wife, Thuthukile, invested R1.6m, while the Skweyiya family trust invested R2m into the company. “Tshepo Kgadima told us that he was raising funds to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on November 28. But when the deadline came, he pushed it forward to March 2012,” said Dr Nkululeko Skweyiya.

title: Shark Attack Survivor Breaks Records
oneLiner: We find out what drives 200m Butterfly Para Olympics record holder & Great White Shark attack survivor Achmat Hassiem as he sets his sights on the London Paralympics
summary: During April 2012 Achmat Hassiem competed in the SA Nedbank National Disabled Championships in KZN, winning eight gold medals of the eight events he had entered and setting six new all African records. The South African National Open Swimming Championships were also held in KZN and treated as trials for both the Paralympic and Olympic Games, for South African athletes wanting to compete in London. Achmat competed in these trials and won the 400m Freestyle in a Paralympic A-qualifying time as well as a new South African and Africa record. He also swam Paralympic A-qualifying time in 100m butterfly and set a new South African and Africa record. Achmat is currently the world champion for 200m butterfly Paralympics. Shark attack survivor, Achmat Hassiem lost his foot to a Great White shark when participating in a lifeguard training session at Sunrise Beach in Muizenberg in 2006. Since then, he has made an amazing recovery, learning to walk with his prosthetic foot, competing in the Beijing 2008 Paralympic Games and 2010 IPC World Swimming Championships in the Netherlands. He also conquered his fear of going back into the seas when he completed the 7.5km Cadiz Robben Island cold water swim in 2010 and 2011. He is captain of the Western Province Swimming Team, and has led them to victory for four years running. Achmat has qualified for the London 2012 Paralympic games and the team will be announced on 20 May 2012. He has set his sights on competing in the able-bodied Olympics too. The story could be produced in the lead up to the paralympics or could include his competing in the London event and include his results there.

title: Ocearch Great White Shark Tagging
oneLiner: we unpack the controversy of Ocearch shark tagging methods, reveal why 30 SA scientists joined the trip, exploring the fall out of the fatal attack & how cancelling permit will affect future research
summary: It’s well known that in SA scientists struggle for funding. So Chris Fischer’s pledge of R15.4mill for research was tempting despite criticism of his SPOT tag techniques & gung ho catching methods. Fischer promised his methods improved & harm to sharks would be minimal if any. Jan 2011 DEA’s Dr Alan Boyd issued a permit for Fischer to film & research. 30 SA scientists chose to participate believing data would contribute to their research. Yet no public announcement made & the expedition kept secret ‘til it was revealed by Dr Schmidt a month after tagging began in Mossel Bay. By the time Ocearch was to move to Gansbaai & False Bay there was much suspicion about the expedition, criticism of scientists who’d been anti Fischer's methods & concern over chumming where shark activity & human interaction was already an issue. Schmidt asked for public awareness & DEA to issue a "precautionary warning for possible increased shark activity" but Boyd publicly dismissed any possibility for increased shark activity calling claims of a possible attack alarmist. So when David Lilienfield died from a vicious attack by a 4m GW Boyd's knee jerk reaction was to suspend Ocearch's permit immediately. It’s reported sharks leave the area after Ocearch’s tagging (also in Mexico & USA). Some critics suggest trauma spurs the mass departure & a displaced GW from Gansbaai may have attacked Lilienfeld. Others blame the chumming in False Bay. While there’ll never be proof Ocearch’s research & Lilienfield’s death are related there’s certain to be repercussions for GW shark research in SA. Under what conditions will permits now be allocated? Will chumming be allowed during research? Who will fund spotters at more beaches? If official warnings were issued would Lilienfield have entered the water? Would more people have been on the lookout & warned officials of sightings earlier? Has this entire incident been a step backwards for protection of GW sharks & who should be held accountable?

title: The Comet Airline 60th Anniversary
oneLiner: Sixty Years on we look at an airlines controversial demise and what we learned for state of the art aircraft
summary: In May 1952, the world’s first commercial airliner took to the skies for the first time. The De Havilland Comet was to become one of the most controversial aircraft ever flown, its advocates commending its revolutionary design features, while its critics warned of untested technology which would eventually lead to tragedy. Today, two of the original Comet team – one a navigator, the other an engineer - recount their memories from their homes in Johannesburg, which was an original destination for the Comet. Their stories dispel many of the myths surround the curse of the Comet, and set the record straight on how this aeroplane set the standard for trans-continental flight for years to come.
