title: Where's my Generator?
oneLiner: Wanting a generator for those blackouts? We confront a company that promises power and then pulls the plug.
summary: Zakpower is a Menlo Park based company which is defrauding people out of thousands of rands by using a search engine optomised web-site to entrap potential victims. After filling in the online form, you are send a very competive generator price as well as other details e.g. web-site, office address etc. Everything runs smoothly until you make the payment for the generator, that is when Zakpower goes quiet and you don't hear from then until you call. Trying to get hold of any of the sales people e.g. Court Ncube is virtually impossible and I believe that the persona is created. They are forever in meetings when you try to get hold of them to find out when is the generator going to be delivered. When you eventually get hold of Thabo, Phule or Eddy, you are being promised that the generator will be delivered and given all sorts of possible excuses. When you try and cancel the order because of non-delivery you are then been told of the terms & conditions on their web-site you should have read. You will then receive a copy of a cancellation form. You complete it and that's where it ends.
caseStudies: Marlon Moon Moon
experts: Mr. Paul Mngwevu Mr. Consumer Protector

title: Conman Carpenter
oneLiner: He promises dream kitchens and beautiful wooden creations, takes your money and heads off on holiday - we track down the conman carpenter.
summary: His name is Eddie Ardendorff and recently warnings about him have appeared in several local rags in the PE/Despatch/Uitenhage areas. He has been operating as a carpenter and handyman in the area for 5 years according to his former partner who has this to say about him: I used to be a friend and partner of this con man until I found out what he is really about. There is an endless list of people he has conned and lied to just to get their money. He has had a two page article in the Son of at least 5 people conned out of huge amounts of money with a resume of downloaded pictures from the internet which he has never done. He pretends to be a Christian and has had many people fooled, a wolf disguised in sheep's clothing. He has been in prison for burglary and armed robbery and is a desperate man who will do anything for money except an honest living. He has taken the life savings of a pensioner and the meager savings of a struggling single mother and gone on holiday with it after ripping out her whole kitchen promising to build the cupboards which never came. I just want to warn people of this man. While he was my partner, he did things behind my back and still owes those people money for work never done. He has robbed me and my wife of a substantial amount of money which we might never get back because he "owns" nothing. The lawyer we are with has a folder thick with complaints and cases logged against him which will never be won because he doesn't have a bank account or anything on his name. Take it from my experience and all those he has robbed in the past, stay away from this man. You will get very low quality work, lies and lots of headaches because once your money is given, you will never get it back again. Rather go with your instinct and deal with a respectable, qualified company which will charge you a bit more, but it will be money well spent..

title: Fight for Survival
oneLiner: We chronicle the brave fight for survival of a rhino, poached and left for dead in the Kariega Reserve.
summary: Last year March we did a story on rhino poaching - at the time we said that one rhino was being poached every day. This year more or less the same time it's two a day. Last year we told you the story of Geza - a white rhino bull found poached but alive. Despite wildlife vet Dr William Fowld's efforts they had to make the decision to euthanase Geza. This year he was confronted with three poached rhino - all alive but callously poached. One died at the scene but the remaining two fought bravely. Determined to save them Dr Fowlds and his team embarked on a mammoth and costly mission to save these rhino. All their efforts have been caught on film and a reality style video diary of the whole exercise is available free of charge to us. Sadly 3 weeks after the attack Themba succombed to his injuries. Thandi is looking well and although not completely out of the woods Dr Fowlds and his team are confident that she will make it.
caseStudies: Will Fowlds Vet Graeme Rushmere Reserve Owner Alan Weyer Reserve Manager
experts: Mr. Pelham Jones

title: Mark Abadi - Energy Medicine
oneLiner: Mark Abadi, holistic therapist tries to bridge the gap between science and spirituality in holistic healing
summary: Mark Abadi, is a spiritual life coach, holistic therapist and quantum psychologist, he blends and expands psychological study with physiological biology and quantum mechanics to better understand the dynamics of the Human Holistic System. He tries to bridge the gap between science and spirituality. He practices what he calls 'Energy Medicine' He is a qualified psychologist and physical therapist. Mark, uses science to outline how information moves through and between bodies of consciousness. Mark tries to dispel some of the claims that disciplines like homeopathy, bodytalk and acupuncutre are unscientific, by using science to explain their efficacy. One of his main preoccupations is 'How pharmaceutical companies keep us sick'. He bases his holistic Homeopathic thinking in what he calls scientific research. He believes that pharmaceutical companies are treating the symptoms of disease and not the true causes. He explains where emotional and mental memory might be stored in the body and how it might be released. With the work of leading biologists and physicists, he looks at how the mind and body interact with the zero point field or quantum vacuum as well as the fundamental physics that make this possible. He answers questions on how do crystals & water hold their charge and memory? What are the mechanisms behind energetic healing? How does the shape of things effect our consciousness? We have and exclusive opportunity for a one-on-one interview with Mark Abadi and we can film in some of his workshops. He is available before the 19th of April for an interview in Durban.
experts: Mr. Mark Abadi Energy Medicine Practicioner

title: Tina's New Heart & Lungs
oneLiner: With a brand new heart and lungs, Tina is doing her best to hold on to life...
summary: Tina Beckbessinger is the only surviving heart-lung patient in the country. Of Hillcrest, KZN, she was born with congenital cardiac disease - a condition that was diagnosed at 6 months old. Initially it was predicted she would not live to be a teenager. At age 13 she had heart failure and had a pacemaker fitted to keep her heart going. She was told that she would one day need a heart/lung transplant - because the heart was putting so much pressure on the lungs that it would damage them beynd repair. As she grew, so her condition worsened. She had a second pacemaker fitted at 21. Without the strength or energy that she'd previously had, she says she lost most of the independence she'd gained. A harsh reality for a 'newly-empowered' 21 yr-old. She had to live with her parents, she couldn't work and spent between 18 - 20 hours a day sleeping. She was put on the transplant waiting-list in April 2009. About 30 long months later - On 29 October 2011 - tina had her transplant. She went home 14 days after the operation. Apart from being the only surviving patient, Tina is also only the sixth heart/lung transplant patient in south africa. She's had some 'rejection scares', worried about her body rejecting not only a new heart, but lungs too. Right now she's been in bed for a week solid with a cold - that's because she has no immune system. Why? She has to take immuno-suppressants, to prevent her immune system from rejecting these foreign organs that have been planted in her body. So she has to avoid getting ill at all - not dissimilar to an HIV patient. And she will have to take them for the rest of her life. Transplant world is emotionally taxing - patients live in hope of an organ becoming available. Right now the hospital has an 8 yr-old boy waiting for a heart... Meanwhile Tina is very positive about her future - and looking forward to participating in the World Transplant Games.
caseStudies: Dave Gillmer Cardiologist
experts: Ms. Natalie Heine Best friend Mr. Robert Kleinloog Cardio Thoracic Surgeon Ms. Cindy Goldie transplant co-ordinator - ethekwini hospital Ms. Samantha Volschenk Organ Donor Foundation Mrs. Bev Pendock Mother

title: Halaal Hot Cross Buns
oneLiner: Are the hot cross buns you are eating Halaal?
summary: Halaal Hot Cross Buns - headline on the streets of Durban today. It seems that the fact that Woolworths is selling hot cross buns with Halaal approval signs has caused a bit of a flutter on Facebook and Twitter. ( I am not sure whether the Easter Eggs also have Halaal stickers on them) There is a lobby who want to boycott Woolworths now. As you know I have been looking at the story for a couple of years now. The crux of the argument is really with the food manufacturers who want to appeal to a bigger market and buy Halaal certification. We have a very small Muslim community in South Africa but at least 90% of our food is Halaal approved. Woolworths has said that next year they will provide hot cross buns without the Halaal certification. The question would be whether these hot cross buns will be cheaper? The Muslim certification boards are a multi million rand enterprise, and the manufacturers have to pay for the certification. I think the programme can work if Woolworths will grant us an interview.

title: TROUT TRIANGLE COAL MINE
oneLiner: It's known for fly fishing, star gazing and snow in winter but it seems the Dullstroom area is going to get a coal mine and all the pollution that's part of that.
summary: William Patrick Bower PTY Ltd or WPB Colliery has applied for a coal mining license in the Trout Triangle in the Dullstroom area of Mpumalanga. The area is part of a World Heritage Site and the community is objecting saying it will affect tourism, fauna and flora. In it's application for a license the mine has stated that it will create 44 jobs but the community says around 1 000 jobs in the tourism industry will be affected if the license is granted. The mining activity is a 5-year project and it will supply only 00.25% of ESKOM's coal mine requirements. The total amount of coal to be mined over the period will not be enough to supply Witbank with electricity for one week. Three major water systems will be affected; The Komati River, the Crocodile River and the Elandspruit which eventually becomes the Elands River. The wetlands known as Lakenvlei and Groenvlei are very close to the proposed mine. The coal transporters will use the same road that is used to reach the Trout Lodges in the area and trout farmers fear the tourism side of business will die as a result of the dust and pollution. There are also fears for the endangered bird species in the area.
caseStudies: Bruce Murray Neighbouring Dairy Farmer Tree Ferns Trout Lodge Frans Krige Nature Concervation Koos Pretorius Technical Advisor Ursula Francke Birdlife SA
experts: Mr. William Bower WPB Colliers

title: Embassies in Arrears
oneLiner: They have diplomatic immunity even when they don't pay their rent. Be warned if you plan to do business with them.
summary: Two South Africans who own up-market properties in Pretoria have been left with hundreds of thousands of Rands in outstanding rent and damages after doing business with foreign embassies. Marga Hofmeyr used to run a guest house called The Diplomat near the Union Buildings and when she moved to Cape Town she rent the property to the Embassy of the Central African Republic for R31 750 pm. But they soon stopped paying and when she tried to evict them they claimed diplomatic immunity. The outstanding amount is now about R100 000, they've paid on and off and even her lawyers have given up. It seems that the Dept of International Relations and Co-Operation (DIRCO) also battles to assist in any way. Marga's even written to the President of the CAR. She still has to pay the bond and their Telkom bill of R8000. Lukie Carelse has a R4-million Rand property in Waterkloof Ridge which he rents to the Zambian Embassy. They have caused more than R150 000 in damages to the house and moved out without paying the rent. They've ignored all Lukie's attempts to get his money, his lawyer has now also given up and Lukie want's to warn people about the pitfalls when dealing with embassies.
caseStudies: Marga Hofmeyr Landlord Lukie Carelse Landlord CAR and Zambia spokesperson
experts: Mr. DIRCO

title: Harrismith: The other side of the story
oneLiner: They didn't want the N3 to bypass their town but is the real reason their monopoly in the truck-stop business?
summary: Harrismith Municipality in the Free State bars trucks from stopping at any place at any time except at the truck stop on the outskirts of the town. The truck-stop sells food, has toilets and allow prostitutes to do business. When full or if the trucks park elsewhere in town for whatever reason, the SAPS or local traffic cops impound them forcing the drivers to pay thousands of Rands to get their vehicles released. The very same truck-stop also acts as the pound and the normal practice in other towns is to fine truck drivers. The owners of the truck-stop are Ben Deysel and his son Benno who featured in our story on the proposed N3 that would bypass Harrismith. According to my source they have the SAPS and traffic cops on their pay roll. The source is a businessman from Pietermaritzburg who owns a lot of trucks. His astonishing story is how much bribes they have to pay in the trucking industry and he's prepared to say that on camera if we hide his identity. Bribes to get contracts with well known companies, bribes to traffic cops, etc. He's talking about thousands of Rands on every trip between Durban and Johannesburg. Curiously no bribes are accepted in Harrismith.
caseStudies: Yacob (HIDE HIS IDENTITY) Dhoda Businessman Ben Deysel Businessman Harrismith SAPS
experts: Mr.

title: Mauritius Cattle Ship
oneLiner: Every year, millions of farm animals are transported thousands of kilometers on hoof just to arrive to meet their cruel death. We follow a ship of horrors and pick up on the NSPCA's plight.
summary: Multi-tiered ships hold the animals on the voyage from East London to Port Louis in Mauritius. The decks are often enclosed without adequate ventilation, dust and ammonia builds up and many face the harsh elements at sea for up to 10 days with just enough space to turn around. We follow one of the biggest consignments of cattle from East London to Mauritius. As the cattle board one get's its hoof caught and breaks it's ankle. To put it out of its misery NSPCA has to put it down. Finally they arrive in Port Louis only to be thrust on a truck for another 1 hour journey. Most cattle are brought in live for Halal slaughter - animals need to be alive when their throats are slashed. NSPCA's Grace & Ashley are the only one's on the lookout for the cattle from South Africa - it takes 14 hours to offload the herd - but the last one had to be humanely put down, the journey was just too much. The NSPCA is on a mission to band the live and inhumane export of farm animals. We pick up on their plight.

title: Pastor Johnnie
oneLiner: Pastor Johnnie van Eeden and his wife Joanita have conned a lot of people to invest in his 'Help me panic Button' business but his own greed may just help to get him arrested.
summary: The 'Help me Panic button' franchise has been widely advertised but it's yet another scam of the elusive Pastor Johnnie van Eeden. Once you've bought your 'area' he disappears with your cash, never taking your calls again. The very impressive contract seems to be worth less the paper it's printed on.
caseStudies: Arnu de Kock victim Leon Van Ronge Victim Andre Norval Victim

title: A New Organ for St Georges
oneLiner: A R10 Million organ for the parish of St Georges
summary: St George’s Anglican church in Parktown, Johannesburg will soon be inaugurating its brand new organ, the first pipe organ to be installed in a church in South Africa in over 70 years. The cost to the tune of R 10 million. The organ, designed and built by Austrian firm Rieger, has been donated to the church by Nicky and Strilli Oppenheimer. The Oppenheimer family has worshipped at St George’s for three generations, and Harry Oppenheimer was a server there for many years. With music playing a central role in worship at St George’s, the need for a new organ became ever more apparent as the existing instrument – installed in the 1920s – had worn out. The five year project to commission and install the new organ has been a major undertaking, and a series of concerts featuring organists from all over the world has been organized to celebrate the new instrument. In a small corner of Johannesburg, a parish and its congregation have shown once again that religion is alive and well in South Africa and that music is an essential ingredient.
caseStudies: Nicky Oppenheimer Organ Donor Michael Garnier Voicer Peter Black Director of Music, St Georges

title: The Sign
oneLiner: One man's investigation into what he believes are the real beginnings of Christianity - We look at the evidence
summary: Thomas de Wesselow is a respected and known art historian at King’s College Cambridge. Known for his ability to solve complex historical problems ultimately led him to investigate the Shroud of Turin. Reflecting on the mysterious image imprinted on this famous relic – generally dismissed as a medieval fake – he suddenly realized that it might have an historical significance that no one had ever suspected. It could explain the Birth of Christianity. This was in 2006 and since then Thomas has spent five years of painstaking study and is finally ready to publish. He believes he can prove beyond doubt that the Shroud is an authentic relic of Jesus, and crucially, that it inspired the belief in the Resurrection. His book will be release world wide at the end of March and in book circles it is believed it will be what ‘Keeper of Genesis’ was to Egyptology.
caseStudies: thomas De Wesselow Art Historian and Author

title: TAKEN FOR A RIDE
oneLiner: An investment con aritist who scammed the poor out of what little they had thought he had got away with it. That's until we tracked him down.
summary: Steve Cochrane, who owns Cochrane Trucking Company, convinced 600 poor and emerging busness owners to invest in his "empowerment donor scheme". He then disappeared with the cash.

title: TRUCKING TROUBLES
oneLiner: We expose Vone Transport, a company that has conned investors our of thousands of Rands, promising phenomenal returns, but delivering nothing but excuses.
summary: With the economic strain of the last couple of years, people are always up for a good investment. Unfortunately for investors, conartists are just as eager to make some money. The Coal Supply Scam is one of the latest cons doing the rounds. Carte Blanche goes undercover to expose Vone Transport, a company that collected deposits from investors, promising returns of up to R200 000 per month – but has delivered nothing but excuses.
caseStudies: VINCENT DE LA GEY TOKOZANE MAHLANGU BARRY AND RONELL
experts: Mr. COMPANY: VONE TRANSPORT - YVONNE LANDMAN Mrs. LILLIAN BEUKES SNITCH

title: SKA
oneLiner: WE did it, SA and Africa will host the biggest radio telescope in the world .
summary: On the 4th April 2012, South Africa will know whether or not we have won the bid to host the Square Kilometer Array. In the last meeting it was a close call between SA and Australia, but insiders are saying that the SA bid is looking stronger because we are doing more advanced scientific work on Kat 7, the precursor to Meerkat than our arch rival Australia is doing. There is also talk that they could divide the work between SA and Australia. It's been 10 years since the bid process began and local Astronomers are extremely excited. The first Carte Blanche story on SKA won the overall prize in the Siemens Pan African Profile Awards and this insert would be an update and look at the benefits of this project to South Africa. The insert will look at the extensive academic, scientific, and technical developments and inputs to Africa.
caseStudies: Bernie Fanaroff
experts: Dr. Naledi Pandor Ms. Natasha Maddox Dr. Adriaan Tiplady

title: Wedding Woes
oneLiner: A couple from Pretoria who specialise in weddings doing dresses and venues have left many couples with dreams dashed and deposits lost.
summary: Every little girl dreams of her magical wedding day and tying the knot with the man of her dreams! I have found a Pretoria couple that turns wedding dreams into nightmares for a living! AJ & Susann Smith own and run The Wedding Label Boutique and Rhuslancea Wedding Venue. Both these companies have ruined wedding days for at least 15 young couples in love. Wedding dresses arrive in complete if at all and the wedding venue closed its doors a month ago – disappearing with deposits worth R200 000 just weeks before some of the wedding dates. Carte Blanche tracks down this wedding wrecking couple.
caseStudies: Quewen Webb GROUP OF UPSET COUPLES Annrie Nel
experts: Ms. Kirstin Kleinsmidt Miss. Susann Myburgh Mr. AJ Smith

title: Ben Freeth
oneLiner: We meet a man who lives in hope in Harare - despite delivering the biggest insult yet to zimbabwe's Pres Mugabe
summary: Ben Freeth was chased off his farm at night and tortured along with his parents-in-law, in thick miombo woodland with no moon. He didnt buckle and leave, but rather took Pres Mugabe to the SADC human rights tribunal - and won. His story has been told in an international documentary and in a book he's written. Mugabe at one stage has declared him Zimbabwe's 'white enemy #1' - yet he has chosen to stay in Zim, living in Harare - unlike the other authors like Godwin and Fuller who've writen about their early years in the country. Taking his experience further, he has also taken the SADC leaders to court for ignoring the findings of their own tribunal - a case to be heard in April. His is a display of massive courage, just like his story. We will itv him at home in Harare or at his destroyed, empty farm. Our story - his tale - will be supported by compelling visuals shot during the take-over of his farm.
caseStudies: Ben Freeth Freeth Former farm-owner Laura Freeth Joshua Freeth Angela Campbell Peter Asani Gift Konjani

title: House hi-jacking
oneLiner: It is not only cars that get hi-jacked. Your house could be hi-jacked as well.
summary: I have been contacted by people in Van der Bijl Park who have properties/houses that have been hi-jacked by a syndicate operating in the area. If they see people moving out, or if a property is standing empty or being sold, they simply break in, change the locks, move in and rent it out to students/friends. If the owners call the police the syndicate dispute the ownership, saying they have legal claim to the property. The police cannot/does not want to get involved, saying it is a civil case. It means that the owners have to go to court to get the tenants out and it takes months or years. In the meantime the syndicate pockets rent. We have dozens of complaints and many willing interviewees. It seems to be a real problem in that area.
caseStudies: Frans and Bets Landman

title: Facebook Fiend
oneLiner: On Carte Blanche tonight we expose and arrest a Facebook stalker and paedophile.
summary: Carte Blanche was approached by a concerned father who spotted a potential paedophile on Facebook while checking out his 16 year old daughters Facebook. He has tracked him down and knows who he is, where he works and where he lives. As it stands according to the concerned father Des Van Der Merwe, the stalker is Chris Kruger who is 23 years old. Des created a fake facebook profile as a young 14 year old girl Dianka and engaged in conversations with Chris. They became very perverse and Chris sent pictures that were very provocative to Dianka. They engaged in conversations about sex and her virginity. Chris wants to meet Dianka. Chris has many other young girls on his Facebook page. At this stage we are unsure of how many of them have been approached of affected by him. Carte Blanche has approached Luke Lamprecht from the Johannesburg Child Advocacy Forum and the SAPS who are going to take over the case and help us stop and arrest this guy. We are hoping to have access to the arrest and some of the process. Des will tell his story, but his identity may have to remain hidden. Luke is also going to set up a debriefing session for all the girls who are on Chris' Facebook, in case they may require councelling. We are going to inform the public of the dangers of Facebook and the kind of monitoring they have to place on their children. I have also come across a South African who has created a whole lot of protection devices on the internet and for Facebook and has set up a web page to help parents learn how to protect their children against the perils of the electronic media. He has shows how to set up a panic button on your child's Blackberry should they require help. I think this could be a nice addition to the story, duration dependant. The police have asked for about a month to get the whole operation going, but they hope that things can be actioned sooner.
caseStudies: Des Van Der Merwe Father
experts: Mr. Luke Lamprecht JCAF Mr. Detective Warant Officer Karel Geldenhuys SAPS Mr. Detective Warrant Officer Tonja Louwrens SAPS

title: Off Limits Ballet
oneLiner: Carte Blanche gets an off limits opportunity to get behind the scenes of the Cape Town International Ballet competition as we experience the highs and lows the wins and the defeats in the world of bal
summary: The Cape Town International Ballet Competition has been running for four years now. Participants from all over the world are competing. We have the unique opportunity to film this event as well as get behind the scenes footage of the ballet dancers. Backstage, in their hotels, getting to see what they go through. Talking about their life styles as ballet dancers and what they have had to sacrifice to get to where they are. There are some star performers who have won international awards. We will get the opportunity to interview one-one with: A gold medalist Cuban male dancer, a Korean dancer an Armenian dancer, A South African dancer who is 14 years old and is set to be a superstar, as well as an American boy who was runner up in Beijing. We will get to see them preparing and dancing in the competition. We have also been offered all the handicam footage as well as HD footage that they have been shooting so far and we will get footage of the winners. We will also speak to two of the judges who are of international acclaim: The newly appointed director of the Royal Ballet of London Kevin O'Hare and Letisha Metler who was a prima ballerina in South Africa and then went on to international acclaim. She can talk on the state of ballet in South Africa and where it is heading and draw from her own experiences. The judges will also talk about what they are looking for in the dancers. We will also interview Dirk Badenhorst who is the brains behind this competition and his aspirations for ballet in the next couple of years as well as the aim of the competition.
caseStudies: Korean girl Korean Korean
experts: Mr. Cuban Dancer boy Cuban Cuban Miss. American boy American American Miss. South African girl South African South African Mr. Dirk Badenhorst Mr. Kevin O'Hare Mrs. Letisha Metler

title: STRESS
oneLiner: Are our jobs leading to burn out?
summary: The global financial crunch has led to an increase in workplace stress. In South Africa, over R3 billion a year is lost due to workplace stress, a recent study has shown. More and more employees are frustrated and resentful. In many companies, the recession has led to retrenchments, employees being shunted around, fewer perks, longer hours and in some cases, less pay. We ask why workplace stress is so high, what it's like to live on the edge of boiling stress and what companies are doing wrong.
caseStudies: MIKE CLARK to be supplied to be supplied
experts: Ms. VICKY ERIKSSON

title: BMW almost 600 days in storage (consumer shortie)
summary: Aziz Riaz bought a BMW 320i from Lyndhurst Motors in Sandton. It was a used car and had originally belonged to his sister, however he bought it through the dealership. The car has had problems with overheating since he bought it and has been taken back to various BMW dealerships to be fixed. He drove the car after it had apparently been fixed and it overheated damaging the engine. He took it back to the dealership and they promised to investigate. It took 586 days for BMW to conclude that the damage was due to conditions of use and not poor workmanship. He is now being held liable for over R50,000 of storage fees and the mechanic’s fees to investigate the problem as part of BMW’s investigation. Aziz says he only drove the car after he was told it had been fixed, however he suspects that the repairs were not carried out – his son was apparently at the dealership when the mechanics said there was no job card for that particular BMW. He has also taken his complaint to the Motor Industry Ombud who has yet to issue him with a case number for his case. He has also complained to BMW head office and BMW in Germany.
caseStudies: Aziz Riaz BMW owner

title: Maritzburg Mess- clean up or cover up?
oneLiner: Operation Pitbull was meant to clean up the Umsunduzi Municipality. But was it a cleanup or a cover up.
summary: In October 2010 Carte Blanche told the story of the mess in Maritzburg. Corruption and mismanagement had destroyed the city’s finances. The city was placed under administration and Johan Mettler from SALGA was brought in to clean things up. At the time Mettler believed it would take three years for the city to completely recover and he told Carte Blanche that he is going nowhere until he can see real change. We go back to see if he has stuck to his promises.
caseStudies: Johan Mettler

title: The Downfall of Juan Mayer
oneLiner: Juan Mayer shot into the limelight when he alleged that a business deal with Radovan Krejcir had gone bad and Radovan was trying to kill him. But his biggest enemy seems to be SARS, not crime boss Rad
summary: 18 months ago Juan Mayer would sit in a Rhapsody’s in Centurion and when it came time to pay he would peel notes off a wad of cash. Surrounded by his eight body guards Juan Mayer strutted his stuff as one of the underworld’s Mr Big. Now it seems he has come crashing down.
caseStudies: Juan Mayer
experts: Mr. Reichel Du Toit

title: The giant tyre cutter (consumer; 4 minute)
oneLiner: A new South African invention - the first of its kind in the world - that will help to rid the environment from its black carbon footprint.
summary: A South African company and invention can now assist in sweeping the carbon black footprint left especially by mines. It is the first such invention in the world. Giant tyres used by mining companies in large earthmovers are too big to recycle, mainly because it cannot be moved. This has caused that all these massive tyres were just dumped on dumping sites, causing mining companies not to be able to comply to the Waste Tyre regulations. South African company Tiputone invented a first of its kind in the world jumbo tyre cutter that can now cut these giant tyres in four pieces before it is moved to a plant where it is then recycled and used to make crude oil, a highly flammable liquid used widely in the steel industry as well as in dynamite to blow open cast mines for mining and heating processes in various industries. The giant cutter weighs 6000 kg, can cope with tyres up to 6 metres in diameter and costs R3,9 million and the first one is now used at Kumba Iron Ore's Sishen mine near Kathu in the Northern Cape. Tiputone MD, Cobus Botha, says the technology will help mines to clear waste from their sites and will also create jobs.
caseStudies: Cobus Botha MD Tiputone

title: Cameron's Camel Campaign
oneLiner: A Young South African boy sets out to save some camels
summary: Cameron Olivier, a 14 year old South African boy is determined to clean up the desert surrounding Abu Dhabi in the UAE to make it safe for the rapidly diminishing population camels who because of the gross amount of plastic litter are dying slow and painful deaths.
caseStudies: Cameron Olivier
experts: Mr. Vet

title: Midvaal Municipality
oneLiner: The Midvaal Municipality has already been slammed by the Pubic Protector for breaching financial and administrative policies. But there's no end to frustrated land owners who've had it.
summary: In November 2011 Public Protector Thuli Madonsela released a sctahing report on the Midvaal Municipality, saying it had breached financial and administrative policies. She found that the municipality, the only one run by the DA in Gauteng, violated the Preferential Procurement Policy Framework because over the past 30 years it had retained the same legal firm without going through proper procedures. The same legal firm, owned by Midvaal DA leader Andre Odendaal, also does debt collection and auctioneering in violation of the Local Government Transition Act. "The company's contract was deliberately and continuously extended which allowed it to gain an unfair advantage over other prospective service providers." After the Public Protector's report was released, DA MP and chairperson of the party's federal executive James Selfe said that the DA will be reviewing the rules that govern the actions of its public office-bearers. However, promises are still made by the Midvaal municiplaity that are not being honoured. We will tell the story through Pepe Marais, a Joburger who bought land about 30km from Meyerton in the jurisdiction of the Midvaal Municipality. He had written a letter to Helen Zille to state his frustration with the municipality and DA-mayor Timothy Nast, but she only referred him to the DA-leader in Meyerton, Andre Odendaal.

title: Seli 1 Update
oneLiner: SEli 1 has become SEli 3 and we still have not updated our maritme legislation in 33 years and continue to carry the cost of mop up operations from maritime disasters on our coastline
summary: In September 2009 the Seli 1 ran aground in massive seas onto Blouberg beach in Table bay, Cape Town. The Seli’ 1 owners and insurance company could never be held accountable for the salvage operation. The City of Cape Town contracted Smit Amandla to do the emergency salvage operation, removing fuel and the coal to avert the immediate pollution and over the last two years it has broken into 3 parts and is colloquially know as the SEli 3 SAMSA has spent over R40 million to clean the initial damage but it will take a further R30 million to complete the operation and the City of Cape Town is not in a position to continue to carry the costs. It has to be jointly carried by Transnet, SAMSA as well as the Department of Transport and Environmental Affairs, but neither of the latter two departments are coming to the party and an inter government dispute has now been formally tabled. When Carte Blanche originally covered the story we pointed out that SA has outdated maritime legislation that has not been updated for the last 33 years. Since the Seli 1 we have had several more ship wrecks each potentially posing a massive environmental disaster. If we updated the legislation we could claim for salvage and clean up operations from International Oil companies insurance funds which provides for exactly these circumstances. SA remains vulnerable to unscrupulous ship owners who abandon their ships and have no insurance coverage for clean-up operations. Maritime lawyers have been pressurizing the government since 1974 to change the legislation and still nothing has changed.
caseStudies: Jeremy Cronin
experts: Mr. Parick Hollaway

title: NGO's funding crisis
oneLiner: The Black Sash is having to close its doors after 50 years of providing a vital stop gap to the Grahamstown community in a town where government insitutions have failed
summary: Non Governmental Organisations or NGO’s are facing a massive funding crisis and have to downscale or close completely, no longer able to provide essential services that the state is failing to provide. Over the last couple of years it’s been harder and harder to raise funds from the international community as the global economic crisis has become more entrenched, but 2012 finally saw many NGOs hit rock bottom. Established NGOs like the Black Sash, IDASA, Molo Songolo, St Josephs Adult Education, all established during Apartheid and having successfully redefined their role post Apartheid are now facing closure having lost millions in funding. For example the Black Sash has a R24 million shortfall in funding this year and one casualty has been the closing of the Grahamstown office which has been open since the early 60’s. NGO’s play an important watch dog role of the state and create a voice for civil society. IDASA has lost its funding from R100 million annually to R50 million, as a result it had to close the Cape Town office which was its media and Political Information and Monitoring Services. They have had to retrench half their staff nationally, as has the Black Sash. The Treatment Action Campaign is also facing major funding crisis and smaller NGOs like CASE in Hanover Park that provide adult education, homework support, school councilors and have a massive impact in this embattled community, lurches from month to month dependent on the good will of volunteers. The irony is that there is plenty of money within South Africa raised via the Lotto but it’s impossible to access.The other major source of funds, big corporate companies CSI funding is inaccessible because they provide funding for projects, but not the office running costs. The insert will look at the impact of the global economic crisis on NGOs, and the vital role they play.
caseStudies: Black Sash, TAC, CASE, IDASA
experts: Mr. James Taylor

summary: Not everone can afford a Porsche and I am sure that when you decide to buy one or sell yours, you will do so at a reputable dealership that specializes in buying and selling Porsche. title: ESKOM Crisis 2
oneLiner: Why has construction cost a Medupi and Kusile gone up 200%
summary: South Africans first learnt about Medupi at Lepalale in Limpopo and Kusile near Ogies in Mpumalanga about 7 years ago. When completed Medupi will be the largest dry-cooled coal fired power station in the world with six boilers, each powering an 800 MW turbine, producing 4800 MW of electricity. Construction started in 2007 and the power station’s first unit was scheduled for service in 2012 with the last one due in 2015. But Medupi has had construction delays and will now only come online in 2013 at the earliest and experts doubt that this date will be honoured. The Kusile power station, the second coal-fired power station being built by Eskom, is scheduled for completion in 2017. The first generating unit was planned to go online by 2013, followed by an additional unit every eight months there after. Kusile is a base-load power station that will consist of six generating units with a capacity of approximately 4 800 megawatts.
caseStudies: Foreign workers Ted Blohm

title: Chapmans Peak Toll Plaza saga
oneLiner: Murray and Roberts plan to build the ultimat corporate office on iconic Chapman Peak drive
summary: Cape Town’s Chapmans Peak Drive, one of the most scenic drives in the world, is set to have a three storey office block and full toll plaza built on it and residents are up in arms. 2000 protestors delivered a memorandum to Transport MEC Robin Carlisle to protest the action and since then the spotlight has been focused on an allegedly corrupt contract. Carlisle says he has dramatically renegotiated and improved the contract with Entilini, whose major shareholder is Murray and Roberts but that he cannot prevent the building from going ahead as he is contractually bound to deliver on it. Local residents’ associations and Civil Rights Groups say they agree that the City needs to toll the road in order to regain some of the money spent making it safe, but does it require a R53 million building? The plans for the building and toll are 10 years old, designed when the original contract was entered into, and since then technology has advanced dramatically and a simple boom, electronically operated with multiple paying options needs to be considered. This boom can be operated from Johannesburg or Cape Town central and nothing more than a simple boom gate would be necessary on the world heritage site. Residents and their legal advisors say Carlisle could cancel the contract because the EIA is flawed and the building is illegal because it is on Table Mountain National Park land, which requires Parliament to cede the land. To date this application has not been made. But legal wrangling aside, many of the objectors say that the real issue here is the alienation of National Parks land – land that is owned by the people of South Africa – to a private company. And on top of that, they say, is the fact that Murray and Roberts will in effect have gained a venue for corporate functions with one of the best views in the world – the dramatic vista of Chapmans Peak and Hout Bay across to the Sentinel.

title: Eastgate Mall
oneLiner: Hundreds of millions of Rands have been spent to refurbish the Eastgate Mall but at what cost to the tenants?
summary: Brothers Alexi and Phillip Karafilakis opened Café Bacini’s doors to the public on the 26 September 2006. The store was purposely built as a flagship store for the launch of a new franchise concept. The landlord was very well aware this. Over 3 Million Rand was invested in the opening of the store, however at no stage did the landlord indicate it’s intention to embark on a R750 Million extension to the centre in the very near future. The information was purposefully withheld as the landlord must have know about this. Since the construction started 4 years ago many shops had to close down due to a lack of business. Delays kept many shops in a state of limbo for the last three years and nine months. Alexi has a complete paper trail including minutes of meetings, email correspondence, contracts, video, photo’s and audio recordings of the events. Another tenant has video of the dangerous circumstances in which they had to trade. Many waiters and shop attendants have lost their jobs and one shop that closed down had been there for 16 years. The owner is almost 60. Alexi moved to Australia because he too has lost millions. His brother Phillip was a partner and he knows the story. The delays are allegedly as a direct result of the bully tactics and incompetence of the landlord, Liberty Group Properties (Limited) a public company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
caseStudies: Phillip and Alexi Karafilakis Business men Paris Kaptanis Liberty Property

summary: The ultimate dream for any sports fan is to see your team in action, live on the field. SA Sports Package is a local one-stop-shop travel agency specialising in sporting event holidays – selling the dream to sports fans around the country. But this February, a group of English Premier League fans signed up for trip to the UK to see a match at Old Trafford, got a nightmare deal instead. R20 000 later - NO accommodation was booked! title: Supermarket Super Bugs
oneLiner: Tonight on Carte Blanche we trace a new superbug, found on our food, as it spreads across the globe.
summary: Antibiotics were once the wonder drug. Now an increasing number of highly resistant -- and deadly -- bacteria are spreading around the world. These dangerous pathogens are no longer only the feared "hospital bugs". Instead, they have become ever-present. NB: We will pay for a presenter to go to Germany and Holland. If CB can cover costs of Accommodation/ S&T and visas. I also have an additional interview for another story we can pick up will in Germany. And research points to a new breeding ground for a more virulent form of the previously dreaded hospital acquired-MRSA bug: animal factory farms. Here animals are treated with human antibiotics whether they are sick or not. The result is that they build up a resistance – creating new superbugs which are deadly to humans. It’s growing on our food and can be found on products sold in our supermarkets - from meat to the vegetables. The World Health Organization (WHO) recently warned against an impending medical catastrophe. In response, governments and public agencies across Europe and the USA are attempting to put the brakes on the use of human antibiotics on animals.
caseStudies: still to be sourced in SA and Germany
experts: Mr. 5.Steven Roach

title: Terence Reis
oneLiner: 50 year old fan becomes rock star "overnight"
summary: At 16 (in the 1970s), Terence Reis was more than a fan of Dire Straits. He bought a guitar just like the lead singer/guitarist, Mark Knopfler had. He researched the amps and pedals used to create the unique sound. And he played and sang along with the records, to get those electric solos note-perfect. 20 years later, when Dire Straits were asked to do a reunion concert, Mark Knopfler was not available, so the rest of the band members and their management searched for a replacement - and found an ancient Youtube clip of Terence playing "Sultans of Swing". A few weeks later he was fronting the band simply called "The Straits" at the Royal Albert Hall.

title: Defending Dugongs - Karen Allen's Mermaids
oneLiner: Are we too late to protect the Mermaids of the sea? This conservationist is gung-ho in defending the dugongs but are Bazaruto's manatees soon to become a myth?
summary: There are only an estimated 250 dugongs off Africa's east coast. They could all vanish in as little as 40 years according to the Convention on Migratory Species of Wild Animals. Unless Mozambique's last viable population is given adequate protection through law enforcement, they have no chance of survival. But their last hope is EWT's Karen Allen - who's on the front line against the assault by longliners, seine and gill net fishing with military precision she is orchestrating a front line of defence by means of aircraft and boats who will be deployed to defend the dugongs. If they are unable to consume the preferred quantity and quality of sea-grass their staple food not only will the starve to death but won't breed and to date 60% of the ocean's sea-grass has destroyed- by means of dredging, coastal pollution and sedimentation from over silted river loads. The IUCN recently placed importance of sea-grass as a significant carbon sink. So far Karen's efforts to save Bazaruto's mermaids is gaining ground. We jump on board with her and go in search of the last dugongs who's continued existence depends on this 27 year old, who's exchanged her predictable city life to draw the battle line in Mozambique's most popular island We aim to create not only a visually spectacular piece incorporating underwater footage and air visuals but a high octane reality style insert as we film Karen, conducting a full throttle defense in order to save the last manatees of the Indian Ocean.

title: A COJ Crisis - A CB March
oneLiner: On Carte Blanche tonight… We take to the streets with thousands of irate Johannesburg residents and march on the mayor’s office in a bid for action following a decade long billing crisis
summary: For over a decade the City of Johannesburg's billing department has been in crises and the nightmare continues despite the City’s ‘road map’. Illegal cut offs, non-payment of deposits over several years (which is essentially theft) and blatant dis-regard for the concerns of consumers. The City is seems is untouchable ... The so-called ‘crisis’ has been covered in the media countless times and CB has done several investigations over the years. Still the complaints mount … In a massive departure from the norm, Carte Blanche galvanizes its viewers and leads a protest march to the Mayor Parks Tau’s office. The City currently has over 100 000 outstanding queries on it’s system - 56 000 of those are billing related. If we managed to get even a fraction of those complainants to a Carte Blanche protest march, it would make for impressive television (and create news of its own) It’s time to turn the tide ….

title: The Burzynski Clinic and a Cure for Cancer
oneLiner: The story of the Burzynski clinic with a revolutionary and successful treatment for cancer and the efforts of the US Government and big pharma to shut it down.
summary: Dr Stanislaw Burzynski is a Polish doctor/biochemist in the USA who developed a non-toxic cure for cancer in the late 1970’s. He has devised a kind of epigenetic treatment decades before current efforts. His success rate is far greater than that of chemotherapy/radiation and there are no side effects (besides possible dehydration because of the high level of sodium in the treatment). Instead of embracing this cure, it seems the FDA and big pharma have bee trying to close him down and jail him. Burzynski believes it is because the huge profits of the pharmaceutical companies who produce the chemotherapy and radiation treatments will be wiped out if his treatment is accepted generally. A recent film also supports this theory.
caseStudies: Asaad Wilson head Clinical Trials

title: Sports Package Scam
oneLiner: 170 people scammed out of thousands for sports tours that never materialised.
summary: My son and I were due to leave for the UK on 09/02/12 to watch the Man Untied v Liverpool match on 11/02/2012. However, on the day we were about to leave for the airport (as we were putting our bags into the car) we received a call from the agent at SA Sports Package advising us that we in fact had no match tickets! We had made full payment for the package in the amount of R27 990-00. This package included the cost of the match tickets, the accomodation in the UK, transfers and return flights on Emirates. Prior to us leaving for our flights my son had called SA Sport Packages on numerous occasions to confirm when we would be receiving the match tickets and so forth. The phone (both mobile and land line) just kept ringing. My son sent numerous e-mails and whilst we waited for their response we had already obtained our UK visa (for which we had to pay approximately R1000 each) and booked tickets for the Stadium/Museum tour at Old Trafford.

title: Egg Mule
oneLiner: We speak to the South African man who the British press dubbed as one of the biggest wildlife smugglers in decades.
summary: Jeff Lendrum is a Zimbabwean born South African bird enthusiast who last year was caught with 14 peregrine falcon eggs stapped to his body at Heathrow. He was immediately jailed and his story featured on CNN Sky and the BBC. The press dubbed him the biggest wildlife smuggler in decades and showed dramatic footage of him clad in black swinging from a helicopter at cliff faces where rare raptor nests were situated. The footage came from his own hard drive. As a bird preservationist he has spent his life studying and researching rare raptors. And this is why he says he felt the urge to save these birds. This is how he relates the story: He was on holiday in Wales and he heard that some of the locals who are keen on racing pigeons were fed up with the peregrine falcons in the area who were killing their birds during training flights. Since top class pigeons can cost a pretty penny they were determined to decimate the nests of the falcons to prevent them breeding. That's where Jeff stepped in. He located the nests, removed the eggs and decided to come back to SA with them. So he came up with a plan to smuggle the eggs back in socks. He went through customs at Heathrow with them in a box and once near the departure gate he went to the bathrooms where he removed the eggs from the egg boxes and placed them in socks before strapping them to his body to keep them warm and help incubate them. Before leaving the bathroom he threw the egg boxes into the bin which is where they were found by a cleaner who alerted security to his odd behaviour. He was stopped and searched and thrown into jail. Which is where he remained in high security for 4 months along with some dangerous criminals. He shared a cell with a man who had murdered his wife by bludgeoning her to death and then wrapped her in cling film. Yet Jeff was seen as the celebrity criminal because his story dominated the news far more!
caseStudies: Jeff Lendrum Preservationist
experts: Mr. John Ledger Conservationist

title: The Frozen Ark
oneLiner: A new Ark has been constructed in England and the animals are being herded in one by one.
summary: The Frozen Ark is a project aiming at saving the DNA and the viable cells of the world's endangered animals. It is necessary because species go extinct at an alarming rate: • In early November 2011 the World Wildlife Fund declared the Vietnam Javan Rhinoceros (Rhinoceros sondaicus annamiticus) extinct. • On 15 November 2011 the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) declared the Western Black Rhino (Diceros bicornis longipes) of Africa extinct. Luckily the DNA of these two species has not been lost. It is safe in cryopreservation in the Frozen Ark in Nottingham in the UK.

title: Taxi Hunts - Betting on illegal dog hunts
oneLiner: They are called taxi hunts - it's catered for the well heeled - winning dogs can earn tens of thousands of rand in a single hunt and it's threatening endangered wildlife. Carte Blanche goes undercove
summary: There are reports of up to 40 people being involved in a single taxi hunt. Successful dogs can fetch anything between R10k and R24k. Hunts take place with 30 dogs or more. It's called taxi hunts because most people involved are taxi owners. While illegal hunting with dogs is driven by the need for food - taxi hunts is a form of sport or gambling. And while it's increasing in popularity, wildlife especially rare antelope are being pushed to red alert status. We delve into the underworld of taxi hunts and confront the top players one being the former head of SAPS stock theft unit who is apparently still involved in this illegal activity.

title: Japan Economy
oneLiner: Japan has an amazing ability to rise from the ashes - is there confidence they can rise from all that seems to be going wrong?
summary: Japan affects our everyday lives. From the car we drive to the tv we watch to the cellphone we use to the appliances in our homes. Japan has always been present as far as our collective memories goes over half a century back. It’s an amazing country that has always had the ability to bounce back to recover from whatever challenges it faces. Whether it is World War 2 or a tsunami. Most of these disasters would have crippled a nation, but in a way it seems events like these only strengthen a nation like Japan. Economically, Japan is at a cross roads. It’s economy has been in stagflation for over a decade. It’s dropped to third place on the world ranking of world’s largest economies. Yet, we still use Japanese products and we are influenced by this great culture.

title: FNB
oneLiner: Ever had the feeling that your bank has a vendetta against you and there is nobody and no place where you can find protection? Then don’t miss Carte Blanche on Sunday.
summary: A Jo’burg resident and owner of several properties in the city learned the hard way that the motto for his bank, “How can we help you?”, does not hold any promise of fairness and honesty. All his properties were bonded to FNB. Instead, Nico Niemand says FNB registered 8 sales in execution between 2004 and 2010, which were unfair and proper procedures were not followed.

title: Lying Lawyers
oneLiner: If the NPLS (Northern Province Law Society) was diligent in its efforts, unscrupulous lawyers would be stopped in their tracks; the Fidelity Fund would not be at risk
summary: Christo Uys is a practising lawyer in Vanderbijl Park. The only problem is, he shouldn’t be practising at all, according to the Northern Province Law Society (NPLS). Not only is he is still practising, but he has defrauded numerous people in the Vanderbijil Park area, liquidating pensions, doing fraudulent bridging finances to name a few. Christo seems to be a law unto himself. (016 933 0081) Three years ago, Lynn Kennedy required that Christo Uys account for R600 000 that was paid into the Trust Account of Rooth and Wessels Vanderbijlpark (RWV), which was owing to her. She decided to take him on, and has been attempting to bring the arm of the law known as the NPLS to stop Christo Uys and his associates from practising further.

title: Project Dreamwings
oneLiner: Tonight on Carte Blanche … They had a brief encounter over Angola during the Bush War in 1987 but now Arthur Piercy wants to fly to Cuba to meet the pilot who shot him down and left him a quadripleg
summary: Former SADF fighter pilot who’s confined to a wheelchair is building an aircraft to fly around the world and meet the Cuban pilot who shot him down over Angola in 1987.

title: Horse Slaughter
oneLiner: On Carte Blanche tonight – horse meat being sold in a local butchery as beef – we trace it’s cruel beginnings.
summary: For many years now rumours have circulated about an illegal horse slaughterhouse in the veld near Brakpan. On many occasions the Highveld Horse Care Unit has gone out to try and see if they can track the perpetrators down – on one of these occasions we went with them and the only evidence we could find was slaughter equipment. Following up on a lead Inspector Bobbie from the HHCU managed to get a court order last week to raid a property in Brakpan where she found 4 donkeys and a pony slaughtered. Unfortunately Carte Blanche could not gain access due to the magistrate crossing us off the court order. Bobbie did however manage to film some material although it is shaky. The horses are slaughtered in the veld and have their throats slit after they have been immobilized by cutting a vertebrae in their backs.

title: Crowdfunding for conservation
oneLiner: On Carte Blanche tonight we take a look at a unique approach to conservation – donors from around the world have rallied to prevent oil companies from destroying a pristine corner of the Amazon rain
summary: An innovative approach to conservation has prevented oil exploration in what is considered to be the most biologically diverse forest in the world.

title: Royal Bafokeng
oneLiner: How the Royal Bafokeng are building their nation the Singaporean way.
summary: With the controversy raging re what is spent and not spent, on education, teachers and their bonus’s and educational facilities …..a couple of hours from Johannesburg the Lebone II College, stands like a sanctuary on a hill overlooking Phokeng, the dusty but well- organised capital city in North West Province. This college is the Royal Bafokeng Nation’s newest community project and it’s construction cost a cool R 554m. Nothing was spared in the college’s construction, which is built on 80ha and designed like a contemporary village with educational, social and boarding facilities. King of the Royal Bafoking Nation, Kgosi Leruo Molotlegi, met with resistance from community members for spending so much, takes the criticism in his stride. “In that rural environment, there was no tangible model to showcase excellence. I wanted to introduce that. Now I want to use that energy to drive excellence at the community’s other schools.” But this is only a small, although important, part in how the Royal Bafoking are building their success, Called Vision 2020 - it was inspired by Singapore’s transformation from a slum city to a world class productive city in under 40 years, and is the nation’s plan to diversify its economy away from its dependence on mining and embark on infrastructure development.

title: Green City Success
oneLiner: Carte Blanche explores this little German village of big dreams and great green success.
summary: Going Green has a become an idealist goal for many! We all know we should, we all want to, but can it really be done on a large scale? YES! The small 2600 population of the agricultural German village of Wildpoldsried is showing the world that green living is an achievable goal and a profitable one too. The town generates 321 % more renewable energy than it utilises and makes around $5.7 million in additional revenue annually by selling the surplus energy to government. Today, Wildpoldsried has become a model of how to achieve community sustainability in the 21st century — and stay out of the RED. Carte Blanche explores this German village where big dreams and great green success are a way of living.

title: Illegal Cigarretes
oneLiner: To showcase how big a problem illicit Cigarettes are in South Africa.
summary: The story focuses on the lucrative illicit cigarettes trade in South Africa. About 80% of the lucrative Cigarette illicit trade in South Africa comes from Zimbabwe. Illicit cigarettes are transported via a mule network that carries the packs on their backs and cross the border to sell them South Africa. While this is only part of a bigger crime network, the story follows the Illicit cigarette trail from Musina to Johannesburg and Pretoria, that form 60% of the offloading market for these cigarettes.

title: Ghosts
oneLiner: A journey through some of the Cape’s most captivating ghost stories.
summary: We take a journey through the Cape’s present and past, looking at the ghosts that have haunted political figures and mansions, historical places and forested areas in and around Cape Town….from the Castle to Leeuwenhof, and Newlands House to the trees beneath Kloof Nek Drive….from Helen Zille to Pik Botha.

title: Storm Approaching
oneLiner: Tonight on Carte Blanche…. Proposed amendments to law prohibit warnings of severe weather and pollution without sanction – effectively gagging independent weather services and environmentalists wh
summary: Draconian amendments to the SA Weather Service bill threaten independent forecasters with fines and imprisonment for issuing severe weather warnings "They are an attempt... to establish and protect an unfair monopoly on services offered by the Weather Service, some of which are commercial services "The bill, if passed in its current form, will have various undesirable consequences, and will make South Africans less safe,"

title: Forced Adoptions
summary: The South African grandparents of 2 little boys living in the UK claim that their grandchildren have been torn from loving parent for no good reason; taken by the State and put up for adoption. It sounds an unbelievable story, but ‘forced adoptions’ at the hands of British Authorities – particularly of foreigner’s children is seemingly a growing phenomenon. According to a journalist for the UK Telegraph… “The horrors of 'child protection' as it is often practiced now - particularly on foreign children - would be a theme for a latter-day Dickens.

title: Cape Argus Cycle Tour
oneLiner: On Carte Blanche tonight – we go behind the scenes of one of the biggest timed cycle tours in the world, and one of the largest sporting events in South Africa - the Cape Argus Cycle Tour.
summary: Good luck if yr trying to get accommodation in Cape Town around the Argus Cycle Tour – all flights are booked and all rooms are taken. The Cape Argus has been ridden for 35 yrs. It’s the largest timed cycling race in the world – with 35 000 entries. It gets more international entries than the London marathon. But it’s not just a race – as with the London Marathon raising about 25 million GBP p/year, a huge element of the Argus is about charity. But that’s just one element – we explore the massive machine that the Cape Argus has become.

title: Silicon Beach
summary: A little company in Durban, staffed by youngsters of all races and genders, with a sweeping view of the beach - is in the front row of the most revolutionary show currently on the digital world stage. This is ‘Silicon Beach’. An example of ‘brain-ready’ rather than ‘shovel-ready’ job-creation. It centres around Apps – Applications – which have changed the way business is being done - and life is lived - today. From schoolbooks to maps, sport, games, media, calculators and even reproductions of scratchy vinyl record sounds…as the Apple advert says, ‘there’s an App for that’. Why else is it possible for my 2 and a half yr-old and his grandad to play with iPad / tablet? We look at this company – Immedia - that produces Apps for Supersport, DStv, Moneyweb, Computicket and a few overseas clients – as a perfect example of how South Africa can be competitive on the world stage, by creating locally relevant jobs – in a world where growth apparently doesn’t exist.
